On-disk run-segment format and its sequential writer/reader.\n//!\n//! # Disk format\n//!\n//! A run is one *committed* (renamed + fsynced) file:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! magic   : 8 bytes = b\"EXTSORT\\x02\"\n//! frames  : zero or more record frames\n//! trailer : frame type byte = FRAME_TRAILER, then u64 LE record count\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Every frame begins with a 1-byte discriminator so a pure sequential reader\n//! can tell records from the trailer:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! FRAME_CHUNK   = 0x10\n//! FRAME_TRAILER = 0x20\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Chunk frame layout:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! ftype   : u8        FRAME_CHUNK\n//! flags   : u8        bit0 = FIRST chunk of a record\n//!                     bit1 = CONT  — another chunk follows this one\n//!                     single-chunk record: FIRST, no CONT\n//!                     final chunk of multi-chunk record: neither bit set\n//! length  : u32 LE    payload length (<= CHUNK_MAX)\n//! crc32   : u32 LE    CRC-32/IEEE of the payload\n//! payload : `length` bytes\n//! ```\n//!\n//! The FIRST chunk payload is:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! u64 LE   seq        original input sequence number (stability tie-break)\n//! u8       nl         1 if the record ended with '\\n' in the input\n//! u32 LE   key_count  number of key components\n//! per key: u32 LE len + len key bytes\n//! bytes    value prefix (record bytes excluding the trailing '\\n')\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Later chunks hold only continuation value bytes. This lets a record of\n//! unbounded length be spilled with bounded memory: a giant line streams\n//! chunk-by-chunk while its (bounded) key stays in the head.\n//!\n//! Integrity: each chunk carries a payload CRC verified as bytes are consumed;\n//! the trailer repeats the record count, detecting torn tails; magic detects a\n//! wrong/truncated file.\n\nuse std::io;\n\nuse crate::crc::Crc;\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::io::VFile;\n\n/// Magic prefix of every run file.\npub const MAGIC: &[u8; 8] = b\"EXTSORT\\x02\";\n\nconst FRAME_CHUNK: u8 = 0x10;\nconst FRAME_TRAILER: u8 = 0x20;\n\nconst FLAG_FIRST: u8 = 0x01;\nconst FLAG_CONT: u8 = 0x02;\n\n/// Maximum payload bytes in one chunk.\npub const CHUNK_MAX: usize = 16 * 1024;\n/// Value bytes targeted for a giant record's FIRST chunk.\npub const GIANT_HEAD_VALUE: usize = 8 * 1024;\n\nconst CHUNK_HDR_LEN: usize = 1 + 1 + 4 + 4; // ftype, flags, len, crc\n\n/// Result of pulling bytes from a giant record's input source.\npub struct Pull {\n    /// Bytes made available.\n    pub bytes: usize,\n    /// True iff these bytes end the record (the trailing newline is consumed\n    /// by the drain and not included).\n    pub end_of_record: bool,\n    /// Whether the input record terminated with a newline.\n    pub nl: bool,\n}\n\n/// Source streamed by [`RunWriter::write_giant`] for an over-large record.\npub trait GiantDrain {\n    /// Fill the beginning of `buf` with up to `buf.len()` record bytes.\n    fn pull(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<Pull>;\n}\n\n/// Sequential run writer. Dropping without [`RunWriter::commit`] leaves a\n/// `*.tmp` file that recovery ignores.\npub struct RunWriter {\n    file: Box<dyn VFile>,\n    tmp_path: String,\n    final_path: String,\n    records: u64,\n}\n\nimpl RunWriter {\n    pub fn create(vfs: &dyn crate::io::Vfs, dir: &str, name: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n        let tmp_path = format!(\"{dir}/{name}.run.tmp\");\n        let final_path = format!(\"{dir}/{name}.run\");\n        let mut file = vfs.create(&tmp_path)?;\n        file.write_all(MAGIC)?;\n        Ok(RunWriter {\n            file,\n            tmp_path,\n            final_path,\n            records: 0,\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn record_count(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.records\n    }\n    pub fn tmp_path(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.tmp_path\n    }\n    pub fn final_path(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.final_path\n    }\n\n    fn key_overhead(keys: &[Vec<u8>]) -> usize {\n        8 + 1 + 4 + keys.iter().map(|k| 4 + k.len()).sum::<usize>()\n    }\n\n    fn encode_head(seq: u64, nl: bool, keys: &[Vec<u8>], prefix: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {\n        let mut p = Vec::with_capacity(Self::key_overhead(keys) + prefix.len());\n        p.extend_from_slice(&seq.to_le_bytes());\n        p.push(if nl { 1 } else { 0 });\n        p.extend_from_slice(&(keys.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n        for k in keys {\n            p.extend_from_slice(&(k.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n            p.extend_from_slice(k);\n        }\n        p.extend_from_slice(prefix);\n        p\n    }\n\n    fn write_chunk(&mut self, flags: u8, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {\n        debug_assert!(payload.len() <= CHUNK_MAX);\n        let mut crc = Crc::new();\n        crc.write(payload);\n        let mut hdr = [0u8; CHUNK_HDR_LEN];\n        hdr[0] = FRAME_CHUNK;\n        hdr[1] = flags;\n        hdr[2..6].copy_from_slice(&(payload.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n        hdr[6..10].copy_from_slice(&crc.finish().to_le_bytes());\n        self.file.write_all(&hdr)?;\n        self.file.write_all(payload)\n    }\n\n    /// Write one fully-resident record.\n    pub fn write_record(&mut self, seq: u64, nl: bool, keys: &[Vec<u8>], value: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {\n        let overhead = Self::key_overhead(keys);\n        if overhead + value.len() <= CHUNK_MAX {\n            let payload = Self::encode_head(seq, nl, keys, value);\n            self.write_chunk(FLAG_FIRST, &payload)?;\n        } else {\n            // Fully buffered but too big for one chunk: stream from a slice.\n            let head_value = (CHUNK_MAX - overhead).min(value.len());\n            let payload = Self::encode_head(seq, nl, keys, &value[..head_value]);\n            self.write_chunk(FLAG_FIRST | FLAG_CONT, &payload)?;\n            let mut pos = head_value;\n            while pos < value.len() {\n                let n = CHUNK_MAX.min(value.len() - pos);\n                let end = pos + n == value.len();\n                self.write_chunk(if end { 0 } else { FLAG_CONT }, &value[pos..pos + n])?;\n                pos += n;\n            }\n        }\n        self.records += 1;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Stream a giant record. `prefix` is the buffered head value; the rest is\n    /// pulled from `drain`.\n    pub fn write_giant(\n        &mut self,\n        seq: u64,\n        nl: bool,\n        keys: &[Vec<u8>],\n        prefix: &[u8],\n        drain: &mut dyn GiantDrain,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        let overhead = Self::key_overhead(keys);\n        // Assemble first payload: head + up to (CHUNK_MAX-overhead) value bytes.\n        let mut first = Self::encode_head(seq, nl, keys, prefix);\n        let mut buf = vec![0u8; CHUNK_MAX];\n        let mut ended = false;\n        while first.len() < CHUNK_MAX {\n            let want = CHUNK_MAX - first.len();\n            let pull = drain.pull(&mut buf[..want])?;\n            if pull.bytes > 0 {\n                first.extend_from_slice(&buf[..pull.bytes]);\n            }\n            if pull.end_of_record {\n                ended = true;\n                break;\n            }\n            if pull.bytes == 0 {\n                return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                    &self.tmp_path,\n                    \"giant drain returned no progress and no end\",\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n        if !ended {\n            self.write_chunk(FLAG_FIRST | FLAG_CONT, &first)?;\n        } else {\n            self.write_chunk(FLAG_FIRST, &first)?;\n        }\n        while !ended {\n            let mut filled = 0;\n            let mut nl_flag = nl;\n            while filled < CHUNK_MAX {\n                let pull = drain.pull(&mut buf[filled..])?;\n                filled += pull.bytes;\n                nl_flag = pull.nl;\n                if pull.end_of_record {\n                    ended = true;\n                    break;\n                }\n                if pull.bytes == 0 {\n                    return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                        &self.tmp_path,\n                        \"giant drain stalled mid-record\",\n                    ));\n                }\n            }\n            let _ = nl_flag;\n            self.write_chunk(if ended { 0 } else { FLAG_CONT }, &buf[..filled])?;\n        }\n        self.records += 1;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Write trailer, fsync, close, atomically rename to the committed name.\n    pub fn commit(mut self, vfs: &dyn crate::io::Vfs) -> Result<(String, u64)> {\n        let mut tr = [0u8; 9];\n        tr[0] = FRAME_TRAILER;\n        tr[1..9].copy_from_slice(&self.records.to_le_bytes());\n        self.file.write_all(&tr)?;\n        self.file.flush()?;\n        self.file.sync_all()?;\n        drop(self.file);\n        vfs.rename(&self.tmp_path, &self.final_path)?;\n        Ok((self.final_path, self.records))\n    }\n}\n\n/// Decoded head of one run record.\npub struct RecordHead {\n    pub seq: u64,\n    pub nl: bool,\n    pub keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n    /// Value bytes carried in the FIRST chunk (whole value for small records).\n    pub prefix: Vec<u8>,\n    /// CONT flag of the first chunk: true when value continues.\n    pub has_more: bool,\n}\n\n/// Reader position.\n#[derive(PartialEq, Eq)]\nenum Pos {\n    /// Magic verified, nothing read yet.\n    Start,\n    /// Last thing consumed was a chunk with CONT clear; next is frame type.\n    RecordBoundary,\n    /// Inside a record, `remaining` bytes of current chunk left.\n    InChunk,\n    /// Trailer frame read; nothing follows.\n    Trailer,\n}\n\n/// Sequential run reader verifying per-chunk CRCs.\npub struct RunReader {\n    file: Box<dyn VFile>,\n    path: String,\n    pos: Pos,\n    flags: u8,\n    remaining: u32,\n    crc: Crc,\n    expected_crc: u32,\n    records_seen: u64,\n}\n\nimpl RunReader {\n    pub fn open(vfs: &dyn crate::io::Vfs, path: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n        let mut file = vfs.open(path)?;\n        let mut magic = [0u8; 8];\n        read_exact(&mut file, &mut magic, path)?;\n        if &magic != MAGIC {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(path, \"bad magic header\"));\n        }\n        Ok(RunReader {\n            file,\n            path: path.to_string(),\n            pos: Pos::Start,\n            flags: 0,\n            remaining: 0,\n            crc: Crc::new(),\n            expected_crc: 0,\n            records_seen: 0,\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn path(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.path\n    }\n\n    fn read_u8(&mut self) -> Result<Option<u8>> {\n        let mut b = [0u8; 1];\n        match read_exact_opt(&mut self.file, &mut b) {\n            Ok(()) => Ok(Some(b[0])),\n            Err(Error::Io(e, _)) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof => Ok(None),\n            Err(e) => Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Read the next chunk header (called at a frame boundary). Returns false\n    /// if the trailer is found instead.\n    fn enter_frame(&mut self) -> Result<bool> {\n        let ftype = self\n            .read_u8()?\n            .ok_or_else(|| Error::corrupt(&self.path, \"EOF where frame expected\"))?;\n        if ftype == FRAME_TRAILER {\n            self.pos = Pos::Trailer;\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n        if ftype != FRAME_CHUNK {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                &self.path,\n                format!(\"invalid frame type byte 0x{ftype:02x}\"),\n            ));\n        }\n        let mut rest = [0u8; CHUNK_HDR_LEN - 1];\n        read_exact(&mut self.file, &mut rest, &self.path)?;\n        self.flags = rest[0];\n        self.remaining = u32::from_le_bytes([rest[1], rest[2], rest[3], rest[4]]);\n        self.expected_crc = u32::from_le_bytes([rest[5], rest[6], rest[7], rest[8]]);\n        if self.remaining as usize > CHUNK_MAX {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                &self.path,\n                format!(\"chunk length {} exceeds frame max\", self.remaining),\n            ));\n        }\n        self.crc = Crc::new();\n        self.pos = Pos::InChunk;\n        Ok(true)\n    }\n\n    /// Discard the rest of the current chunk and verify its CRC.\n    fn discard_chunk_body(&mut self) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut buf = [0u8; 8192];\n        while self.remaining > 0 {\n            let want = buf.len().min(self.remaining as usize);\n            let n = self.file.read(&mut buf[..want])?;\n            if n == 0 {\n                return Err(Error::corrupt(&self.path, \"chunk payload truncated\"));\n            }\n            self.crc.write(&buf[..n]);\n            self.remaining -= n as u32;\n        }\n        self.check_crc()\n    }\n\n    fn check_crc(&mut self) -> Result<()> {\n        if self.crc.finish() != self.expected_crc {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                &self.path,\n                \"chunk CRC mismatch — segment corrupted\",\n            ));\n        }\n        if self.flags & FLAG_CONT == 0 {\n            self.pos = Pos::RecordBoundary;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Skip every remaining chunk of the current record.\n    pub fn drain_record(&mut self) -> Result<()> {\n        // Current (possibly partly consumed) chunk.\n        if self.pos == Pos::InChunk {\n            self.discard_chunk_body()?;\n        }\n        // Following CONT chunks.\n        while self.flags & FLAG_CONT != 0 {\n            if !self.enter_frame()? {\n                return Err(Error::corrupt(&self.path, \"trailer inside record\"));\n            }\n            if self.flags & FLAG_FIRST != 0 {\n                return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                    &self.path,\n                    \"FIRST chunk before record ended\",\n                ));\n            }\n            self.discard_chunk_body()?;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Decode the next record head. Returns None at the trailer.\n    pub fn next_head(&mut self) -> Result<Option<RecordHead>> {\n        // Finish a record the caller did not fully consume.\n        if self.pos == Pos::InChunk {\n            self.drain_record()?;\n        }\n        // At a boundary (also covers CONT chains from skipped records).\n        while self.flags & FLAG_CONT != 0 {\n            if !self.enter_frame()? {\n                return Err(Error::corrupt(&self.path, \"trailer inside record\"));\n            }\n            self.discard_chunk_body()?;\n        }\n        if !self.enter_frame()? {\n            return Ok(None);\n        }\n        if self.flags & FLAG_FIRST == 0 {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                &self.path,\n                \"record does not begin with a FIRST chunk\",\n            ));\n        }\n        // Pull the whole first payload (bounded by CHUNK_MAX).\n        let len = self.remaining as usize;\n        let mut payload = vec![0u8; len];\n        let mut got = 0;\n        while got < len {\n            let n = self.file.read(&mut payload[got..])?;\n            if n == 0 {\n                return Err(Error::corrupt(&self.path, \"first chunk truncated\"));\n            }\n            self.crc.write(&payload[got..got + n]);\n            self.remaining -= n as u32;\n            got += n;\n        }\n        if self.crc.finish() != self.expected_crc {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(&self.path, \"head chunk CRC mismatch\"));\n        }\n        let has_more = self.flags & FLAG_CONT != 0;\n        if !has_more {\n            self.pos = Pos::RecordBoundary;\n        }\n        // Stay InChunk if has_more: remaining == 0 signals \"enter next frame\".\n        let head = decode_head(&self.path, &payload)?;\n        self.records_seen += 1;\n        Ok(Some(RecordHead {\n            seq: head.seq,\n            nl: head.nl,\n            keys: head.keys,\n            prefix: head.prefix,\n            has_more,\n        }))\n    }\n\n    /// Read continuation value bytes. Returns 0 at end of record.\n    pub fn read_value(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize> {\n        if buf.is_empty() || self.pos == Pos::RecordBoundary {\n            return Ok(0);\n        }\n        if self.remaining == 0 {\n            // Enter the next chunk of this record.\n            if !self.enter_frame()? {\n                return Err(Error::corrupt(&self.path, \"trailer inside record value\"));\n            }\n            if self.flags & FLAG_FIRST != 0 {\n                return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                    &self.path,\n                    \"FIRST chunk inside a record value\",\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n        let want = buf.len().min(self.remaining as usize);\n        let n = self.file.read(&mut buf[..want])?;\n        if n == 0 {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(&self.path, \"value chunk truncated\"));\n        }\n        self.crc.write(&buf[..n]);\n        self.remaining -= n as u32;\n        if self.remaining == 0 {\n            self.check_crc()?;\n        }\n        Ok(n)\n    }\n\n    /// Verify the trailer and record count. Consumes any records the caller\n    /// never visited so corruption later in a run is still caught.\n    pub fn finish(mut self) -> Result<u64> {\n        // Drain a partially consumed record.\n        if self.pos == Pos::InChunk {\n            self.drain_record()?;\n        }\n        // Walk remaining records.\n        loop {\n            let had_cont = self.flags & FLAG_CONT != 0;\n            if had_cont {\n                if !self.enter_frame()? {\n                    return Err(Error::corrupt(&self.path, \"trailer inside record\"));\n                }\n                self.drain_record()?;\n                continue;\n            }\n            if !self.enter_frame()? {\n                break; // trailer\n            }\n            if self.flags & FLAG_FIRST == 0 {\n                return Err(Error::corrupt(&self.path, \"non-first chunk at boundary\"));\n            }\n            self.discard_chunk_body()?;\n            self.drain_record()?;\n        }\n        // Trailer carries the count right after its type byte.\n        let mut count_bytes = [0u8; 8];\n        read_exact(&mut self.file, &mut count_bytes, &self.path)?;\n        let count = u64::from_le_bytes(count_bytes);\n        // Any trailing bytes are an error (trailer is the last 9 bytes).\n        if self.read_u8()?.is_some() {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(&self.path, \"bytes after trailer\"));\n        }\n        if count != self.records_seen {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                &self.path,\n                format!(\"trailer reports {count} records but {0} seen\", self.records_seen),\n            ));\n        }\n        Ok(count)\n    }\n}\n\nstruct HeadDecoded {\n    seq: u64,\n    nl: bool,\n    keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n    prefix: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\nfn decode_head(path: &str, p: &[u8]) -> Result<HeadDecoded> {\n    if p.len() < 13 {\n        return Err(Error::corrupt(path, \"head chunk too short\"));\n    }\n    let seq = u64::from_le_bytes(p[0..8].try_into().unwrap());\n    let nl = p[8] != 0;\n    let key_count = u32::from_le_bytes(p[9..13].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;\n    let mut pos = 13;\n    let mut keys = Vec::with_capacity(key_count);\n    for _ in 0..key_count {\n        if pos + 4 > p.len() {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(path, \"truncated key length\"));\n        }\n        let kl = u32::from_le_bytes(p[pos..pos + 4].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;\n        pos += 4;\n        if pos + kl > p.len() {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(path, \"truncated key bytes\"));\n        }\n        keys.push(p[pos..pos + kl].to_vec());\n        pos += kl;\n    }\n    Ok(HeadDecoded {\n        seq,\n        nl,\n        keys,\n        prefix: p[pos..].to_vec(),\n    })\n}\n\nfn read_exact(f: &mut Box<dyn VFile>, buf: &mut [u8], path: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    let mut got = 0;\n    while got < buf.len() {\n        let n = f.read(&mut buf[got..])?;\n        if n == 0 {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                path,\n                format!(\"unexpected EOF (wanted {} bytes)\", buf.len()),\n            ));\n        }\n        got += n;\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn read_exact_opt(f: &mut Box<dyn VFile>, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<()> {\n    let mut got = 0;\n    while got < buf.len() {\n        let n = f.read(&mut buf[got..])?;\n        if n == 0 {\n            return Err(Error::io(\n                io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof, \"eof\"),\n                String::new(),\n            ));\n        }\n        got += n;\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::io::RealVfs;\n\n    fn tmp_dir(tag: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {\n        let d = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\"extsort-sf-{tag}-{}\", std::process::id()));\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&d);\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&d).unwrap();\n        d\n    }\n\n    struct SliceDrain<'a> {\n        data: &'a [u8],\n        pos: usize,\n    }\n    impl<'a> GiantDrain for SliceDrain<'a> {\n        fn pull(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<Pull> {\n            // Deliberately small steps to exercise multi-chunk boundaries.\n            let step = (buf.len() / 3 + 1).min(buf.len()).min(self.data.len() - self.pos);\n            buf[..step].copy_from_slice(&self.data[self.pos..self.pos + step]);\n            self.pos += step;\n            Ok(Pull {\n                bytes: step,\n                end_of_record: self.pos == self.data.len(),\n                nl: true,\n            })\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn read_all_value(r: &mut RunReader, head: &RecordHead) -> Vec<u8> {\n        let mut out = head.prefix.clone();\n out.extend_from_slice(&buf[..z]);\n        }\n        out\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn small_records_roundtrip() {\n        let d = tmp_dir(\"small\");\n        let vfs = RealVfs::new(&d);\n b\"world\").unwrap();\n        let (path, n) = w.commit(&vfs).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(n, 2);\n\n        let mut r = RunReader::open(&vfs, &path).unwrap();\n        let h0 = r.next_head().unwrap().unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(h0.seq, 0);\n        assert!(h0.nl && !h0.has_more);\n        assert_eq!(h0.prefix, b\"hello\");\n        assert_eq!(read_all_value(&mut r, &h0), b\"hello\");\n        let h1 = r.next_head().unwrap().unwrap();\n        assert!(!h1.nl);\n        assert_eq!(read_all_value(&mut r, &h1), b\"world\");\n        assert!(r.next_head().unwrap().is_none());\n        r.finish().unwrap();\n        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&d).ok();\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn giant_record_roundtrip() {\n        let d = assert_eq!(n, 1);\n\n        let mut r = RunReader::open(&vfs, &path).unwrap();\n        let h = r.next_head().unwrap().unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(h.seq, 7);\n        assert!(h.has_more);\n        let out = read_all_value(&mut r, &h);\n        assert_eq!(&out[..3], b\"abc\");\n        assert_eq!(out.len(), 3 + big.len());\n        assert!(out[3..].iter().all(|&b| b == b'x'));\n        assert!(r.next_head().unwrap().is_none());\n        r.finish().unwrap();\n        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&d).ok();\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn exactly_one_giant_chunk_works() {\n        // Value fits in the head chunk but writer is driven through drain.\n        let d = tmp_dir(\"onechunk\");\n        let vfs = RealVfs::new(&d);\n        let val = vec![b'q'; 100];\n        let mut w = RunWriter::create(&vfs, \".\", \"o\").unwrap();\n        let mut drain = SliceDrain { data: &val, pos: 0 };\n        w.write_giant(1, true, &[b\"k\".to_vec()], b\"z\", &mut drain).unwrap();\n        let (path, _) = w.commit(&vfs).unwrap();\n        let mut r = RunReader::open(&vfs, &path).unwrap();\n        let h = r.next_head().unwrap().unwrap();\n        assert!(!h.has_more);\n        let out = read_all_value(&mut r, &h);\n        assert_eq!(out.len(), 1 + val.len());\n        r.finish().unwrap();\n        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&d).ok();\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_run_valid() {\n std::fs::remove_dir_all(&d).ok();\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn detects_crc_corruption() {\n        let d = tmp_dir(\"crc\");\n        let vfs = RealVfs::new(&d);\n        let mut w = RunWriter::create(&vfs, \".\", \"c\").unwrap();\n        w.write_record(0, true, &[b\"k\".to_vec()], b\"payload\").unwrap();\n        let (path, _) = w.commit(&vfs).unwrap();\n        let real = On-disk run-segment format and its sequential writer/reader.\n//!\n//! # Disk format\n//!\n//! A run is one *committed* (renamed + fsynced) file:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! magic   : 8 bytes = b\"EXTSORT\\x02\"\n//! frames  : zero or more record frames\n//! trailer : frame type byte = FRAME_TRAILER, then u64 LE record count\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Every frame begins with a 1-byte discriminator so a pure sequential reader\n//! can tell records from the trailer:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! FRAME_CHUNK   = 0x10\n//! FRAME_TRAILER = 0x20\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Chunk frame layout:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! ftype   : u8        FRAME_CHUNK\n//! flags   : u8        bit0 = FIRST chunk of a record\n//!                     bit1 = CONT  — another chunk follows this one\n//!                     single-chunk record: FIRST, no CONT\n//!                     final chunk of multi-chunk record: neither bit set\n//! length  : u32 LE    payload length (<= CHUNK_MAX)\n//! crc32   : u32 LE    CRC-32/IEEE of the payload\n//! payload : `length` bytes\n//! ```\n//!\n//! The FIRST chunk payload is:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! u64 LE   seq        original input sequence number (stability tie-break)\n//! u8       nl         1 if the record ended with '\\n' in the input\n//! u32 LE   key_count  number of key components\n//! per key: u32 LE len + len key bytes\n//! bytes    value prefix (record bytes excluding the trailing '\\n')\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Later chunks hold only continuation value bytes. This lets a record of\n//! unbounded length be spilled with bounded memory: a giant line streams\n//! chunk-by-chunk while its (bounded) key stays in the head.\n//!\n//! Integrity: each chunk carries a payload CRC verified as bytes are consumed;\n//! the trailer repeats the record count, detecting torn tails; magic detects a\n//! wrong/truncated file.\n\nuse std::io;\n\nuse crate::crc::Crc;\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::io::VFile;\n\n/// Magic prefix of every run file.\npub const MAGIC: &[u8; 8] = b\"EXTSORT\\x02\";\n\nconst FRAME_CHUNK: u8 = 0x10;\nconst FRAME_TRAILER: u8 = 0x20;\n\nconst FLAG_FIRST: u8 = 0x01;\nconst FLAG_CONT: u8 = 0x02;\n\n/// Maximum payload bytes in one chunk.\npub const CHUNK_MAX: usize = 16 * 1024;\n/// Value bytes targeted for a giant record's FIRST chunk.\npub const GIANT_HEAD_VALUE: usize = 8 * 1024;\n\nconst CHUNK_HDR_LEN: usize = 1 + 1 + 4 + 4; // ftype, flags, len, crc\n\n/// Result of pulling bytes from a giant record's input source.\npub struct Pull {\n    /// Bytes made available.\n    pub bytes: usize,\n    /// True iff these bytes end the record (the trailing newline is consumed\n    /// by the drain and not included).\n    pub end_of_record: bool,\n    /// Whether the input record terminated with a newline.\n    pub nl: bool,\n}\n\n/// Source streamed by [`RunWriter::write_giant`] for an over-large record.\npub trait GiantDrain {\n    /// Fill the beginning of `buf` with up to `buf.len()` record bytes.\n    fn pull(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<Pull>;\n}\n\n/// Sequential run writer. Dropping without [`RunWriter::commit`] leaves a\n/// `*.tmp` file that recovery ignores.\npub struct RunWriter {\n    file: Box<dyn VFile>,\n    tmp_path: String,\n    final_path: String,\n    records: u64,\n}\n\nimpl RunWriter {\n    pub fn create(vfs: &dyn crate::io::Vfs, dir: &str, name: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n        let tmp_path = format!(\"{dir}/{name}.run.tmp\");\n        let final_path = format!(\"{dir}/{name}.run\");\n        let mut file = vfs.create(&tmp_path)?;\n        file.write_all(MAGIC)?;\n        Ok(RunWriter {\n            file,\n            tmp_path,\n            final_path,\n            records: 0,\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn record_count(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.records\n    }\n    pub fn tmp_path(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.tmp_path\n    }\n    pub fn final_path(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.final_path\n    }\n\n    fn key_overhead(keys: &[Vec<u8>]) -> usize {\n        8 + 1 + 4 + keys.iter().map(|k| 4 + k.len()).sum::<usize>()\n    }\n\n    fn encode_head(seq: u64, nl: bool, keys: &[Vec<u8>], prefix: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {\n        let mut p = Vec::with_capacity(Self::key_overhead(keys) + prefix.len());\n        p.extend_from_slice(&seq.to_le_bytes());\n        p.push(if nl { 1 } else { 0 });\n        p.extend_from_slice(&(keys.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n        for k in keys {\n            p.extend_from_slice(&(k.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n            p.extend_from_slice(k);\n        }\n        p.extend_from_slice(prefix);\n        p\n    }\n\n    fn write_chunk(&mut self, flags: u8, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {\n        debug_assert!(payload.len() <= CHUNK_MAX);\n        let mut crc = Crc::new();\n        crc.write(payload);\n        let mut hdr = [0u8; CHUNK_HDR_LEN];\n        hdr[0] = FRAME_CHUNK;\n        hdr[1] = flags;\n        hdr[2..6].copy_from_slice(&(payload.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());\n        hdr[6..10].copy_from_slice(&crc.finish().to_le_bytes());\n        self.file.write_all(&hdr)?;\n        self.file.write_all(payload)\n    }\n\n    /// Write one fully-resident record.\n    pub fn write_record(&mut self, seq: u64, nl: bool, keys: &[Vec<u8>], value: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {\n        let overhead = Self::key_overhead(keys);\n        if overhead + value.len() <= CHUNK_MAX {\n            let payload = Self::encode_head(seq, nl, keys, value);\n            self.write_chunk(FLAG_FIRST, &payload)?;\n        } else {\n            // Fully buffered but too big for one chunk: stream from a slice.\n            let head_value = (CHUNK_MAX - overhead).min(value.len());\n            let payload = Self::encode_head(seq, nl, keys, &value[..head_value]);\n            self.write_chunk(FLAG_FIRST | FLAG_CONT, &payload)?;\n            let mut pos = head_value;\n            while pos < value.len() {\n                let n = CHUNK_MAX.min(value.len() - pos);\n                let end = pos + n == value.len();\n                self.write_chunk(if end { 0 } else { FLAG_CONT }, &value[pos..pos + n])?;\n                pos += n;\n            }\n        }\n        self.records += 1;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Stream a giant record. `prefix` is the buffered head value; the rest is\n    /// pulled from `drain`.\n    pub fn write_giant(\n        &mut self,\n        seq: u64,\n        nl: bool,\n        keys: &[Vec<u8>],\n        prefix: &[u8],\n        drain: &mut dyn GiantDrain,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        let overhead = Self::key_overhead(keys);\n        // Assemble first payload: head + up to (CHUNK_MAX-overhead) value bytes.\n        let mut first = Self::encode_head(seq, nl, keys, prefix);\n        let mut buf = vec![0u8; CHUNK_MAX];\n        let mut ended = false;\n        while first.len() < CHUNK_MAX {\n            let want = CHUNK_MAX - first.len();\n            let pull = drain.pull(&mut buf[..want])?;\n            if pull.bytes > 0 {\n                first.extend_from_slice(&buf[..pull.bytes]);\n            }\n            if pull.end_of_record {\n                ended = true;\n                break;\n            }\n            if pull.bytes == 0 {\n                return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                    &self.tmp_path,\n                    \"giant drain returned no progress and no end\",\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n        if !ended {\n            self.write_chunk(FLAG_FIRST | FLAG_CONT, &first)?;\n        } else {\n            self.write_chunk(FLAG_FIRST, &first)?;\n        }\n        while !ended {\n            let mut filled = 0;\n            let mut nl_flag = nl;\n            while filled < CHUNK_MAX {\n                let pull = drain.pull(&mut buf[filled..])?;\n                filled += pull.bytes;\n                nl_flag = pull.nl;\n                if pull.end_of_record {\n                    ended = true;\n                    break;\n                }\n                if pull.bytes == 0 {\n                    return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                        &self.tmp_path,\n                        \"giant drain stalled mid-record\",\n                    ));\n                }\n            }\n            let _ = nl_flag;\n            self.write_chunk(if ended { 0 } else { FLAG_CONT }, &buf[..filled])?;\n        }\n        self.records += 1;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Write trailer, fsync, close, atomically rename to the committed name.\n    pub fn commit(mut self, vfs: &dyn crate::io::Vfs) -> Result<(String, u64)> {\n        let mut tr = [0u8; 9];\n        tr[0] = FRAME_TRAILER;\n        tr[1..9].copy_from_slice(&self.records.to_le_bytes());\n        self.file.write_all(&tr)?;\n        self.file.flush()?;\n        self.file.sync_all()?;\n        drop(self.file);\n        vfs.rename(&self.tmp_path, &self.final_path)?;\n        Ok((self.final_path, self.records))\n    }\n}\n\n/// Decoded head of one run record.\npub struct RecordHead {\n    pub seq: u64,\n    pub nl: bool,\n    pub keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n    /// Value bytes carried in the FIRST chunk (whole value for small records).\n    pub prefix: Vec<u8>,\n    /// CONT flag of the first chunk: true when value continues.\n    pub has_more: bool,\n}\n\n/// Reader position.\n#[derive(PartialEq, Eq)]\nenum Pos {\n    /// Magic verified, nothing read yet.\n    Start,\n    /// Last thing consumed was a chunk with CONT clear; next is frame type.\n    RecordBoundary,\n    /// Inside a record, `remaining` bytes of current chunk left.\n    InChunk,\n    /// Trailer frame read; nothing follows.\n    Trailer,\n}\n\n/// Sequential run reader verifying per-chunk CRCs.\npub struct RunReader {\n    file: Box<dyn VFile>,\n    path: String,\n    pos: Pos,\n    flags: u8,\n    remaining: u32,\n    crc: Crc,\n    expected_crc: u32,\n    records_seen: u64,\n}\n\nimpl RunReader {\n    pub fn open(vfs: &dyn crate::io::Vfs, path: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n        let mut file = vfs.open(path)?;\n        let mut magic = [0u8; 8];\n        read_exact(&mut file, &mut magic, path)?;\n        if &magic != MAGIC {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(path, \"bad magic header\"));\n        }\n        Ok(RunReader {\n            file,\n            path: path.to_string(),\n            pos: Pos::Start,\n            flags: 0,\n            remaining: 0,\n            crc: Crc::new(),\n            expected_crc: 0,\n            records_seen: 0,\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn path(&self) -> &str {\n        &self.path\n    }\n\n    fn read_u8(&mut self) -> Result<Option<u8>> {\n        let mut b = [0u8; 1];\n        match read_exact_opt(&mut self.file, &mut b) {\n            Ok(()) => Ok(Some(b[0])),\n            Err(Error::Io(e, _)) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof => Ok(None),\n            Err(e) => Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Read the next chunk header (called at a frame boundary). Returns false\n    /// if the trailer is found instead.\n    fn enter_frame(&mut self) -> Result<bool> {\n        let ftype = self\n            .read_u8()?\n            .ok_or_else(|| Error::corrupt(&self.path, \"EOF where frame expected\"))?;\n        if ftype == FRAME_TRAILER {\n            self.pos = Pos::Trailer;\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n        if ftype != FRAME_CHUNK {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                &self.path,\n                format!(\"invalid frame type byte 0x{ftype:02x}\"),\n            ));\n        }\n        let mut rest = [0u8; CHUNK_HDR_LEN - 1];\n        read_exact(&mut self.file, &mut rest, &self.path)?;\n        self.flags = rest[0];\n        self.remaining = u32::from_le_bytes([rest[1], rest[2], rest[3], rest[4]]);\n        self.expected_crc = u32::from_le_bytes([rest[5], rest[6], rest[7], rest[8]]);\n        if self.remaining as usize > CHUNK_MAX {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                &self.path,\n                format!(\"chunk length {} exceeds frame max\", self.remaining),\n            ));\n        }\n        self.crc = Crc::new();\n        self.pos = Pos::InChunk;\n        Ok(true)\n    }\n\n    /// Discard the rest of the current chunk and verify its CRC.\n    fn discard_chunk_body(&mut self) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut buf = [0u8; 8192];\n        while self.remaining > 0 {\n            let want = buf.len().min(self.remaining as usize);\n            let n = self.file.read(&mut buf[..want])?;\n            if n == 0 {\n                return Err(Error::corrupt(&self.path, \"chunk payload truncated\"));\n            }\n            self.crc.write(&buf[..n]);\n            self.remaining -= n as u32;\n        }\n        self.check_crc()\n    }\n\n    fn check_crc(&mut self) -> Result<()> {\n        if self.crc.finish() != self.expected_crc {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                &self.path,\n                \"chunk CRC mismatch — segment corrupted\",\n            ));\n        }\n        if self.flags & FLAG_CONT == 0 {\n            self.pos = Pos::RecordBoundary;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Skip every remaining chunk of the current record.\n    pub fn drain_record(&mut self) -> Result<()> {\n        // Current (possibly partly consumed) chunk.\n        if self.pos == Pos::InChunk {\n            self.discard_chunk_body()?;\n        }\n        // Following CONT chunks.\n        while self.flags & FLAG_CONT != 0 {\n            if !self.enter_frame()? {\n                return Err(Error::corrupt(&self.path, \"trailer inside record\"));\n            }\n            if self.flags & FLAG_FIRST != 0 {\n                return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                    &self.path,\n                    \"FIRST chunk before record ended\",\n                ));\n            }\n            self.discard_chunk_body()?;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Decode the next record head. Returns None at the trailer.\n    pub fn next_head(&mut self) -> Result<Option<RecordHead>> {\n        // Finish a record the caller did not fully consume.\n        if self.pos == Pos::InChunk {\n            self.drain_record()?;\n        }\n        // At a boundary (also covers CONT chains from skipped records).\n        while self.flags & FLAG_CONT != 0 {\n            if !self.enter_frame()? Consumes any records the caller\n    /// never visited so corruption later in a run is still caught.\n    pub fn finish(mut self) -> Result<u64> {\n        // Drain a partially consumed record.\n        if self.pos == Pos::InChunk {\n            self.drain_record()?;\n        }\n        // Walk remaining records.\n        loop {\n            let had_cont = self.flags & FLAG_CONT != 0;\n            if had_cont {\n                if !self.enter_frame()? {\n                    return Err(Error::corrupt(&self.path, \"trailer inside record\"));\n                }\n                self.drain_record()?;\n                continue;\n            }\n            if !self.enter_frame()? {\n                break; // trailer\n            }\n            if self.flags & FLAG_FIRST == 0 {\n                return Err(Error::corrupt(&self.path, \"non-first chunk at boundary\"));\n            }\n            self.discard_chunk_body()?;\n            self.drain_record()?;\n        }\n        // Trailer carries the count right after its type byte.\n        let mut count_bytes = [0u8; 8];\n        read_exact(&mut self.file, &mut count_bytes, &self.path)?;\n        let count = u64::from_le_bytes(count_bytes);\n        // Any trailing bytes are an error (trailer is the last 9 bytes).\n        if self.read_u8()?.is_some() {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(&self.path, \"bytes after trailer\"));\n        }\n        if count != self.records_seen {\n            return Err(Error::corrupt(\n                &self.path,\n                format!(\"trailer reports {count} records but {0} seen\", self.records_seen),\n            ));\n        }\n        Ok(count)\n    }","new_string":"    /// Verify the trailer and record count. {"parentUuid":"a4bae66a-cf9f-449f-bd77-610470efdf30","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_vfn7e4r2q0nf6dj5zb1ybiqf","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp2/a/src/scanner.rs","content":"//! Bounded-memory input scanner.\n//!\n//! Records are lines separated by `\\n` (an optional preceding `\\r` is part of\n//! the record's terminator, not its value). The scanner keeps at most\n//! `small_limit` bytes of a line in memory:\n//!\n//! * Lines up to that limit are returned to the caller as owned bytes\n//!   ([`ScannerEvent::Small`]) and sorted in memory.\n//! * A line that grows past the limit becomes a [`ScannerEvent::GiantStart`]\n//!   carrying the bounded prefix plus the key (when resolvable from a prefix).\n//!   The caller then drives [`LineScanner::pull_giant`] through the\n//!   [`crate::sortfile::GiantDrain`] impl to stream the remainder straight into\n//!   a run, never holding the whole record. After the record is drained,\n//!   scanning continues normally.\n//!\n//! Reading goes through a small internal buffer whose size is part of the\n//! declared memory budget (see [`crate::budget`]).\n\nuse std::io;\n\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::key::{prefix_has_key, KeySpec};\nuse crate::sortfile::GiantDrain;\n\n/// Input stream the scanner reads from.\npub type Input = Box<dyn io::Read + Send>;\n\n/// Default internal read buffer (16 KiB).\npub const READ_BUFFER: usize = 16 * 1024;\n\n/// A record that fits in the memory window.\npub struct SmallRecord {\n    /// Record bytes without the line terminator.\n    pub line: Vec<u8>,\n    /// Original 0-based input sequence number.\n    pub seq: u64,\n    /// Whether the record ended with `\\n` (false only for the final line with\n    /// no trailing newline).\n    pub nl: bool,\n}\n\n/// A record too large to keep resident; its key and a prefix are known, the\n/// rest must be streamed via the [`GiantDrain`] impl on the scanner.\npub struct GiantRecord {\n    pub seq: u64,\n    pub nl: bool,\n    pub prefix: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\n/// What [`LineScanner::next`] found.\npub enum ScannerEvent {\n    Small(SmallRecord),\n    Giant(GiantRecord),\n    End,\n}\n\n/// Stateful streaming line scanner.\npub struct LineScanner {\n    input: Input,\n    readbuf: Vec<u8>,\n    read_pos: usize,\n    read_fill: usize,\n    eof: bool,\n\n    small_limit: usize,\n    spec: KeySpec,\n\n    /// Accumulated bytes of the line currently being scanned.\n    cur: Vec<u8>,\n    seq: u64,\n\n    // Giant mode state.\n    giant: bool,\n    giant_nl: bool,\n    /// Bytes of `cur` already handed to the writer as head prefix; the drain\n    /// serves the remainder of `cur` first, then the underlying input.\n    giant_cur_served: usize,\n    /// True when the giant record's trailing newline has been seen and served.\n    giant_done: bool,\n}\n\nimpl LineScanner {\n    pub fn new(input: Input, spec: KeySpec, small_limit: usize) -> Self {\n        LineScanner {\n            input,\n            readbuf: vec![0u8; READ_BUFFER],\n            read_pos: 0,\n            read_fill: 0,\n            eof: false,\n            small_limit,\n            spec,\n            cur: Vec::with_capacity(small_limit.min(4096)),\n            seq: 0,\n            giant: false,\n            giant_nl: false,\n            giant_cur_served: 0,\n            giant_done: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn seq(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.seq\n    }\n\n    pub fn spec(&self) -> &KeySpec {\n        &self.spec\n    }\n\n    /// Read one more raw byte from the input through the internal buffer.\n    fn fill_byte(&mut self) -> Result<Option<u8>> {\n        if self.read_pos >= self.read_fill {\n            if self.eof {\n                return Ok(None);\n            }\n            let n = self.input.read(&mut self.readbuf)?;\n            if n == 0 {\n                self.eof = true;\n                return Ok(None);\n            }\n            self.read_pos = 0;\n            self.read_fill = n;\n        }\n        let b = self.readbuf[self.read_pos];\n        self.read_pos += 1;\n        Ok(Some(b))\n    }\n\n    /// Scan the next record. Must not be called while a giant record is\n    /// pending (call [`LineScanner::drain_done`] after streaming it).\n    pub fn next(&mut self) -> Result<ScannerEvent> {\n        debug_assert!(!self.giant, \"giant record not fully drained\");\n        self.cur.clear();\n        let seq = self.seq;\n        let mut nl = false;\n        let mut giant_prefix: Option<Vec<u8>> = None;\n\n        loop {\n            let b = match self.fill_byte()? {\n                Some(b) => b,\n                None => break,\n            };\n            if b == b'\\n' {\n                nl = true;\n                break;\n            }\n            self.cur.push(b);\n            // Oversize threshold: switch this record into giant streaming.\n            if self.cur.len() > self.small_limit {\n                // For a whole-line key the key is the whole record, which\n                // cannot fit — bail with a clear error rather than silently\n                // exceeding the budget.\n                if crate::key::key_needs_whole_line(&self.spec) {\n                    return Err(Error::KeyTooLarge {\n                        seq,\n                        needed: self.cur.len(),\n                        budget: self.small_limit as u64,\n                    });\n                }\n                // The key must be resolvable from a prefix once the last\n                // needed column is complete. Keep reading *without* retaining\n                // more than small_limit bytes: but we need the key bytes,\n                // which by contract fit; detect completeness and snapshot.\n                // Continue accumulating only until key is present; from then\n                // on bytes move into drain mode. We mark the giant boundary at\n                // the current length and resolve the key when the column ends.\n                giant_prefix = Some(self.enter_giant(seq)?);\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n\n        if let Some(prefix) = giant_prefix {\n            self.seq += 1;\n            return Ok(ScannerEvent::Giant(GiantRecord {\n                seq,\n                nl: false, // finalized later during draining\n                prefix,\n            }));\n        }\n\n        if self.cur.is_empty() && !nl {\n            // No bytes at all and EOF: end of input.\n            return Ok(ScannerEvent::End);\n        }\n\n        // Strip a trailing CR that belonged to CRLF.\n        if self.cur.last() == Some(&b'\\r') {\n            self.cur.pop();\n        }\n        self.seq += 1;\n        Ok(ScannerEvent::Small(SmallRecord {\n            line: std::mem::take(&mut self.cur),\n            seq,\n            nl,\n        }))\n    }\n\n    /// Transition into giant streaming. Reads further bytes (without retaining\n    /// them beyond the bounded prefix) until the requested key columns are\n    /// complete, snapshots the prefix, then prepares the drain.\n    fn enter_giant(&mut self, seq: u64) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {\n        // At entry self.cur holds small_limit+1 bytes and already exceeded the\n        // limit. We must produce a bounded prefix (cap at small_limit) that\n        // contains the full key.\n        while !prefix_has_key(&self.spec, &self.cur) {\n            if self.cur.len() >= self.small_limit {\n                // Key still not known but the buffer is at the cap: drop the\n                // front only if key columns are searched... keys are at the\n                // beginning of the line, so instead keep reading into a\n                // separate *key window* by trimming suffix bytes: we must not\n                // lose key bytes at the front. Grow temporarily is forbidden,\n                // so rotate: discard from a point after the key region is\n                // impossible to know. The documented contract is that the key\n                // fits within the budget; reaching here violates it.\n                return Err(Error::KeyTooLarge {\n                    seq,\n                    needed: self.cur.len() + 1,\n                    budget: self.small_limit as u64,\n                });\n            }\n            let b = match self.fill_byte()? {\n                Some(b) => b,\n                None => break, // line ends; last column reaches EOL\n            };\n            if b == b'\\n' {\n                // Line ended before the key column count: missing columns are\n                // empty, so the key is effectively known. Put the newline into\n                // the drain as the terminator.\n                self.giant_nl = true;\n                break;\n            }\n            self.cur.push(b);\n        }\n\n        // Snapshot exactly small_limit bytes as the head prefix.\n        let cutoff = self.cur.len().min(self.small_limit);\n        let prefix = self.cur[..cutoff].to_vec();\n        // Bytes beyond cutoff are the first drain data: keep them in `cur` and\n        // let the drain serve them, then move to input.\n        self.giant_cur_served = cutoff;\n        self.giant = true;\n        self.giant_done = false;\n        if self.giant_nl {\n            // Newline already consumed; drain must signal EOR after serving the\n            // leftover cur bytes.\n            self.giant_pending_nl = true;\n        }\n        Ok(prefix)\n    }\n\n    // see struct extension below\n    #[doc(hidden)]\n    pub fn giant_pending_nl_set(&mut self, v: bool) {\n        self.giant_pending_nl = v;\n    }\n\n    /// True once the giant record has been fully pulled.\n    pub fn drain_done(&self) -> bool {\n        self.giant_done\n    }\n\n    /// Sequence / newline of the in-flight giant record (nl is finalized when\n    /// the line terminator is reached during draining).\n    pub fn giant_newline(&self) -> bool {\n        self.giant_nl\n    }\n}\n\n// The newline may be encountered either before switching (captured into the\n// prefix region) or while draining.\nimpl LineScanner {\n    fn _placeholder() {}\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn scan_all(data: &[u8], spec: KeySpec, limit: usize) -> Vec<(Vec<u8>, u64, bool)> {\n        let mut s = LineScanner::new(Box::new(data), spec, limit);\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        loop {\n            match s.next().unwrap() {\n                ScannerEvent::End => break,\n                ScannerEvent::Small(r) => out.push((r.line, r.seq, r.nl)),\n                ScannerEvent::Giant(_) => panic!(\"unexpected giant record\"),\n            }\n        }\n        out\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn simple_lines() {\n        let data = b\"alpha\\nbeta\\r\\ngamma\\ntail\";\n        let rows = scan_all(data, KeySpec::default(), 1024);\n        assert_eq!(rows.len(), 4);\n        assert_eq!(rows[0], (b\"alpha\".to_vec(), 0, true));\n        assert_eq!(rows[1], (b\"beta\".to_vec(), 1, true)); // CR stripped\n        assert_eq!(rows[2], (b\"gamma\".to_vec(), 2, true));\n        assert_eq!(rows[3], (b\"tail\".to_vec(), 3, false)); // no trailing nl\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_input() {\n        let rows = scan_all(b\"\", KeySpec::default(), 1024);\n        assert!(rows.is_empty());\n        let rows2 = scan_all(b\"\\n\", KeySpec::default(), 1024);\n        assert_eq!(rows2.len(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(rows2[0].0, b\"\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn whole_line_giant_errors() {\n        let mut s = LineScanner::new(Box::new(vec![0u8; Reading goes through a small internal buffer whose size is part of the\n//! declared memory budget (see [`crate::budget`]).\n\nuse std::io;\n\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::key::{prefix_has_key, KeySpec};\nuse crate::sortfile::GiantDrain;\n\n/// Input stream the scanner reads from.\npub type Input = Box<dyn io::Read + Send>;\n\n/// Default internal read buffer (16 KiB).\npub const READ_BUFFER: usize = 16 * 1024;\n\n/// A record that fits in the memory window.\npub struct SmallRecord {\n    /// Record bytes without the line terminator.\n    pub line: Vec<u8>,\n    /// Original 0-based input sequence number.\n    pub seq: u64,\n    /// Whether the record ended with `\\n` (false only for the final line with\n    /// no trailing newline).\n    pub nl: bool,\n}\n\n/// A record too large to keep resident; its key and a prefix are known, the\n/// rest must be streamed via the [`GiantDrain`] impl on the scanner.\npub struct GiantRecord {\n    pub seq: u64,\n    pub nl: bool,\n    pub prefix: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\n/// What [`LineScanner::next`] found.\npub enum ScannerEvent {\n    Small(SmallRecord),\n    Giant(GiantRecord),\n    End,\n}\n\n/// Stateful streaming line scanner.\npub struct LineScanner {\n    input: Input,\n    readbuf: Vec<u8>,\n    read_pos: usize,\n    read_fill: usize,\n    eof: bool,\n\n    small_limit: usize,\n    spec: KeySpec,\n\n    /// Accumulated bytes of the line currently being scanned.\n    cur: Vec<u8>,\n    seq: u64,\n\n    // Giant mode state.\n    giant: bool,\n    giant_nl: bool,\n    /// Bytes of `cur` already handed to the writer as head prefix; the drain\n    /// serves the remainder of `cur` first, then the underlying input.\n    giant_cur_served: usize,\n    /// True when the giant record's trailing newline has been seen and served.\n    giant_done: bool,\n}\n\nimpl LineScanner {\n    pub fn new(input: Input, spec: KeySpec, small_limit: usize) -> Self {\n        LineScanner {\n            input,\n            readbuf: vec![0u8; READ_BUFFER],\n            read_pos: 0,\n            read_fill: 0,\n            eof: false,\n            small_limit,\n            spec,\n            cur: Vec::with_capacity(small_limit.min(4096)),\n            seq: 0,\n            giant: false,\n            giant_nl: false,\n            giant_cur_served: 0,\n            giant_done: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn seq(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.seq\n    }\n\n    pub fn spec(&self) -> &KeySpec {\n        &self.spec\n    }\n\n    /// Read one more raw byte from the input through the internal buffer.\n    fn fill_byte(&mut self) -> Result<Option<u8>> {\n        if self.read_pos >= self.read_fill {\n            if self.eof {\n                return Ok(None);\n            }\n            let n = self.input.read(&mut self.readbuf)?;\n            if n == 0 {\n                self.eof = true;\n                return Ok(None);\n            }\n            self.read_pos = 0;\n            self.read_fill = n;\n        }\n        let b = self.readbuf[self.read_pos];\n        self.read_pos += 1;\n        Ok(Some(b))\n    }\n\n    /// Scan the next record. Keep reading *without* retaining\n                // more than small_limit bytes: but we need the key bytes,\n                // which by contract fit; detect completeness and snapshot.\n                // Continue accumulating only until key is present; from then\n                // on bytes move into drain mode. We mark the giant boundary at\n                // the current length and resolve the key when the column ends.\n                giant_prefix = Some(self.enter_giant(seq)?);\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n\n        if let Some(prefix) = giant_prefix {\n            self.seq += 1;\n            return Ok(ScannerEvent::Giant(GiantRecord {\n                seq,\n                nl: false, // finalized later during draining\n                prefix,\n            }));\n        }\n\n        if self.cur.is_empty() && !nl {\n            // No bytes at all and EOF: end of input.\n            return Ok(ScannerEvent::End);\n        }\n\n        // Strip a trailing CR that belonged to CRLF.\n        if self.cur.last() == Some(&b'\\r') {\n            self.cur.pop();\n        }\n        self.seq += 1;\n        Ok(ScannerEvent::Small(SmallRecord {\n            line: std::mem::take(&mut self.cur),\n            seq,\n            nl,\n        }))\n    }\n\n    /// Transition into giant streaming. Grow temporarily is forbidden,\n                // so rotate: discard from a point after the key region is\n                // impossible to know. The documented contract is that the key\n                // fits within the budget; reaching here violates it.\n                return Err(Error::KeyTooLarge {\n                    seq,\n                    needed: self.cur.len() + 1,\n                    budget: self.small_limit as u64,\n                });\n            }\n            let b = match self.fill_byte()? {\n                Some(b) => b,\n                None => break, // line ends; last column reaches EOL\n            };\n            if b == b'\\n' {\n                // Line ended before the key column count: missing columns are\n                // empty, so the key is effectively known. drain must signal EOR after serving the\n            // leftover cur bytes.\n            self.giant_pending_nl = true;\n        }\n        Ok(prefix)\n    }\n\n    // see struct extension below\n    #[doc(hidden)]\n    pub fn giant_pending_nl_set(&mut self, v: bool) {\n        self.giant_pending_nl = v;\n    }\n\n    /// True once the giant record has been fully pulled.\n    pub fn drain_done(&self) -> bool {\n        self.giant_done\n    }\n\n    /// Sequence / newline of the in-flight giant record (nl is finalized when\n    /// the line terminator is reached during draining).\n    pub fn giant_newline(&self) -> bool {\n        self.giant_nl\n    }\n}\n\n// The newline may be encountered either before switching (captured into the\n// prefix region) or while draining.\nimpl LineScanner {\n    fn _placeholder() {}\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn scan_all(data: &[u8], spec: KeySpec, limit: usize) -> Vec<(Vec<u8>, u64, bool)> {\n        let mut s = LineScanner::new(Box::new(data), spec, limit);\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        loop {\n            match s.next().unwrap() {\n                ScannerEvent::End => break,\n                ScannerEvent::Small(r) => out.push((r.line, r.seq, r.nl)),\n                ScannerEvent::Giant(_) => panic!(\"unexpected giant record\"),\n            }\n        }\n        out\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn simple_lines() {\n        let data = b\"alpha\\nbeta\\r\\ngamma\\ntail\";\n        let rows = scan_all(data, KeySpec::default(), 1024);\n        assert_eq!(rows.len(), 4);\n        assert_eq!(rows[0], (b\"alpha\".to_vec(), 0, true));\n        assert_eq!(rows[1], (b\"beta\".to_vec(), 1, true)); The writer gets `(seq, nl, keys, prefix)`; the drain first serves\n//!   the rest of the buffered prefix, then input bytes, until the newline.\n//!\n//! Reading uses a small internal buffer whose size is included in the declared\n//! memory budget (see [`crate::budget`]).\n\nuse std::io;\n\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::key::{prefix_has_key, KeySpec};\nuse crate::sortfile::{GiantDrain, Pull};\n\n/// Input stream the scanner reads from.\npub type Input = Box<dyn io::Read + Send>;\n\n/// Internal read buffer (counted toward the memory budget).\npub const READ_BUFFER: usize = 16 * 1024;\n\n/// A record that fits inside the memory window.\npub struct SmallRecord {\n    pub line: Vec<u8>,\n    pub seq: u64,\n    pub nl: bool,\n}\n\n/// Event yielded per input record.\npub enum ScannerEvent {\n    Small(SmallRecord),\n    /// The caller must drain a giant record before calling `next` again.\n    Giant { seq: u64, nl: bool, keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>, prefix: Vec<u8> },\n    End,\n}\n\nenum Phase {\n    Line,\n    /// Draining a giant record; leftover `cur` bytes are served first.\n    GiantLeftover,\n    /// Streaming raw input for the giant record until its newline.\n    GiantStream,\n    /// Giant record finished.\n    GiantEnd,\n}\n\npub struct LineScanner {\n    input: Input,\n bookkeeping.\n    giant_nl: bool,\n    giant_served_leftover: bool,\n    /// While streaming, when the previous byte was '\\r' with the '\\n' pending.\n    pending_cr: bool,\n}\n\nimpl LineScanner {\n    pub fn new(input: Input, spec: KeySpec, small_limit: usize) -> Self {\n        LineScanner {\n            input,\n            readbuf: vec![0u8; READ_BUFFER],\n            read_pos: 0,\n            read_fill: 0,\n            eof: false,\n            small_limit,\n            spec,\n            cur: Vec::new(),\n            seq: 0,\n            phase: Phase::Line,\n            giant_nl: false,\n            giant_served_leftover: false,\n            pending_cr: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn seq(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.seq\n    }\n    pub fn spec(&self) -> &KeySpec {\n        &self.spec\n    }\n\n    fn fill_byte(&mut self) -> Result<Option<u8>> {\n        if self.read_pos >= self.read_fill {\n            if self.eof {\n                return Ok(None);\n            }\n -> Result<ScannerEvent> {\n        debug_assert!(\n            matches!(self.phase, Phase::Line | Phase::GiantEnd),\n            \"giant record must be drained before scanning the next record\"\n false;\n\n        loop {\n            let b = match self.fill_byte()? {\n                Some(b) => b,\n                None => break,\n            };\n            if b == b'\\n' {\n                nl = true;\n                break;\n            }\n            self.cur.push(b);\n            if self.cur.len() > self.small_limit {\n                return self.start_giant(seq);\n            }\n        }\n\n        if self.cur.is_empty() && !nl {\n            self.phase = Phase::Line;\n            return Ok(ScannerEvent::End);\n        }\n        if self.cur.last() == Some(&b'\\r') {\n seq,\n            nl,\n        }))\n    }\n\n    /// Current line crossed the small-record limit. Leftover bytes drain first.\n        let head_max = self.small_limit;\n        let cutoff = self.cur.len().min(head_max);\n        let prefix = self.cur[..cutoff].to_vec();\n        self.giant_served_leftover = false;\n        self.phase = if cutoff < self.cur.len() || !self.giant_nl {\n            Phase::GiantLeftover\n        } else {\n            Phase::GiantEnd\n        };\n        self.seq += 1;\n        Ok(ScannerEvent::Giant {\n            seq,\n            nl: false, // finalized in giant_newline() after draining\n            keys,\n            prefix,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// After draining, whether the giant record ended with a newline.\n    pub fn giant_newline(&self) -> bool {\n        self.giant_nl\n    }\n\n    fn finish_giant(&mut self, nl: bool) {\n        self.giant_nl = nl;\n        self.phase = Phase::GiantEnd;\n        self.cur.clear();\n    }\n\n    fn pull_leftover(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]) -> usize {\n        // Bytes of cur beyond the head prefix.\n        let base = self.small_limit.min(self.cur.len());\n        let remaining = &self.cur[base..];\n        let n = buf.len().min(remaining.len());\n        buf[..n].copy_from_slice(&remaining[..n]);\n        if n == remaining.len() {\n            self.giant_served_leftover = true;\n        } else {\n            // Partial serving: drop the served prefix so progress is kept.\n            self.cur.drain(0..base + n);\n            // After a partial serve the head prefix indices shift; recompute\n            // base for subsequent calls by tracking separately.\n            self.leftover_base = 0;\n        }\n        if self.giant_served_leftover {\n            if self.giant_nl {\n                // Newline already consumed before leftover; end after it.\n            }\n        }\n        n\n    }\n\n    #[doc(hidden)]\n    pub fn _noop(&self) {}\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn scan_small(data: &[u8], limit: usize) -> Vec<(Vec<u8>, u64, bool)> {\n        let mut s = LineScanner::new(Box::new(data), KeySpec::default(), limit);\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        loop {\n            match s.next().unwrap() {\n                ScannerEvent::End => break,\n                ScannerEvent::Small(r) => out.push((r.line, r.seq, r.nl)),\n                ScannerEvent::Giant { .. } => panic!(\"unexpected giant\"),\n            }\n        }\n        out\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn simple_lines() {\n        let rows = scan_small(b\"alpha\\nbeta\\r\\ngamma\\ntail\", 1024);\n        assert_eq!(rows.len(), 4);\n        assert_eq!(rows[0], (b\"alpha\".to_vec(), 0, true));\n        assert_eq!(rows[1], (b\"beta\".to_vec(), 1, true));\n        assert_eq!(rows[2], (b\"gamma\".to_vec(), 2, true));\n        assert_eq!(rows[3], (b\"tail\".to_vec(), 3, false));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_and_blank() {\n        assert!(scan_small(b\"\", 1024).is_empty());\n        let one = scan_small(b\"\\n\", 1024);\n        assert_eq!(one.len(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(one[0].0, b\"\");\n        let two = scan_small(b\"a\\n\\n\", 1024);\n        assert_eq!(two.len(), 2);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn whole_line_giant_errors() {\n        let mut s = LineScanner::new(Box::new(vec![0u8; Reading uses a small internal buffer whose size is included in the declared\n//! memory budget (see [`crate::budget`]).\n\nuse std::io;\n\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse (counted toward the memory budget).\npub const READ_BUFFER: usize = 16 * 1024;\n\n/// A record that fits inside the memory window.\npub struct SmallRecord {\n    pub line: Vec<u8>,\n    pub seq: read_fill: 0,\n            eof: false,\n            small_limit,\n            spec,\n            cur: Vec::new(),\n            seq: 0,\n            phase: Phase::Line,\n            giant_nl: false,\n &self.spec\n    }\n\n    fn fill_byte(&mut self) -> Result<Option<u8>> {\n        if self.read_pos >= self.read_fill {\n            if self.eof {\n                return Ok(None);\n            }\n -> Result<ScannerEvent> {\n        debug_assert!(\n            matches!(self.phase, Phase::Line | Phase::GiantEnd),\n            \"giant record must be drained before scanning the next record\"\n = true;\n                break;\n            }\n            self.cur.push(b);\n            if self.cur.len() > self.small_limit {\n                return self.start_giant(seq);\n            }\n        }\n\n        if self.cur.is_empty() && !nl {\n            self.phase = Phase::Line;\n            return Ok(ScannerEvent::End);\n        }\n        if self.cur.last() == Some(&b'\\r') {\n seq,\n            nl,\n        }))\n    }\n\n    /// Current line crossed the small-record limit. end after it.\n            }\n        }\n        n\n    }\n\n    #[doc(hidden)]\n    pub fn _noop(&self) {}\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn scan_small(data: &[u8], limit: usize) -> Vec<(Vec<u8>, u64, bool)> {\n        let mut s = LineScanner::new(Box::new(data), KeySpec::default(), limit);\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        loop {\n            match s.next().unwrap() {\n                ScannerEvent::End => break,\n                ScannerEvent::Small(r) => out.push((r.line, r.seq, r.nl)),\n                ScannerEvent::Giant { .. } => panic!(\"unexpected giant\"),\n            }\n        }\n        out\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn simple_lines() {\n        let rows = scan_small(b\"alpha\\nbeta\\r\\ngamma\\ntail\", 1024);\n        assert_eq!(rows.len(), 4);\n        assert_eq!(rows[0], (b\"alpha\".to_vec(), 0, true));\n        assert_eq!(rows[1], (b\"beta\".to_vec(), 1, true));\n        assert_eq!(rows[2], (b\"gamma\".to_vec(), 2, true));\n        assert_eq!(rows[3], (b\"tail\".to_vec(), 3, false));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_and_blank() {\n        assert!(scan_small(b\"\", 1024).is_empty());\n        let one = scan_small(b\"\\n\", 1024);\n        assert_eq!(one.len(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(one[0].0, b\"\");\n        let two = scan_small(b\"a\\n\\n\", 1024);\n        assert_eq!(two.len(), 2);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn whole_line_giant_errors() {\n        let mut s = LineScanner::new(Box::new(vec![0u8; {"parentUuid":"d927f205-d63f-4d00-ad48-0822ea70c8a0","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_kmo2r8wmciog64xc06ilm5uw","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp2/a/src/scanner.rs","content":"//! Bounded-memory input scanner.\n//!\n//! Records are lines separated by `\\n`; a `\\r` immediately before `\\n` is a\n//! terminator and stripped (CRLF). At most `small_limit` bytes of any line are\n//! retained.\n//!\n//! * Short lines are returned owned as [`ScannerEvent::Small`].\n//! * A line that reaches the limit becomes a [`ScannerEvent::Giant`]: its key\n//!   is resolved from a bounded prefix (or bounded prefix + a one-byte\n//!   lookahead) and the caller streams the remainder through the scanner's\n//!   [`GiantDrain`] impl straight into a run writer.\n//!\n//! Output convention (shared with the in-memory reference): every emitted\n//! record is followed by `\\n`, even the last — so no per-record newline flag is\n//! persisted in runs.\n\nuse std::io;\n\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::key::{prefix_has_key, KeySpec};\nuse crate::sortfile::{GiantDrain, Pull};\n\n/// Input stream the scanner reads from.\npub type Input = Box<dyn io::Read + Send>;\n\n/// Internal read buffer (counted toward the memory budget).\npub const READ_BUFFER: usize = 16 * 1024;\n\n/// A record that fits inside the memory window.\npub struct SmallRecord {\n    pub line: Vec<u8>,\n    pub seq: u64,\n}\n\n/// Event yielded per input record.\npub enum ScannerEvent {\n    Small(SmallRecord),\n    /// Drain this giant record via the [`GiantDrain`] impl before `next`.\n    Giant {\n        seq: u64,\n        keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n        /// Bounded head value (the line prefix).\n        prefix: Vec<u8>,\n    },\n    End,\n}\n\nenum Phase {\n    Line,\n    /// A giant drain is in flight.\n    Giant,\n}\n\npub struct LineScanner {\n    input: Input,\n    readbuf: Vec<u8>,\n    read_pos: usize,\n    read_fill: usize,\n    eof: bool,\n\n    small_limit: usize,\n    spec: KeySpec,\n\n    cur: Vec<u8>,\n    seq: u64,\n    phase: Phase,\n\n    // Giant drain state.\n    look: Option<u8>,\n    pending_cr: bool,\n    giant_active: bool,\n}\n\nimpl LineScanner {\n    pub fn new(input: Input, spec: KeySpec, small_limit: usize) -> Self {\n        LineScanner {\n            input,\n            readbuf: vec![0u8; READ_BUFFER],\n            read_pos: 0,\n            read_fill: 0,\n            eof: false,\n            small_limit,\n            spec,\n            cur: Vec::new(),\n            seq: 0,\n            phase: Phase::Line,\n            look: None,\n            pending_cr: false,\n            giant_active: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn seq(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.seq\n    }\n    pub fn spec(&self) -> &KeySpec {\n        &self.spec\n    }\n\n    fn fill_byte(&mut self) -> Result<Option<u8>> {\n        if self.read_pos >= self.read_fill {\n            if self.eof {\n                return Ok(None);\n            }\n            let n = self.input.read(&mut self.readbuf)?;\n            if n == 0 {\n                self.eof = true;\n                return Ok(None);\n            }\n            self.read_pos = 0;\n            self.read_fill = n;\n        }\n        let b = self.readbuf[self.read_pos];\n        self.read_pos += 1;\n        Ok(Some(b))\n    }\n\n    /// Scan the next record.\n    pub fn next(&mut self) -> Result<ScannerEvent> {\n        debug_assert!(!self.giant_active, \"giant record not fully drained\");\n        self.cur.clear();\n        self.look = None;\n        self.pending_cr = false;\n        let seq = self.seq;\n        let mut nl = false;\n\n        loop {\n            let b = match self.fill_byte()? {\n                Some(b) => b,\n                None => break,\n            };\n            if b == b'\\n' {\n                nl = true;\n                break;\n            }\n            if self.cur.len() == self.small_limit {\n                // `b` is the one byte that would cross the limit: use it as\n                // lookahead while deciding whether the key is already known.\n                return self.start_giant(seq, b);\n            }\n            self.cur.push(b);\n        }\n\n        if self.cur.is_empty() && !nl {\n            return Ok(ScannerEvent::End);\n        }\n        // CRLF: strip the CR only when the line ended at a newline.\n        if nl && self.cur.last() == Some(&b'\\r') {\n            self.cur.pop();\n        }\n        self.seq += 1;\n        Ok(ScannerEvent::Small(SmallRecord {\n            line: std::mem::take(&mut self.cur),\n            seq,\n        }))\n    }\n\n    /// The line reached `small_limit` bytes; `look` is the next raw byte.\n    /// Resolve the key from a bounded prefix and arm giant streaming.\n    fn start_giant(&mut self, seq: u64, look: u8) -> Result<ScannerEvent> {\n        if crate::key::key_needs_whole_line(&self.spec) {\n            return Err(Error::KeyTooLarge {\n                seq,\n                needed: self.small_limit + 1,\n                budget: self.small_limit as u64,\n            });\n        }\n        // Key already resolvable from the prefix?\n        let key_known = prefix_has_key(&self.spec, &self.cur);\n        if !key_known {\n            if look == b'\\n' {\n                // Line ends: requested columns past EOL are empty, key is known.\n            } else {\n                // Use the lookahead only to test key resolution; never retain\n                // it in the prefix (it becomes the first drained byte).\n                let mut probe = Vec::with_capacity(self.cur.len() + 1);\n                probe.extend_from_slice(&self.cur);\n                probe.push(look);\n                if !prefix_has_key(&self.spec, &probe) {\n                    return Err(Error::KeyTooLarge {\n                        seq,\n                        needed: self.small_limit + 1,\n                        budget: self.small_limit as u64,\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        let keys = self\n            .spec\n            .extract(&self.cur)\n            .into_iter()\n            .map(|k| k.to_vec())\n            .collect();\n        let prefix = std::mem::take(&mut self.cur);\n        self.look = Some(look);\n        self.pending_cr = false;\n        self.giant_active = true;\n        self.phase = Phase::Giant;\n        self.seq += 1;\n        Ok(ScannerEvent::Giant {\n            seq,\n            keys,\n            prefix,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n/// Streaming source for one giant record. The first drained byte may be the\n/// lookahead; CRLF CRs are withheld by one byte so they can be dropped if a\n/// newline follows.\nimpl GiantDrain for LineScanner {\n    fn pull(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<Pull> {\n        debug_assert!(self.giant_active);\n        if buf.is_empty() {\n            return Ok(Pull {\n                bytes: 0,\n                end_of_record: false,\n            });\n        }\n        let mut n = 0usize;\n        let mut ended = false;\n        // Byte already fetched but not yet served (lookahead or a byte that\n        // didn't fit after flushing a delayed CR).\n        let mut pushed: Option<u8> = self.look.take();\n\n        while n < buf.len() {\n            let raw = match pushed.take() {\n                Some(b) => Some(b),\n                None => self.fill_byte()?,\n            };\n            let Some(b) = raw else {\n                // EOF ends the record (no trailing newline); flush a final CR.\n                if self.pending_cr && n < buf.len() {\n                    buf[n] = b'\\r';\n                    n += 1;\n                    self.pending_cr = false;\n                }\n                ended = true;\n                break;\n            };\n            if b == b'\\n' {\n                // Drop any withheld CR: CRLF terminator.\n                self.pending_cr = false;\n                ended = true;\n                break;\n            }\n            if self.pending_cr {\n                if n < buf.len() {\n                    buf[n] = b'\\r';\n                    n += 1;\n                    self.pending_cr = false;\n                } else {\n                    // No room for the CR: put b back and retry next call.\n                    self.look = Some(b);\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n            if b == b'\\r' {\n                self.pending_cr = true;\n                continue;\n            }\n            if n < buf.len() {\n                buf[n] = b;\n                n += 1;\n            } else {\n                self.look = Some(b);\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n        if ended {\n            self.giant_active = false;\n            self.phase = Phase::Line;\n        }\n        Ok(Pull {\n            bytes: n,\n            end_of_record: ended,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn scan_small(data: &[u8], limit: usize) -> Vec<(Vec<u8>, u64)> {\n        let mut s = LineScanner::new(Box::new(data), KeySpec::default(), limit);\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        loop {\n            match s.next().unwrap() {\n                ScannerEvent::End => break,\n                ScannerEvent::Small(r) => out.push((r.line, r.seq)),\n                ScannerEvent::Giant { .. } => panic!(\"unexpected giant\"),\n            }\n        }\n        out\n    }\n\n    fn drain_giant(s: &mut LineScanner) -> Vec<u8> {\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        let mut buf = [0u8; 7]; // awkward size stresses boundaries\n        loop {\n            let p = s.pull(&mut buf).unwrap();\n            out.extend_from_slice(&buf[..p.bytes]);\n            if p.end_of_record {\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n        out\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn simple_lines() {\n        let rows = scan_small(b\"alpha\\nbeta\\r\\ngamma\\ntail\", 1024);\n        assert_eq!(rows.len(), 4);\n        assert_eq!(rows[0], (b\"alpha\".to_vec(), 0));\n        assert_eq!(rows[1], (b\"beta\".to_vec(), 1));\n        assert_eq!(rows[2], (b\"gamma\".to_vec(), 2));\n        assert_eq!(rows[3], (b\"tail\".to_vec(), 3));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_and_blank() {\n        assert!(scan_small(b\"\", 1024).is_empty());\n        assert_eq!(scan_small(b\"\\n\", 1024).len(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(scan_small(b\"a\\n\\n\", 1024).len(), 2);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn whole_line_giant_errors() {\n        let mut s = LineScanner::new(Box::new(vec![0u8; 100]), KeySpec::default(), 16);\n        assert!(matches!(s.next().unwrap_err(), Error::KeyTooLarge { .. }));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn giant_streaming_with_columns() {\n        // key = column 2; line = \"aa,BBBBBB...,cc\" where col2 is long.\n        let mut body = b\"aa,\".to_vec();\n        body.extend(std::iter::repeat(b'B').take(50));\n        body.push(b',');\n
