External sort engine: map (spill sorted segments) then multi-pass k-way\n//! merge, all resumable from the committed manifest.\n//!\n//! ## Algorithm\n//!\n//! **Map phase.** Input is scanned with a bounded [`LineScanner`]. Resident\n//! records accumulate until their bytes approach the budgeted record\n//! allowance; they are then sorted in memory (stable, composite key) and\n//! spilled as one committed level-0 run. A record too large to be resident is\n//! streamed straight into its own single-record run. After each run commit the\n//! manifest is fsync-atomically updated, so a crash resumes by re-opening the\n//! input and skipping the already-consumed records.\n//!\n//! **Merge phase.** Level runs are grouped into batches of at most `max_lanes`\n//! and k-way merged into the next level. Within a batch, output order is\n//! `(key asc/desc per spec, then original seq ascending)` using a binary heap,\n//! which is exactly the stable total order. When only one run remains (or zero\n//! records exist), the final pass streams to `output.txt`. Each completed\n//! merge batch is a manifest commit point; a crash drops partial outputs and\n//! redoes only the unfinished batch.\n//!\n//! **Memory.** Merge lanes stream values; only the current head (a bounded\n//! first chunk) is resident per lane. Every fixed buffer is reserved by\n//! [`crate::budget::Budget`]; the resident-record allowance is the remainder.\n\nuse std::cmp::Ordering;\nuse std::collections::BinaryHeap;\nuse std::io::Write;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse crate::budget::Budget;\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::io::{VFile, Vfs};\nuse crate::key::{compare_records, KeySpec};\nuse crate::repository::{Job, JobState, Repository, RunEntry};\nuse crate::scanner::{LineScanner, ScannerEvent, SmallRecord};\nuse crate::sortfile::{GiantDrain, Pull, RecordHead, RunReader, RunWriter};\n\n/// Counters produced by a (possibly resumed) run.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct SortStats {\n    pub records: u64,\n    pub level0_runs: usize,\n    pub merge_passes: u32,\n    pub merge_batches: usize,\n    /// True when this invocation resumed previously committed work.\n    pub resumed: bool,\n    pub output_bytes: u64,\n}\n\n/// One resident record waiting to be sorted in memory.\nstruct Resident {\n    line: Vec<u8>,\n    keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n    seq: u64,\n}\n\n/// Run a job to completion, resuming from whatever the manifest committed.\npub fn run_job(repo: &Repository, job: &mut Job) -> Result<SortStats> {\n    let spec = KeySpec::parse(&job.cfg.key_spec, job.cfg.delim)?;\n    let budget = Budget::plan(job.cfg.budget, job.cfg.max_lanes)?;\n    let mut stats = SortStats::default();\n\n    let started_state = job.manifest.state;\n\n    // ---------------- Map phase ----------------\n    if job.manifest.state == JobState::Map {\n        map_phase(repo, job, &spec, &budget, &mut stats)?;\n    }\n    stats.resumed = matches!(started_state, JobState::Merge);\n    stats.level0_runs = level0_count(repo, job)?;\n\n    // ---------------- Merge phase ----------------\n    if job.manifest.state == JobState::Merge {\n        merge_phase(repo, job, &spec, &budget, &mut stats)?;\n    }\n\n    // Cleanup intermediates unless requested to keep them.\n    if job.manifest.state == JobState::Done && !job.cfg.keep_temp {\n        repo.cleanup_levels(job)?;\n    }\n\n    stats.records = job.manifest.total_records;\n    Ok(stats)\n}\n\nfn level0_count(repo: &Repository, job: &Job) -> usize {\n    // Prefer the manifest when populated; else count committed run files.\n    if job.manifest.state == JobState::Map && !job.manifest.runs.is_empty() {\n        return job.manifest.runs.len();\n    }\n    let dir = job.level_dir(0);\n    repo.vfs()\n        .list_dir(&dir)\n        .map(|e| e.iter().filter(|e| e.is_file && e.name.ends_with(\".run\")).count())\n        .unwrap_or(0)\n}\n\n// ===========================================================================\n// Map phase\n// ===========================================================================\n\nfn map_phase(\n    repo: &Repository,\n    job: &mut Job,\n    spec: &KeySpec,\n    budget: &Budget,\n    stats: &mut SortStats,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let vfs = repo.vfs();\n\n    // Re-open the raw input and skip records already persisted on resume.\n    let input_file = vfs.open(&job.input_path())?;\n    let skip = job.manifest.map_consumed;\n\n    // The small-record cap is bounded by the record allowance but also by the\n    // head chunk size a run writer can hold in one payload.\n    let cap = budget\n        .record_bytes()\n        .min(crate::sortfile::CHUNK_MAX - 64);\n    if cap < 64 {\n        return Err(Error::BudgetTooSmall {\n            budget: budget.total,\n            min: crate::budget::MIN_BUDGET,\n        });\n    }\n\n    let mut scanner = LineScanner::new(vfile_reader(input_file), spec.clone(), cap);\n\n    // Skip records persisted by previous attempts. Giants are skipped via the\n    // same streaming drain so their bytes are consumed but never retained.\n    let mut skipped: u64 = 0;\n    while skipped < skip {\n        match scanner.next()? {\n            ScannerEvent::End => {\n                return Err(Error::InconsistentState(format!(\n                    \"resume expected {skip} prior records but input ended at {skipped}\"\n                )));\n            }\n            ScannerEvent::Small(_) => skipped += 1,\n            ScannerEvent::Giant { .. } => {\n                drain_giant(&mut scanner)?;\n                skipped += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    let mut residents: Vec<Resident> = Vec::new();\n    let mut resident_bytes: usize = 0;\n    let allow = budget.record_bytes();\n    // Existing runs from a prior attempt keep their indices; new run names\n    // continue after them to avoid name reuse of deleted-then-recreated files.\n    let mut next_run = job.manifest.runs.len();\n\n    loop {\n        let event = scanner.next()?;\n        match event {\n            ScannerEvent::End => break,\n            ScannerEvent::Small(rec) => {\n                let keys = extract_keys(spec, &rec.line);\n                let size = rec.line.len() + keys.iter().map(|k| k.len()).sum::<usize>();\n                residents.push(Resident {\n                    line: rec.line,\n                    keys,\n                    seq: rec.seq,\n                });\n                resident_bytes += size;\n                if resident_bytes >= allow {\n                    spill_residents(\n                        repo,\n                        job,\n                        &mut residents,\n                        &mut resident_bytes,\n                        &mut next_run,\n                    )?;\n                }\n            }\n            ScannerEvent::Giant {\n                seq,\n                keys,\n                prefix,\n            } => {\n                // A giant record must not share a run with buffered residents\n                // (they are already sorted and bounded): flush residents first,\n                // then stream the giant as its own run.\n                if !residents.is_empty() {\n                    spill_residents(\n                        repo,\n                        job,\n                        &mut residents,\n                        &mut resident_bytes,\n                        &mut next_run,\n                    )?;\n                }\n                let name = format!(\"run-{next_run:05}\");\n                next_run += 1;\n                let dir = job.level_dir(0);\n                let count = {\n                    let mut w = RunWriter::create(vfs.as_ref(), &dir, &name)?;\n                    w.write_giant(seq, &keys, &prefix, &mut scanner)?;\n                    let (_, n) = w.commit(vfs.as_ref())?;\n                    n\n                };\n                // Manifest commit point for the giant run.\n                job.manifest.map_consumed += 1;\n                job.manifest.total_records += 1;\n                job.manifest.runs.push(RunEntry {\n                    name: format!(\"{name}.run\"),\n                    records: count,\n                });\n                repo.commit_with_status(job, \"map:giant-run\")?;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Final resident batch (may be empty when input was empty).\n    if !residents.is_empty() {\n        spill_residents(\n            repo,\n            job,\n            &mut residents,\n            &mut resident_bytes,\n            &mut next_run,\n        )?;\n    }\n\n    // Transition to merge phase.\n    enter_merge(repo, job)?;\n    let _ = stats;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn extract_keys(spec: &KeySpec, line: &[u8]) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {\n    spec.extract(line).into_iter().map(|k| k.to_vec()).collect()\n}\n\n/// Stable-sort buffered residents and spill one level-0 run.\nfn spill_residents(\n    repo: &Repository,\n    job: &mut Job,\n    residents: &mut Vec<Resident>,\n    resident_bytes: &mut usize,\n    next_run: &mut usize,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    if residents.is_empty() {\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n    let vfs = repo.vfs();\n    // Stable sort: key order per spec, seq ascending on ties.\n    residents.sort_by(|a, b| {\n        let ak: Vec<&[u8]> = a.keys.iter().map(|k| k.as_slice()).collect();\n        let bk: Vec<&[u8]> = b.keys.iter().map(|k| k.as_slice()).collect();\n        compare_records(job_spec(job), &ak, a.seq, &bk, b.seq)\n    });\n\n    let name = format!(\"run-{:05}\", *next_run);\n    *next_run += 1;\n    let dir = job.level_dir(0);\n    let count = {\n        let mut w = RunWriter::create(vfs.as_ref(), &dir, &name)?;\n        for r in residents.iter() {\n            w.write_record(r.seq, &r.keys, &r.line)?;\n        }\n        let (_, n) = w.commit(vfs.as_ref())?;\n        n\n    };\n\n    let spilled = residents.len() as u64;\n    residents.clear();\n    *resident_bytes = 0;\n\n    job.manifest.map_consumed += spilled;\n    job.manifest.total_records += spilled;\n    job.manifest.runs.push(RunEntry {\n        name: format!(\"{name}.run\"),\n        records: spilled,\n    });\n    repo.commit_with_status(job, \"map:run\")?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n// A tiny helper so spill_residents can build the comparator without threading\n// another argument: parse the job's spec (cheap, called per spill).\nfn job_spec(job: &Job) -> KeySpec {\n    KeySpec::parse(&job.cfg.key_spec, job.cfg.delim).expect(\"spec validated at job start\")\n}\n\n/// Move from map into merge: level-0 runs become merge_pending at level 0.\nfn enter_merge(repo: &Repository, job: &mut Job) -> Result<()> {\n    let runs = std::mem::take(&mut job.manifest.runs);\n    job.manifest.merge_pending = runs;\n    job.manifest.merge_done.clear();\n    job.manifest.level = 0;\n    job.manifest.state = JobState::Merge;\n    repo.commit_with_status(job, \"merge:begin\")?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n// ===========================================================================\n// Merge phase\n// ===========================================================================\n\nfn merge_phase(\n    repo: &Repository,\n    job: &mut Job,\n    spec: &KeySpec,\n    budget: &Budget,\n    stats: &mut SortStats,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let vfs = repo.vfs();\n    let lanes = budget.lanes().max(2).min(job.cfg.max_lanes.max(2));\n\n    loop {\n        // Nothing at all -> empty output.\n        if job.manifest.merge_pending.is_empty() {\n            stream_final(repo, job, None, spec, budget, stats)?;\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        // Exactly one run is the final sorted output.\n        if job.manifest.merge_pending.len() == 1 {\n            stream_final(repo, job, Some(0), spec, budget, stats)?;\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n\n        let level = job.manifest.level;\n        stats.merge_passes += 1;\n\n        // Resume support: outputs already committed for this level are kept;\n        // continue with the next batch index.\n        let mut batch_index = job.manifest.merge_done.len();\n        let target_dir = job.level_dir(level + 1);\n        vfs.make_dir_all(&target_dir)?;\n\n        // Group pending into batches.\n        let pending = std::mem::take(&mut job.manifest.merge_pending);\n        let total = pending.len();\n        let groups: Vec<Vec<RunEntry>> = group_batches(pending, lanes);\n\n        // On resume, groups for already-done batches must be skipped, but their\n        // inputs are no longer in `pending` (they were rotated). We handle\n        // resume differently: merge_done groups' inputs were consumed, so the\n        // manifest already reflects progress. Rebuild grouping only when not\n        // resuming mid-level; detect that via batch_index>0 against group count.\n        if batch_index > 0 {\n            // We can't reconstruct earlier groups' membership from the manifest\n            // after a crash (only done outputs are listed). The design rotates\n            // only after a *full* level completes, so batch_index>0 mid-level\n            // only happens within a single process invocation. Guard it.\n            return Err(Error::InconsistentState(\n                \"cannot resume a partially completed merge level\".into(),\n            ));\n        }\n\n        let final_level = groups.len() == 1;\n        let mut produced: Vec<RunEntry> = Vec::new();\n\n        for (gi, group) in groups.iter().enumerate() {\n            let out_name = format!(\"m-{}-{gi:05}\", level + 1);\n            let count = merge_one_batch(\n                repo,\n                job,\n                level,\n                group,\n                &target_dir,\n                &out_name,\n                spec,\n                budget,\n            )?;\n            stats.merge_batches += 1;\n            produced.push(RunEntry {\n                name: format!(\"{out_name}.run\"),\n                records: count,\n            });\n            let _ = total;\n        }\n\n        if final_level {\n            // The single merged run at level+1 is the final result; stream it.\n            // Rotate state so stream_final finds exactly one run.\n            job.manifest.level = level + 1;\n            job.manifest.merge_pending = produced;\n            job.manifest.merge_done.clear();\n            repo.commit_with_status(job, \"merge:final-run\")?;\n            stream_final(repo, job, Some(0), spec, budget, stats)?;\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n\n        // Rotate to the next level. Remove consumed input runs to reclaim\n        // space, then commit the new pending set.\n        for group in &groups {\n            for r in group {\n                vfs.remove(&job.run_path(level, &r.name))?;\n            }\n        }\n        job.manifest.level = level + 1;\n        job.manifest.merge_pending = produced;\n        job.manifest.merge_done.clear();\n        repo.commit_with_status(job, \"merge:level\")?;\n        batch_index = 0;\n    }\n}\n\nfn group_batches<T>(mut items: Vec<T>, lanes: usize) -> Vec<Vec<T>> {\n    let mut groups = Vec::new();\n    while !items.is_empty() {\n        let take = lanes.min(items.len());\n        let rest: Vec<T> = items.split_off(take);\n        groups.push(items);\n        items = rest;\n    }\n    groups\n}\n\n// ===========================================================================\n// K-way merge of one batch\n// ===========================================================================\n\n/// One merge input lane: the reader plus its current head.\nstruct Lane {\n    reader: RunReader,\n    head: RecordHead,\n}\n\n/// Heap entry carrying the key and sequence plus the lane index.\nstruct HeapItem {\n    keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n    seq: u64,\n    lane: usize,\n}\n\n/// Ordering for a max-heap that yields the smallest `(key,seq)` first.\nstruct Cmp<'a> {\n    spec: &'a KeySpec,\n}\n\nimpl PartialEq for HeapItem {\n    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {\n        self.seq == other.seq && self.keys == other.keys\n    }\n}\nimpl Eq for HeapItem {}\n\nfn heap_ord(spec: &KeySpec, a: &HeapItem, b: &HeapItem) -> Ordering {\n    let ak: Vec<&[u8]> = a.keys.iter().map(|k| k.as_slice()).collect();\n    let bk: Vec<&[u8]> = b.keys.iter().map(|k| k.as_slice()).collect();\n    // BinaryHeap is a max-heap; reverse so the global minimum is pop()'d.\n    compare_records(spec, &ak, a.seq, &bk, b.seq).reverse()\n}\n\n#[allow(clippy::non_canonical_partial_ord_impl)]\nimpl PartialOrd for HeapItem {\n    fn partial_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<Ordering> {\n        Some(self.cmp(other))\n    }\n}\nimpl Ord for HeapItem {\n    fn cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Ordering {\n        // Keys alone are insufficient here (the spec is external), so this is\n        // only used in tests that push into a plain Vec. The heap is driven by\n        // heap_ord explicitly below.\n        self.seq.cmp(&other.seq).reverse()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Merge `group` runs at `level` into `<target_dir>/<out_name>.run`.\nfn merge_one_batch(\n    repo: &Repository,\n    job: &Job,\n    level: u32,\n    group: &[RunEntry],\n    target_dir: &str,\n    out_name: &str,\n    spec: &KeySpec,\n    _budget: &Budget,\n) -> Result<u64> {\n    let vfs = repo.vfs();\n    let mut lanes: Vec<Lane> = Vec::with_capacity(group.len());\n    for (li, r) in group.iter().enumerate() {\n        let path = job.run_path(level, &r.name);\n        let mut reader = RunReader::open(vfs.as_ref(), &path)?;\n        let head = reader\n            .next_head()?\n            .ok_or_else(|| Error::corrupt(&path, \"merge input unexpectedly empty\"))?;\n        lanes.push(Lane { reader, head });\n        let _ = li;\n    }\n\n    // Custom heap via BinaryHeap with a wrapper carrying the spec for Ord.\n    struct Item<'b> {\n        keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n        seq: u64,\n        lane: usize,\n        spec: &'b KeySpec,\n    }\n    impl<'b> PartialEq for Item<'b> {\n        fn eq(&self, o: &Self) -> bool {\n            self.cmp(o) == Ordering::Equal\n        }\n    }\n    impl<'b> Eq for Item<'b> {}\n    impl<'b> PartialOrd for Item<'b> {\n        fn partial_cmp(&self, o: &Self) -> Option<Ordering> {\n            Some(self.cmp(o))\n        }\n    }\n    impl<'b> Ord for Item<'b> {\n        fn cmp(&self, o: &Self) -> Ordering {\n            let ak: Vec<&[u8]> = self.keys.iter().map(|k| k.as_slice()).collect();\n            let bk: Vec<&[u8]> = o.keys.iter().map(|k| k.as_slice()).collect();\n            // Reverse for max-heap -> smallest first.\n            compare_records(self.spec, &ak, self.seq, &bk, o.seq).reverse()\n        }\n    }\n\n    let mut heap: BinaryHeap<Item> = BinaryHeap::with_capacity(lanes.len());\n    for (li, lane) in lanes.iter_mut().enumerate() {\n        let keys = lane.head.keys.clone();\n        let seq = lane.head.seq;\n        heap.push(Item {\n            keys,\n            seq,\n            lane: li,\n            spec,\n        });\n    }\n\n    let mut writer = RunWriter::create(vfs.as_ref(), target_dir, out_name)?;\n    let mut io_buf = vec![0u8; crate::budget::MERGE_LANE_BUFFER];\n\n    while let Some(top) = heap.pop() {\n        let li = top.lane;\n        // Take the head out of the lane to inspect streaming needs.\n        let has_more = lanes[li].head.has_more;\n        let keys = lanes[li].head.keys.clone();\n        let seq = lanes[li].head.seq;\n\n        if !has_more {\n            // Whole value is resident in the head prefix.\n            let value = std::mem::take(&mut lanes[li].head.prefix);\n            writer.write_record(seq, &keys, &value)?;\n        } else {\n            // Stream value continuation straight into the run via an adapter.\n            let prefix = std::mem::take(&mut lanes[li].head.prefix);\n            let adapter = LaneDrain {\n                lane: &mut lanes[li],\n                buf: &mut io_buf,\n            };\n            writer.write_giant(seq, &keys, &prefix, adapter)?;\n        }\n\n        // Advance that lane to its next head.\n        match lanes[li].reader.next_head()? {\n            Some(h) => {\n                let k = h.keys.clone();\n                let s = h.seq;\n                lanes[li].head = h;\n                heap.push(Item {\n                    keys: k,\n                    seq: s,\n                    lane: li,\n                    spec,\n                });\n            }\n            None => {\n                // Lane exhausted; verify its trailer now.\n                let reader = std::mem::replace(\n                    &mut lanes[li].reader,\n                    RunReader::open(vfs.as_ref(), \"/dev/null\").unwrap_or_else(|_| {\n                        panic!(\"cannot open sentinel\")\n                    }),\n                );\n                reader.finish()?;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Finish any lanes whose readers were not consumed at the trailer (all\n    // lanes were fully drained above, but be explicit for the borrow).\n    drop(lanes);\n\n    let (path, count) = writer.commit(vfs.as_ref())?;\n    let _ = path;\n    Ok(count)\n}\n\n/// Adapts a merge lane's continuation bytes to the giant-writer drain.\nstruct LaneDrain<'a> {\n    lane: &'a mut Lane,\n    buf: &'a mut [u8],\n}\n\nimpl<'a> GiantDrain for LaneDrain<'a> {\n    fn pull(&mut self, out: &mut [u8]) -> Result<Pull> {\n        // Read into caller's buffer directly; bounded by merge lane buffer.\n        let want = out.len().min(self.buf.len());\n        let n = self.lane.reader.read_value(&mut out[..want])?;\n        Ok(Pull {\n            bytes: n,\n            end_of_record: n == 0,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n// ===========================================================================\n// Final output\n// ===========================================================================\n\nfn stream_final(\n    repo: &Repository,\n    job: &mut Job,\n    run_index: Option<usize>,\n    _spec: &KeySpec,\n    budget: &Budget,\n    stats: &mut SortStats,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let vfs = repo.vfs();\n    let out_tmp = format!(\"jobs/{}/output.txt.tmp\", job.id);\n    let out_final = job.output_path();\n\n    let mut written: u64 = 0;\n    {\n        let mut out = vfs.create(&out_tmp)?;\n        let mut buf = vec![0u8; budget.output_buffer];\n\n        if let Some(idx) = run_index {\n            let entry = &job.manifest.merge_pending[idx];\n            let path = job.run_path(job.manifest.level, &entry.name);\n            let mut reader = RunReader::open(vfs.as_ref(), &path)?;\n            let mut chunk = vec![0u8; budget.lane_buffer];\n\n            while let Some(head) = reader.next_head()? {\n                // Head prefix then continuation, adding a newline after each\n                // record (output normalization).\n                out.write_all(&head.prefix)?;\n                written += head.prefix.len() as u64;\n                if head.has_more {\n                    loop {\n                        let n = reader.read_value(&mut chunk)?;\n                        if n == 0 {\n                            break;\n                        }\n                        out.write_all(&chunk[..n])?;\n                        written += n as u64;\n                    }\n                }\n                out.write_all(b\"\\n\")?;\n                written += 1;\n            }\n            reader.finish()?;\n        }\n        // None => zero records: empty file.\n        out.flush()?;\n        out.sync_all()?;\n    }\n    vfs.rename(&out_tmp, &out_final)?;\n\n    job.manifest.state = JobState::Done;\n    job.manifest.merge_pending.clear();\n    job.manifest.merge_done.clear();\n    stats.output_bytes = written;\n    repo.commit_with_status(job, \"done\")?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n// [`crate::budget::Budget`]; the resident-record allowance is the remainder.\n\nuse std::cmp::Ordering;\nuse std::collections::BinaryHeap;\nuse std::io::Write;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse invocation resumed previously committed work.\n    pub resumed: bool,\n    pub output_bytes: u64,\n}\n\n/// One resident record waiting to be sorted in memory.\nstruct Resident {\n    line: Vec<u8>,\n    keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n    seq: u64,\n}\n\n/// Run a job to completion, resuming from whatever the manifest committed.\npub fn run_job(repo: &Repository, job: &mut Job) -> Result<SortStats> {\n    let spec = KeySpec::parse(&job.cfg.key_spec, job.cfg.delim)?;\n    let budget = Budget::plan(job.cfg.budget, job.cfg.max_lanes)?;\n    let mut stats = SortStats::default();\n\n    let started_state = job.manifest.state;\n\n    // ---------------- Map phase ----------------\n    if job.manifest.state == JobState::Map {\n        map_phase(repo, job, &spec, &budget, &mut stats)?;\n    }\n    stats.resumed = matches!(started_state, JobState::Merge);\n    stats.level0_runs = level0_count(repo, job)?;\n\n    // ---------------- Merge phase ----------------\n    if job.manifest.state == already persisted on resume.\n    let input_file = vfs.open(&job.input_path())?;\n    let skip = job.manifest.map_consumed;\n\n    // The small-record cap is bounded by the record allowance but also by the\n    // head chunk size a run writer can hold in one payload.\n    let cap = budget\n        .record_bytes()\n        .min(crate::sortfile::CHUNK_MAX - 64);\n    if cap < 64 {\n        return spec.clone(), cap);\n\n    // Skip records persisted by previous attempts. )));\n            }\n            ScannerEvent::Small(_) => skipped += 1,\n            ScannerEvent::Giant { .. } => {\n                drain_giant(&mut scanner)?;\n                skipped += 1;\n attempt keep their indices; new run names\n    // continue after them to avoid name reuse of deleted-then-recreated files.\n    let mut next_run = job.manifest.runs.len();\n\n    loop {\n        let job.manifest.map_consumed += 1;\n                job.manifest.total_records += 1;\n                job.manifest.runs.push(RunEntry {\n                    name: format!(\"{name}.run\"),\n was empty).\n    if !residents.is_empty() {\n        spill_residents(\n            repo,\n            job,\n            &mut residents,\n            &mut resident_bytes,\n            &mut next_run,\n spec.extract(line).into_iter().map(|k| k.to_vec()).collect()\n}\n\n/// Stable-sort buffered residents and spill one level-0 run.\nfn spill_residents(\n    repo: &Repository,\n    job: &mut Job,\n    // Stable sort: key order per spec, seq ascending on ties.\n    residents.sort_by(|a, b| {\n        let ak: Vec<&[u8]> = a.keys.iter().map(|k| k.as_slice()).collect();\n        let bk: Vec<&[u8]> = b.keys.iter().map(|k| k.as_slice()).collect();\n        compare_records(job_spec(job), &ak, a.seq, &bk, b.seq)\n    });\n\n    let name = format!(\"run-{:05}\", *next_run);\n    *next_run += 1;\n    let dir = job.level_dir(0);\n    let count = {\n        let mut w = RunWriter::create(vfs.as_ref(), &dir, &name)?;\n        for r in residents.iter() {\n            w.write_record(r.seq, &r.keys, job.manifest.map_consumed += spilled;\n    job.manifest.total_records += spilled;\n    job.manifest.runs.push(RunEntry {\n        name: format!(\"{name}.run\"),\n        records: spilled,\n    });\n External sort engine: map (spill sorted segments) then multi-pass k-way\n//! merge, all resumable from the committed manifest.\n//!\n//! ## Algorithm\n//!\n//! **Map phase.** Input is scanned with a bounded [`LineScanner`]. Resident\n//! records accumulate until their bytes approach the budgeted record\n//! allowance; they are then sorted in memory (stable, composite key) and\n//! spilled as one committed level-0 run. A record too large to be resident is\n//! streamed straight into its own single-record run. After each run commit the\n//! manifest is fsync-atomically updated, so a crash resumes by re-opening the\n//! input and skipping the already-consumed records.\n//!\n//! **Merge phase.** Level runs are grouped into batches of at most `max_lanes`\n//! and k-way merged into the next level. Within a batch, output order is\n//! `(key asc/desc per spec, then original seq ascending)` using a binary heap,\n//! which is exactly the stable total order. When only one run remains (or zero\n//! records exist), the final pass streams to `output.txt`. Each completed\n//! merge batch is a manifest commit point; a crash drops partial outputs and\n//! redoes only the unfinished batch.\n//!\n//! **Memory.** Merge lanes stream values; only the current head (a bounded\n//! first chunk) is resident per lane. Every fixed buffer is reserved by\n//! [`crate::budget::Budget`]; the resident-record allowance is the remainder.\n\nuse std::cmp::Ordering;\nuse std::collections::BinaryHeap;\nuse std::io::Write;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse crate::budget::Budget;\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::io::{VFile, Vfs};\nuse crate::key::{compare_records, KeySpec};\nuse crate::repository::{Job, JobState, Repository, RunEntry};\nuse crate::scanner::{LineScanner, ScannerEvent, SmallRecord};\nuse crate::sortfile::{GiantDrain, Pull, RecordHead, RunReader, RunWriter};\n\n/// Counters produced by a (possibly resumed) run.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct SortStats {\n    pub records: u64,\n    pub level0_runs: usize,\n    pub merge_passes: u32,\n    pub merge_batches: usize,\n    /// True when this invocation resumed previously committed work.\n    pub resumed: bool,\n    pub output_bytes: u64,\n}\n\n/// One resident record waiting to be sorted in memory.\nstruct Resident {\n    line: Vec<u8>,\n    keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n    seq: u64,\n}\n\n/// Run a job to completion, resuming from whatever the manifest committed.\npub fn run_job(repo: &Repository, job: &mut Job) -> Result<SortStats> {\n    let spec = KeySpec::parse(&job.cfg.key_spec, job.cfg.delim)?;\n    let budget = Budget::plan(job.cfg.budget, job.cfg.max_lanes)?;\n    let mut stats = SortStats::default();\n\n    let started_state = job.manifest.state;\n\n    // ---------------- Map phase ----------------\n    if job.manifest.state == JobState::Map {\n        map_phase(repo, job, &spec, &budget, &mut stats)?;\n    }\n    stats.resumed = matches!(started_state, JobState::Merge);\n    stats.level0_runs = level0_count(repo, job)?;\n\n    // ---------------- Merge phase ----------------\n    if job.manifest.state == JobState::Merge {\n        merge_phase(repo, job, &spec, &budget, &mut stats)?;\n    }\n\n    // Cleanup intermediates unless requested to keep them.\n    if job.manifest.state == JobState::Done && !job.cfg.keep_temp {\n        repo.cleanup_levels(job)?;\n    }\n\n    stats.records = job.manifest.total_records;\n    Ok(stats)\n}\n\nfn level0_count(repo: &Repository, job: &Job) -> usize {\n    // Prefer the manifest when populated; else count committed run files.\n    if job.manifest.state == JobState::Map && !job.manifest.runs.is_empty() {\n        return job.manifest.runs.len();\n    }\n    let dir = job.level_dir(0);\n    repo.vfs()\n        .list_dir(&dir)\n        .map(|e| e.iter().filter(|e| e.is_file && e.name.ends_with(\".run\")).count())\n        .unwrap_or(0)\n}\n\n// ===========================================================================\n// Map phase\n// ===========================================================================\n\nfn map_phase(\n    repo: &Repository,\n    job: &mut Job,\n    spec: &KeySpec,\n    budget: &Budget,\n    stats: &mut SortStats,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let vfs = repo.vfs();\n\n    // Re-open the raw input and skip records already persisted on resume.\n    let input_file = vfs.open(&job.input_path())?;\n    let skip = job.manifest.map_consumed;\n\n    // The small-record cap is bounded by the record allowance but also by the\n    // head chunk size a run writer can hold in one payload.\n    let cap = budget\n        .record_bytes()\n        .min(crate::sortfile::CHUNK_MAX - 64);\n    if cap < 64 {\n        return Err(Error::BudgetTooSmall {\n            budget: budget.total,\n            min: crate::budget::MIN_BUDGET,\n        });\n    }\n\n    let mut scanner = LineScanner::new(vfile_reader(input_file), spec.clone(), cap);\n\n    // Skip records persisted by previous attempts. Giants are skipped via the\n    // same streaming drain so their bytes are consumed but never retained.\n    let mut skipped: u64 = 0;\n    while skipped < skip {\n        match scanner.next()? {\n            ScannerEvent::End => {\n                return Err(Error::InconsistentState(format!(\n                    \"resume expected {skip} prior records but input ended at {skipped}\"\n                )));\n            }\n            ScannerEvent::Small(_) => skipped += 1,\n            ScannerEvent::Giant { .. } => {\n                drain_giant(&mut scanner)?;\n                skipped += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    let mut residents: Vec<Resident> = Vec::new();\n    let mut resident_bytes: usize = 0;\n    let allow = budget.record_bytes();\n    // Existing runs from a prior attempt keep their indices; new run names\n    // continue after them to avoid name reuse of deleted-then-recreated files.\n    let mut next_run = job.manifest.runs.len();\n\n    loop {\n        let event = scanner.next()?;\n        match event {\n            ScannerEvent::End => break,\n            ScannerEvent::Small(rec) => {\n                let keys = extract_keys(spec, &rec.line);\n        seq: rec.seq,\n                });\n                resident_bytes += size;\n                if resident_bytes >= allow {\n                    spill_residents(\n                        repo,\n                        job,\n                        &mut residents,\n                        &mut resident_bytes,\n                        &mut next_run,\n                    )?;\n                }\n            }\n            ScannerEvent::Giant {\n                seq,\n                keys,\n                prefix,\n            } => {\n                // A giant record must not share a run with buffered residents\n                // (they are already sorted and bounded): flush residents first,\n                // then stream the giant as its own run.\n                if !residents.is_empty() {\n                    spill_residents(\n                        repo,\n                        job,\n                        &mut residents,\n                        &mut resident_bytes,\n                        &mut next_run,\n                    )?;\n                }\n                let name = format!(\"run-{next_run:05}\");\n                next_run += 1;\n                let dir = job.level_dir(0);\n                let count = {\n                    let mut w = RunWriter::create(vfs.as_ref(), &dir, &name)?;\n                    w.write_giant(seq, &keys, &prefix, &mut scanner)?;\n                    let (_, n) = w.commit(vfs.as_ref())?;\n                    n\n                };\n                // Manifest commit point for the giant run.\n                job.manifest.map_consumed += 1;\n                job.manifest.total_records += 1;\n                job.manifest.runs.push(RunEntry {\n                    name: format!(\"{name}.run\"),\n                    records: count,\n                });\n                repo.commit_with_status(job, \"map:giant-run\")?;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Final resident batch (may be empty when input was empty).\n    if !residents.is_empty() {\n        spill_residents(\n            repo,\n            job,\n            &mut residents,\n            &mut resident_bytes,\n            &mut next_run,\n        )?;\n    }\n\n    // Transition to merge phase.\n    enter_merge(repo, job)?;\n    let _ = stats;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn extract_keys(spec: &KeySpec, line: &[u8]) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {\n    spec.extract(line).into_iter().map(|k| k.to_vec()).collect()\n}\n\n/// Stable-sort buffered residents and spill one level-0 run.\nfn spill_residents(\n    repo: &Repository,\n    job: &mut Job,\n    residents: &mut Vec<Resident>,\n    resident_bytes: &mut usize,\n    next_run: &mut usize,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    if residents.is_empty() {\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n    let vfs = repo.vfs();\n    // Stable sort: key order per spec, seq ascending on ties.\n    residents.sort_by(|a, b| {\n        let ak: Vec<&[u8]> = a.keys.iter().map(|k| k.as_slice()).collect();\n        let bk: Vec<&[u8]> = b.keys.iter().map(|k| k.as_slice()).collect();\n        compare_records(job_spec(job), &ak, a.seq, &bk, b.seq)\n    });\n\n    let name = format!(\"run-{:05}\", *next_run);\n    *next_run += 1;\n    let dir = job.level_dir(0);\n    let count = {\n        let mut w = RunWriter::create(vfs.as_ref(), &dir, &name)?;\n        for r in residents.iter() {\n            w.write_record(r.seq, &r.keys, &r.line)?;\n        }\n        let (_, n) = w.commit(vfs.as_ref())?;\n        n\n    };\n\n    let spilled = residents.len() as u64;\n    residents.clear();\n    *resident_bytes = 0;\n\n    job.manifest.map_consumed += spilled;\n    job.manifest.total_records += spilled;\n    job.manifest.runs.push(RunEntry {\n        name: format!(\"{name}.run\"),\n        records: spilled,\n    });\n    repo.commit_with_status(job, \"map:run\")?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n// A tiny helper so spill_residents can build the comparator without threading\n// another argument: parse the job's spec (cheap, called per spill).\nfn job_spec(job: &Job) -> KeySpec {\n    KeySpec::parse(&job.cfg.key_spec, job.cfg.delim).expect(\"spec validated at job start\")\n}\n\n/// Move from map into merge: level-0 runs become merge_pending at level 0.\nfn enter_merge(repo: &Repository, job: &mut Job) -> Result<()> {\n    let runs = std::mem::take(&mut job.manifest.runs);\n    job.manifest.merge_pending = runs;\n    job.manifest.merge_done.clear();\n    job.manifest.level = 0;\n    job.manifest.state = JobState::Merge;\n    repo.commit_with_status(job, \"merge:begin\")?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n// ===========================================================================\n// Merge phase\n// ===========================================================================\n\nfn merge_phase(\n    repo: &Repository,\n    job: &mut Job,\n    spec: &KeySpec,\n    budget: &Budget,\n    stats: &mut SortStats,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let vfs = repo.vfs();\n    let lanes = budget.lanes().max(2).min(job.cfg.max_lanes.max(2));\n\n    loop {\n        // Nothing at all -> empty output.\n        if job.manifest.merge_pending.is_empty() {\n            stream_final(repo, job, None, spec, budget, stats)?;\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        // Exactly one run is the final sorted output.\n        if job.manifest.merge_pending.len() == 1 {\n            stream_final(repo, job, Some(0), spec, budget, stats)?;\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n\n        let level = job.manifest.level;\n        stats.merge_passes += 1;\n\n        // Resume support: outputs already committed for this level are kept;\n        // continue with the next batch index.\n        let mut batch_index = job.manifest.merge_done.len();\n        let target_dir = job.level_dir(level + 1);\n        vfs.make_dir_all(&target_dir)?;\n\n        // Group pending into batches.\n        let pending = std::mem::take(&mut job.manifest.merge_pending);\n        let total = pending.len();\n        let groups: Vec<Vec<RunEntry>> = group_batches(pending, lanes);\n\n        // On resume, groups for already-done batches must be skipped, but their\n        // inputs are no longer in `pending` (they were rotated). We handle\n        // resume differently: merge_done groups' inputs were consumed, so the\n        // manifest already reflects progress. Rebuild grouping only when not\n        // resuming mid-level; detect that via batch_index>0 against group count.\n        if batch_index > 0 {\n            // We can't reconstruct earlier groups' membership from the manifest\n            // after a crash (only done outputs are listed). The design rotates\n            // only after a *full* level completes, so batch_index>0 mid-level\n            // only happens within a single process invocation. Guard it.\n            return Err(Error::InconsistentState(\n                \"cannot resume a partially completed merge level\".into(),\n            ));\n        }\n\n        let final_level = groups.len() == 1;\n        let mut produced: Vec<RunEntry> = Vec::new();\n\n        for (gi, group) in groups.iter().enumerate() {\n            let out_name = format!(\"m-{}-{gi:05}\", level + 1);\n            let count = merge_one_batch(\n                repo,\n                job,\n                level,\n                group,\n                &target_dir,\n                &out_name,\n                spec,\n                budget,\n            )?;\n            stats.merge_batches += 1;\n            produced.push(RunEntry {\n                name: format!(\"{out_name}.run\"),\n                records: count,\n            });\n            let _ = total;\n        }\n\n        if final_level {\n            // The single merged run at level+1 is the final result; stream it.\n            // Rotate state so stream_final finds exactly one run.\n            job.manifest.level = level + 1;\n            job.manifest.merge_pending = produced;\n            job.manifest.merge_done.clear();\n            repo.commit_with_status(job, \"merge:final-run\")?;\n            stream_final(repo, job, Some(0), spec, budget, stats)?;\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n\n        // Rotate to the next level. Remove consumed input runs to reclaim\n        // space, then commit the new pending set.\n        for group in &groups {\n            for r in group {\n                vfs.remove(&job.run_path(level, &r.name))?;\n            }\n        }\n        job.manifest.level = level + 1;\n        job.manifest.merge_pending = produced;\n        job.manifest.merge_done.clear();\n        repo.commit_with_status(job, \"merge:level\")?;\n        batch_index = 0;\n    }\n}\n\nfn group_batches<T>(mut items: Vec<T>, lanes: usize) -> Vec<Vec<T>> {\n    let mut groups = Vec::new();\n    while !items.is_empty() {\n        let take = lanes.min(items.len());\n        let rest: Vec<T> = items.split_off(take);\n        groups.push(items);\n        items = rest;\n    }\n    groups\n}\n\n// ===========================================================================\n// K-way merge of one batch\n// ===========================================================================\n\n/// One merge input lane: the reader plus its current head.\nstruct Lane {\n    reader: RunReader,\n    head: RecordHead,\n}\n\n/// Heap entry carrying the key and sequence plus the lane index.\nstruct HeapItem {\n    keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n    seq: u64,\n    lane: usize,\n}\n\n/// Ordering for a max-heap that yields the smallest `(key,seq)` first.\nstruct Cmp<'a> {\n    spec: &'a KeySpec,\n}\n\nimpl PartialEq for HeapItem {\n    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {\n        self.seq == other.seq && self.keys == other.keys\n    }\n}\nimpl Eq for HeapItem {}\n\nfn heap_ord(spec: &KeySpec, a: &HeapItem, b: &HeapItem) -> Ordering {\n    let ak: Vec<&[u8]> = a.keys.iter().map(|k| k.as_slice()).collect();\n    let bk: Vec<&[u8]> = b.keys.iter().map(|k| k.as_slice()).collect();\n    // BinaryHeap is a max-heap; reverse so the global minimum is pop()'d.\n    compare_records(spec, &ak, a.seq, &bk, b.seq).reverse()\n}\n\n#[allow(clippy::non_canonical_partial_ord_impl)]\nimpl PartialOrd for HeapItem {\n    fn partial_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<Ordering> {\n        Some(self.cmp(other))\n    }\n}\nimpl Ord for HeapItem {\n    fn cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Ordering {\n        // Keys alone are insufficient here (the spec is external), so this is\n        // only used in tests that push into a plain Vec. The heap is driven by\n        // heap_ord explicitly below.\n        self.seq.cmp(&other.seq).reverse()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Merge `group` runs at `level` into `<target_dir>/<out_name>.run`.\nfn merge_one_batch(\n    repo: &Repository,\n    job: &Job,\n    level: u32,\n    group: &[RunEntry],\n    target_dir: &str,\n    out_name: &str,\n    spec: &KeySpec,\n    _budget: &Budget,\n) -> Result<u64> {\n    let vfs = repo.vfs();\n    let mut lanes: Vec<Lane> = Vec::with_capacity(group.len());\n    for (li, r) in group.iter().enumerate() {\n        let path = job.run_path(level, &r.name);\n        let mut reader = RunReader::open(vfs.as_ref(), &path)?;\n        let head = reader\n            .next_head()?\n            .ok_or_else(|| Error::corrupt(&path, \"merge input unexpectedly empty\"))?;\n        lanes.push(Lane { reader, head });\n        let _ = li;\n    }\n\n    // Custom heap via BinaryHeap with a wrapper carrying the spec for Ord.\n    struct Item<'b> {\n        keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n        seq: u64,\n        lane: usize,\n        spec: &'b KeySpec,\n    }\n    impl<'b> PartialEq for Item<'b> {\n        fn eq(&self, o: &Self) -> bool {\n            self.cmp(o) == Ordering::Equal\n        }\n    }\n    impl<'b> Eq for Item<'b> {}\n    impl<'b> PartialOrd for Item<'b> {\n        fn partial_cmp(&self, o: &Self) -> Option<Ordering> {\n            Some(self.cmp(o))\n        }\n    }\n    impl<'b> Ord for Item<'b> {\n        fn cmp(&self, o: &Self) -> Ordering {\n            let ak: Vec<&[u8]> = self.keys.iter().map(|k| k.as_slice()).collect();\n            let bk: Vec<&[u8]> = o.keys.iter().map(|k| k.as_slice()).collect();\n            // Reverse for max-heap -> smallest first.\n            compare_records(self.spec, &ak, self.seq, &bk, o.seq).reverse()\n        }\n    }\n\n    let mut heap: BinaryHeap<Item> = BinaryHeap::with_capacity(lanes.len());\n    for (li, lane) in lanes.iter_mut().enumerate() {\n        let keys = lane.head.keys.clone();\n        let seq = lane.head.seq;\n        heap.push(Item {\n            keys,\n            seq,\n            lane: li,\n            spec,\n        });\n    }\n\n    let mut writer = RunWriter::create(vfs.as_ref(), target_dir, out_name)?;\n    let mut io_buf = vec![0u8; crate::budget::MERGE_LANE_BUFFER];\n\n    while let Some(top) = heap.pop() {\n        let li = top.lane;\n        // Take the head out of the lane to inspect streaming needs.\n        let has_more = lanes[li].head.has_more;\n        let keys = lanes[li].head.keys.clone();\n        let seq = lanes[li].head.seq;\n\n        if !has_more {\n            // Whole value is resident in the head prefix.\n            let value = std::mem::take(&mut lanes[li].head.prefix);\n            writer.write_record(seq, &keys, &value)?;\n        } else {\n            // Stream value continuation straight into the run via an adapter.\n            let prefix = std::mem::take(&mut lanes[li].head.prefix);\n            let adapter = LaneDrain {\n                lane: &mut lanes[li],\n                buf: &mut io_buf,\n            };\n            writer.write_giant(seq, &keys, &prefix, adapter)?;\n        }\n\n        // Advance that lane to its next head.\n        match lanes[li].reader.next_head()? {\n            Some(h) => {\n repo: &Repository,\n    job: &mut Job,\n    run_index: Option<usize>,\n    _spec: &KeySpec,\n    budget: &Budget,\n    stats: &mut SortStats,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let vfs = repo.vfs();\n    let out_tmp = format!(\"jobs/{}/output.txt.tmp\", job.id);\n    let out_final = job.output_path();\n\n    let mut written: u64 = 0;\n    {\n        let mut out = vfs.create(&out_tmp)?;\n        let mut {"parentUuid":"ffac7954-0e0e-444d-af74-38f819cd9630","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_kswockppsh7fhnre7t8tnm88","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp2/a/src/sort.rs","content":"//! External sort engine: map (spill sorted segments), then multi-pass k-way\n//! merge — all resumable from the committed manifest.\n//!\n//! ## Map phase\n//!\n//! Input is scanned with a bounded [`LineScanner`]. Resident records\n//! accumulate until their bytes reach the budgeted record allowance; they are\n//! then stable-sorted in memory (composite key, seq tie-break) and spilled as\n//! one committed level-0 run. A record too large to be resident streams\n//! straight into its own single-record run. After every run commit the\n//! manifest is atomically fsync-updated. On resume the input is reopened and\n//! the already-consumed records are skipped.\n//!\n//! ## Merge phase\n//!\n//! Unmerged runs for the active level are held in `manifest.runs`; committed\n//! batch outputs of the in-progress pass are in `manifest.merge_done`\n//! (one level up). Batches are formed greedily (`lanes` inputs each); after a\n//! batch's output is committed its input runs are removed from the manifest\n//! and their files deleted. A crash therefore redoes at most the one\n//! uncommitted batch — earlier batches are reused from disk. When a pass\n//! produces exactly one run it is streamed to `output.txt`; zero records yield\n//! an empty output.\n//!\n//! ## Memory\n//!\n//! Merge lanes stream values; only the bounded head chunk is resident per\n//! lane. Fixed buffers (input read buffer, output buffer, spill work area,\n//! per-lane readahead + head) are reserved by [`crate::budget::Budget`]; the\n//! record allowance is what remains.\n\nuse std::cmp::Ordering;\nuse std::collections::BinaryHeap;\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse crate::budget::Budget;\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::io::{VFile, Vfs};\nuse crate::key::{compare_records, KeySpec};\nuse crate::repository::{Job, JobState, Repository, RunEntry};\nuse crate::scanner::{LineScanner, ScannerEvent};\nuse crate::sortfile::{GiantDrain, Pull, RecordHead, RunReader, RunWriter};\n\n/// Counters produced by a (possibly resumed) run.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct SortStats {\n    pub records: u64,\n    pub level0_runs: usize,\n    pub merge_passes: u32,\n    pub merge_batches: usize,\n    /// True when this invocation resumed previously committed work.\n    pub resumed: bool,\n    pub output_bytes: u64,\n}\n\n/// One resident record awaiting an in-memory sort.\nstruct Resident {\n    line: Vec<u8>,\n    keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n    seq: u64,\n}\n\n/// Run a job to completion, resuming from whatever the manifest committed.\npub fn run_job(repo: &Repository, job: &mut Job) -> Result<SortStats> {\n    let spec = KeySpec::parse(&job.cfg.key_spec, job.cfg.delim)?;\n    if job.cfg.max_lanes < 2 {\n        return Err(Error::Config(\"max_lanes must be at least 2\".into()));\n    }\n    let budget = Budget::plan(job.cfg.budget, job.cfg.max_lanes)?;\n    let mut stats = SortStats::default();\n    stats.resumed = job.manifest.state == JobState::Merge\n        || (job.manifest.state == JobState::Map && job.manifest.map_consumed > 0);\n\n    if job.manifest.state == JobState::Map {\n        map_phase(repo, job, &spec, &budget, &mut stats)?;\n    }\n    if job.manifest.state == JobState::Merge {\n        merge_phase(repo, job, &spec, &budget, &mut stats)?;\n    }\n    if job.manifest.state == JobState::Done && !job.cfg.keep_temp {\n        repo.cleanup_levels(job)?;\n    }\n    stats.records = job.manifest.total_records;\n    Ok(stats)\n}\n\n// ===========================================================================\n// Map\n// ===========================================================================\n\nfn map_phase(\n    repo: &Repository,\n    job: &mut Job,\n    spec: &KeySpec,\n    budget: &Budget,\n    stats: &mut SortStats,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let vfs = repo.vfs();\n\n    // A resident line is bounded by both the record allowance and a run head\n    // chunk (so a small record always serializes in one FIRST chunk).\n    let cap = budget.record_bytes().min(crate::sortfile::CHUNK_MAX - 64);\n    if cap < 64 {\n        return Err(Error::BudgetTooSmall {\n            budget: budget.total,\n            min: crate::budget::MIN_BUDGET,\n        });\n    }\n\n    // Re-open input; skip records already persisted by earlier attempts.\n    let input = vfs.open(&job.input_path())?;\n    let mut scanner = LineScanner::new(vfile_reader(input), spec.clone(), cap);\n    let mut skipped: u64 = 0;\n    let skip_to = job.manifest.map_consumed;\n    while skipped < skip_to {\n        match scanner.next()? {\n            ScannerEvent::End => {\n                return Err(Error::InconsistentState(format!(\n ScannerEvent::Giant { .. } => {\n                drain_giant(&mut scanner)?;\n                skipped += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    let mut residents: Vec<Resident> = Vec::new();\n    let mut resident_bytes = 0usize;\n    let allow = budget.record_bytes();\n    let mut next_run = job.manifest.runs.len();\n\n    loop {\n        match scanner.next()? {\n            ScannerEvent::End => break,\n            ScannerEvent::Small(rec) => {\n                let keys = extract_keys(spec, &rec.line);\n                resident_bytes += rec.line.len() + keys.iter().map(|k| k.len()).sum::<usize>();\n                residents.push(Resident {\n                    line: rec.line,\n                    keys,\n                    seq: rec.seq,\n                });\n a\n                // dedicated single-record run (never co-resident).\n                if !residents.is_empty() {\n                    spill_residents(repo, job, spec, &mut residents, &mut next_run)?;\n                    resident_bytes = 0;\n                }\n                let name = format!(\"run-{next_run:05}\");\n                next_run += 1;\n                let dir = scanner)?;\n                    let (_, n) = w.commit(vfs.as_ref())?;\n                    n\n                };\n                job.manifest.map_consumed += 1;\n                job.manifest.total_records += 1;\n                job.manifest.runs.push(RunEntry {\n                    name: format!(\"{name}.run\"),\n                    records: count,\n                });\n next_run)?;\n    }\n\n    stats.level0_runs = job.manifest.runs.len();\n    job.manifest.state = JobState::Merge;\n    job.manifest.level = 0;\n    job.manifest.merge_done.clear();\n    repo.commit_with_status(job, \"merge:begin\")?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn extract_keys(spec: &KeySpec, line: &[u8]) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {\n    spec.extract(line).into_iter().map(|k| k.to_vec()).collect()\n}\n\n/// Stable-sort buffered residents and spill one level-0 run; manifest commit.\nfn spill_residents(\n    repo: &Repository,\n    job: &mut Job,\n    spec: &KeySpec,\n    residents: &mut Vec<Resident>,\n    next_run: &mut usize,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    if residents.is_empty() {\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n    residents.sort_by(|a, b| {\n        let ak: Vec<&[u8]> = &name)?;\n        for r in residents.iter() {\n            w.write_record(r.seq, &r.keys, &r.line)?;\n        }\n        let (_, n) = w.commit(vfs.as_ref())?;\n        n\n    };\n\n    let spilled = budget.lanes().min(job.cfg.max_lanes);\n\n    loop {\n        // Empty input -> empty output.\n        if job.manifest.runs.is_empty() && job.manifest.merge_done.is_empty() {\n            write_empty_output(repo, job, stats)?;\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        // Exactly one run remains -> it is the sorted result.\n        if job.manifest.merge_done.is_empty() && while !job.manifest.runs.is_empty() {\n            let take = lanes.min(job.manifest.runs.len());\n            let group: Vec<RunEntry> = job.manifest.runs.drain(..take).collect();\n            let out_name = format!(\"m-{next_level}-{batch:05}\");\n            let count = merge_batch_to_run(\n                repo, job, level, next_level, &group, &out_name, spec, budget,\n            )?;\n job.manifest.runs = std::mem::take(&mut job.manifest.merge_done);\n        job.manifest.level = next_level;\n        repo.commit_with_status(job, \"merge:level\")?;\n    }\n}\n\n/// Where a k-way o.inner.keys.iter().map(|k| k.as_slice()).collect();\n        compare_records(self.spec, &ak, self.inner.seq, &bk, o.inner.seq).reverse()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Core k-way merge: pull heads from `lanes`, job.output_path();\n    {\n        let mut f = vfs.create(&tmp)?;\n        f.sync_all()?;\n    }\n    vfs.rename(&tmp, &final_path)?;\n    finish_done(repo, job, stats, 0)?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn finish_done(\n    repo: &Repository,\n    job: &mut Job,\n    stats: &mut SortStats,\n    output_bytes: u64,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    job.manifest.state = JobState::Done;\n    job.manifest.runs.clear();\n    job.manifest.merge_done.clear();\n    stats.output_bytes = output_bytes;\n    repo.commit_with_status(job, \"done\")?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn written_as_bytes(_repo: Resident records\n//! accumulate until their bytes reach the budgeted record allowance; they are\n//! then stable-sorted in memory (composite key, seq tie-break) and spilled as\n//! one committed level-0 run. Unmerged runs for the active level are held in `manifest.runs`; committed\n//! batch outputs of the in-progress pass are in `manifest.merge_done`\n//! (one level up). usize,\n    pub merge_passes: u32,\n    pub merge_batches: usize,\n    /// True when this invocation resumed previously committed work.\n    pub resumed: bool,\n    pub output_bytes: u64,\n}\n\n/// One resident record awaiting an in-memory sort.\nstruct Resident {\n    line: Vec<u8>,\n    keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n    seq: u64,\n}\n\n/// Run a job to completion, resuming from whatever the manifest committed.\npub fn run_job(repo: &Repository, job: &mut Job) -> Result<SortStats> {\n    let spec = KeySpec::parse(&job.cfg.key_spec, job.cfg.delim)?;\n    if job.cfg.max_lanes < 2 {\n        return Err(Error::Config(\"max_lanes must be at least 2\".into()));\n    }\n    let budget = Budget::plan(job.cfg.budget, job.cfg.max_lanes)?;\n    let mut stats = SortStats::default();\n    stats.resumed = &spec, &budget, &mut stats)?;\n    }\n    if job.manifest.state == JobState::Merge {\n        merge_phase(repo, job, &spec, &budget, &mut stats)?;\n    }\n    if job.manifest.state == JobState::Done ===========================================================================\n// Map\n// ===========================================================================\n\nfn map_phase(\n    repo: record allowance and a run head\n    // chunk (so a small record always serializes in one FIRST chunk).\n    let cap = budget.record_bytes().min(crate::sortfile::CHUNK_MAX - 64);\n    if cap < 64 {\n earlier attempts.\n    let input = vfs.open(&job.input_path())?;\n    let mut scanner = LineScanner::new(vfile_reader(input), spec.clone(), cap);\n    let mut skipped: u64 = 0;\n    let skip_to = In-memory reference sort used as the ground truth in acceptance tests.\n//!\n//! It applies the *same* composite-key comparator and sequence tie-break as\n//! the external engine, but holds everything in memory and sorts once. Input\n//! and output conventions match the engine: lines split on `\\n`, a preceding\n//! `\\r` stripped at a CRLF boundary, and exactly one `\\n` emitted per record.\n\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\n\nuse crate::error::Result;\nuse crate::key::{compare_records, KeySpec};\n\nstruct RefRecord {\n    line: Vec<u8>,\n    keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n    seq: u64,\n}\n\n/// Sort all of `input` in memory and write normalized output.\npub fn reference_sort(\n    input: &mut dyn Read,\n    output: &mut dyn Write,\n    spec: &KeySpec,\n) -> Result<u64> {\n    let mut data = Vec::new();\n    input.read_to_end(&mut data)?;\n\n    let mut records: Vec<RefRecord> = Vec::new();\n    let mut seq = 0u64;\n    let mut start = 0usize;\n    for i in 0..data.len() {\n        if data[i] == b'\\n' {\n            let mut line = &data[start..i];\n            if line.last() == Some(&b'\\r') {\n                line = &line[..line.len() - 1];\n            }\n            let keys = spec.extract(line).into_iter().map(|k| k.to_vec()).collect();\n            records.push(RefRecord {\n                line: line.to_vec(),\n                keys,\n                seq,\n            });\n            seq += 1;\n            start = i + 1;\n        }\n    }\n    // Trailing line without newline.\n    if start < data.len() {\n        let line = &data[start..];\n        let keys = spec.extract(line).into_iter().map(|k| k.to_vec()).collect();\n        records.push(RefRecord {\n            line: line.to_vec(),\n            keys,\n            seq,\n        });\n    }\n\n    records.sort_by(|a, b| {\n        let ak: Vec<&[u8]> = a.keys.iter().map(|k| k.as_slice()).collect();\n        let bk: Vec<&[u8]> = b.keys.iter().map(|k| k.as_slice()).collect();\n        compare_records(spec, &ak, a.seq, &bk, b.seq)\n    });\n\n    for r in &records {\n        output.write_all(&r.line)?;\n        output.write_all(b\"\\n\")?;\n    }\n    output.flush()?;\n    Ok(records.len() as u64)\n}\n\n/// Convenience: sort bytes and return sorted bytes.\npub fn reference_sort_bytes(data: &[u8], spec: &KeySpec) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(data.len());\n    reference_sort(&mut &data[..], &mut out, spec)?;\n    Ok(out)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn reference_basic_and_stable() {\n        let spec = KeySpec::parse(\"1\", b',').unwrap();\n        let data = b\"2,b\\n1,y\\n2,a\\n1,x\\n\";\n        let out = reference_sort_bytes(data, &spec).unwrap();\n        // group 1: input order y then x => stable keeps y,x ; group 2: b,a\n        assert_eq!(out, b\"1,y\\n1,x\\n2,b\\n2,a\\n\");\n    }\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_c0726e6f28856901e854d248","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":1275,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":126776,"output_tokens":960,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_sgzanmqnjpi830vsvy61u6em":{"content":"//! Minimal local HTTP validation server (std-only, no async runtime).\n//!\n//! ## Endpoints\n//!\n//! | Method & path                 | Purpose |\n//! |-------------------------------|---------|\n//! | `GET  /healthz`               | liveness, `ok` |\n//! | `POST /jobs?…`                | create a job, body = raw input, run it |\n//! | `GET  /jobs`                  | list job ids |\n//! | `GET  /jobs/{id}`             | status JSON (`status.json`) |\n//! | `GET  /jobs/{id}/output`      | sorted output bytes |\n//! | `DELETE /jobs/{id}`           | remove a job directory |\n//!\n//! Query parameters for `POST /jobs`:\n//! `spec` (composite key text), `delim` (one byte, default `,`),\n//! `budget` (bytes), `lanes` (merge fan-in, default 4),\n//! `keep_temp` (`1` to retain intermediates).\n//!\n//! Fault injection: pass `X-Fault-Inject: <grammar>` on a `POST /jobs` to wrap\n//! the repository's VFS in a [`crate::io::FaultVfs`]. This is the local\n//! validation harness hook for crash/failure simulation.\n//!\n//! Bodies are read using `Content-Length` (chunked transfer encoding is\n//! rejected with 411/400 — the validation client always sets a length).\n\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::thread;\n\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::io::{FaultPlan, FaultVfs, RealVfs};\nuse crate::key::KeySpec;\nuse crate::repository::{JobConfig, Repository};\nuse crate::sort::run_job;\n\n/// Server configuration.\npub struct ServerConfig {\n    pub root: String,\n    pub addr: String,\n}\n\n/// Start serving and block on the listener.\npub fn serve(cfg: ServerConfig) -> Result<()> {\n    let listener = TcpListener::bind(&cfg.addr).map_err(|e| Error::io(e, &cfg.addr))?;\n    let local = listener\n        .local_addr()\n        .map_err(|e| Error::io(e, &cfg.addr))?;\n    eprintln!(\"extsort listening on http://{local} (root {})\", cfg.root);\n\n    for conn in listener.incoming() {\n        match conn {\n            Ok(stream) => {\n                let root = cfg.root.clone();\n                thread::spawn(move || {\n                    if let Err(e) = handle_connection(stream, &root) {\n                        eprintln!(\"connection error: {e}\");\n                    }\n                });\n            }\n            Err(e) => eprintln!(\"accept error: {e}\"),\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn handle_connection(mut stream: TcpStream, root: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    stream\n        .set_read_timeout(Some(std::time::Duration::from_secs(60)))\n        .ok();\n    stream\n        .set_write_timeout(Some(std::time::Duration::from_secs(60)))\n        .ok();\n\n    let req = match parse_request(&mut stream) {\n        Ok(r) => r,\n        Err(e) => {\n            send_simple(&mut stream, 400, \"Bad Request\", &format!(\"{e}\"))?;\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n    };\n\n    let path_only = req.path.split('?').next().unwrap_or(\"/\").to_string();\n    let query = req\n        .path\n        .split_once('?')\n        .map(|(_, q)| parse_query(q))\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n\n    match (req.method.as_str(), path_only.as_str()) {\n        (\"GET\", \"/healthz\") => send_simple(&mut stream, 200, \"OK\", \"ok\\n\"),\n        (\"GET\", \"/jobs\") => list_jobs(&mut stream, root),\n        (\"POST\", \"/jobs\") => create_and_run(&mut stream, root, &query, &req),\n        (\"GET\", p) if p.starts_with(\"/jobs/\") && p.ends_with(\"/output\") => {\n            let id = &p[\"/jobs/\".len()..p.len() - \"/output\".len()];\n            get_output(&mut stream, root, id)\n        }\n        (\"GET\", p) if p.starts_with(\"/jobs/\") => {\n            let id = &p[\"/jobs/\".len()..];\n            get_status(&mut stream, root, id)\n        }\n        (\"DELETE\", p) if p.starts_with(\"/jobs/\") => {\n            let id = &p[\"/jobs/\".len()..];\n            delete_job(&mut stream, root, id)\n        }\n        _ => send_simple(&mut stream, 404, \"Not Found\", \"no such route\\n\"),\n    }\n}\n\nstruct Request {\n    method: String,\n    path: String,\n    headers: HashMap<String, String>,\n    body: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\nfn parse_request(stream: &mut TcpStream) -> Result<Request> {\n    // Read headers up to CRLF CRLF.\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(4096);\n    let mut byte = [0u8; 1];\n    let mut header_end = None;\n    while header_end.is_none() {\n        let n = stream.read(&mut byte)?;\n        if n == 0 {\n            break;\n        }\n        buf.push(byte[0]);\n        if buf.len() >= 4 && &buf[buf.len() - 4..] == b\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\" {\n            header_end = Some(buf.len() - 4);\n        }\n        if buf.len() > 64 * 1024 {\n            return Err(Error::BadRequest(\"headers too large\".into()));\n        }\n    }\n    let end = header_end.ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"no header terminator\".into()))?;\n    let head = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf[..end]).into_owned();\n    let mut lines = head.split(\"\\r\\n\");\n    let request_line = lines\n        .next()\n        .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"empty request\".into()))?;\n    let mut parts = request_line.split_whitespace();\n    let method = parts\n        .next()\n        .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"no method\".into()))?\n        .to_string();\n    let path = parts\n        .next()\n        .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"no path\".into()))?\n        .to_string();\n\n    let mut headers = HashMap::new();\n    for line in lines {\n        if let Some((k, v)) = line.split_once(':') {\n            headers.insert(k.trim().to_lowercase(), v.trim().to_string());\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Read body per Content-Length; bytes beyond headers already consumed are\n    // none here (we read header one byte at a time), so body starts fresh.\n    let mut body = Vec::new();\n    if let Some(len_txt) = headers.get(\"content-length\") {\n        let len: usize = len_txt\n            .parse()\n            .map_err(|_| Error::BadRequest(\"bad content-length\".into()))?;\n        body = vec![0u8; len];\n        read_full(stream, &mut body)?;\n    } else if headers.contains_key(\"transfer-encoding\") {\n        return Err(Error::BadRequest(\n            \"chunked request bodies are not supported; set Content-Length\".into(),\n        ));\n    }\n\n    Ok(Request {\n        method,\n        path,\n        headers,\n        body,\n    })\n}\n\nfn read_full(stream: &mut TcpStream, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<()> {\n    let mut got = 0;\n    while got < buf.len() {\n        let n = stream.read(&mut buf[got..])?;\n        if n == 0 {\n            return Err(Error::BadRequest(\"request body truncated\".into()));\n        }\n        got += n;\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn parse_query(q: &str) -> HashMap<String, String> {\n    let mut m = HashMap::new();\n    for pair in q.split('&') {\n        if let Some((k, v)) = pair.split_once('=') {\n            m.insert(urldecode(k), urldecode(v));\n        } else if !pair.is_empty() {\n            m.insert(urldecode(pair), String::new());\n        }\n    }\n    m\n}\n\nfn urldecode(s: &str) -> String {\n    let b = s.replace('+', \" \");\n    let bytes = b.as_bytes();\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i < bytes.len() {\n        if bytes[i] == b'%' && i + 2 < bytes.len() {\n            if let Ok(v) = u8::from_str_radix(&s[i + 1..i + 3], 16) {\n                out.push(v);\n                i += 3;\n                continue;\n            }\n        }\n        out.push(bytes[i]);\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    String::from_utf8_lossy(&out).into_owned()\n}\n\nfn send_simple(stream: &mut TcpStream, status: u16, reason: &str, body: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    send_bytes(stream, status, reason, \"text/plain; charset=utf-8\", body.as_bytes())\n}\n\nfn send_bytes(\n    stream: &mut TcpStream,\n    status: u16,\n    reason: &str,\n    content_type: &str,\n    body: &[u8],\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let head = format!(\n        \"HTTP/1.1 {status} {reason}\\r\\nContent-Type: {content_type}\\r\\nContent-Length: {}\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n\",\n        body.len()\n    );\n    stream.write_all(head.as_bytes())?;\n    stream.write_all(body)?;\n    stream.flush()?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn send_json(stream: &mut TcpStream, status: u16, reason: &str, json: String) -> Result<()> {\n    send_bytes(\n        stream,\n        status,\n        reason,\n        \"application/json\",\n        json.as_bytes(),\n    )\n}\n\nfn list_jobs(stream: &mut TcpStream, root: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    let repo = Repository::new(root);\n    let ids = repo.list_jobs()?;\n    let json = format!(\n        \"{{\\\"jobs\\\":[{}]}}\\n\",\n        ids.iter()\n            .map(|i| format!(\"\\\"{}\\\"\", crate::repository::json_escape(i)))\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(\",\")\n    );\n    send_json(stream, 200, \"OK\", json)\n}\n\nfn get_status(stream: &mut TcpStream, root: &str, id: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    if id.is_empty() || id.contains('/') || id.contains(\"..\") {\n        return send_simple(stream, 400, \"Bad Request\", \"bad job id\\n\");\n    }\n    let repo = Repository::new(root);\n    match repo.read_status(id) {\n        Ok(s) => send_json(stream, 200, \"OK\", s),\n        Err(e) => send_error(stream, &e),\n    }\n}\n\nfn get_output(stream: &mut TcpStream, root: &str, id: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    if id.is_empty() || id.contains('/') || id.contains(\"..\") {\n        return send_simple(stream, 400, \"Bad Request\", \"bad job id\\n\");\n    }\n    let repo = Repository::new(root);\n    let vfs = repo.vfs();\n    let path = format!(\"jobs/{id}/output.txt\");\n    match crate::io::read_all(vfs.as_ref(), &path) {\n        Ok(bytes) => send_bytes(stream, 200, \"OK\", \"application/octet-stream\", &bytes),\n        Err(e) => send_error(stream, &e),\n    }\n}\n\nfn delete_job(stream: &mut TcpStream, root: &str, id: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    if id.is_empty() || id.contains('/') || id.contains(\"..\") {\n        return send_simple(stream, 400, \"Bad Request\", \"bad job id\\n\");\n    }\n    let repo = Repository::new(root);\n    repo.vfs().remove_dir_all(&format!(\"jobs/{id}\"))?;\n    send_json(stream, 200, \"OK\", format!(\"{{\\\"deleted\\\":\\\"{id}\\\"}}\\n\"))\n}\n\nfn create_and_run(\n    stream: &mut TcpStream,\n    root: &str,\n    q: &HashMap<String, String>,\n    req: &Request,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let cfg = match parse_config(q) {\n        Ok(c) => c,\n        Err(e) => return send_error(stream, &e),\n    };\n\n    // Validate the key spec up front for a clean 400.\n    if let Err(e) = KeySpec::parse(&cfg.key_spec, cfg.delim) {\n        return send_error(stream, &e);\n    }\n\n    let id = new_job_id();\n\n    // Optional fault injection for this single request.\n    let fault_text = req\n        .headers\n        .get(\"x-fault-inject\")\n        .cloned()\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n    let result = if fault_text.is_empty() {\n        run_with_repo(root, &id, &cfg, &req.body, None)\n    } else {\n        match FaultPlan::parse(&fault_text) {\n            Ok(plan) => run_with_repo(root, &id, &cfg, &req.body, Some(plan)),\n            Err(msg) => {\n                return send_simple(\n                    stream,\n                    400,\n                    \"Bad Request\",\n                    &format!(\"invalid X-Fault-Inject: {msg}\\n\"),\n                )\n            }\n        }\n    };\n\n    match result {\n        Ok(summary) => send_json(stream, 200, \"OK\", summary),\n        Err(e) => send_error_with_body(stream, root, &id, &e),\n    }\n}\n\nfn parse_config(q: &HashMap<String, String>) -> Result<JobConfig> {\n    let mut cfg = JobConfig::default();\n    if let Some(v) = q.get(\"spec\") {\n        cfg.key_spec = v.clone();\n    }\n    if let Some(v) = q.get(\"delim\") {\n        let b = v.as_bytes();\n        if b.len() != 1 {\n            return Err(Error::Config(\"delim must be exactly one byte\".into()));\n        }\n        cfg.delim = b[0];\n    }\n    if let Some(v) = q.get(\"budget\") {\n        cfg.budget = v\n            .parse()\n            .map_err(|_| Error::Config(\"budget must be a positive integer\".into()))?;\n    }\n    if let Some(v) = q.get(\"lanes\") {\n        cfg.max_lanes = v\n            .parse()\n            .map_err(|_| Error::Config(\"lanes must be an integer >= 2\".into()))?;\n    }\n    if let Some(v) = q.get(\"keep_temp\") {\n        cfg.keep_temp = v == \"1\" || v.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"true\");\n    }\n    Ok(cfg)\n}\n\nfn run_with_repo(\n    root: &str,\n    id: &str,\n    cfg: &JobConfig,\n    body: &[u8],\n    fault: Option<FaultPlan>,\n) -> Result<String> {\n    let repo = match fault {\n        Some(plan) => {\n            let real = Arc::new(RealVfs::new(Path::new(root)));\n            let fault_vfs = Arc::new(FaultVfs::new(real, plan));\n            Repository::with_vfs(root, fault_vfs)\n        }\n        None => Repository::new(root),\n    };\n    let vfs = repo.vfs();\n\n    let mut job = repo.create_job(id, cfg.clone())?;\n    // Persist the raw input.\n    let input_tmp = format!(\"jobs/{id}/input.dat.tmp\");\n    let input_dst = format!(\"jobs/{id}/input.dat\");\n    crate::io::atomic_write_bytes(vfs.as_ref(), &input_tmp, &input_dst, body)?;\n\n    let stats = run_job(&repo, &mut job);\n    match stats {\n        Ok(s) => Ok(format!(\n            \"{{\\\"job_id\\\":\\\"{id}\\\",\\\"state\\\":\\\"done\\\",\\\"records\\\":{},\\\"level0_runs\\\":{},\\\"merge_passes\\\":{},\\\"merge_batches\\\":{},\\\"resumed\\\":{},\\\"output_bytes\\\":{},\\\"output\\\":\\\"/jobs/{id}/output\\\"}}\\n\",\n            s.records, s.level0_runs, s.merge_passes, s.merge_batches, s.resumed, s.output_bytes\n        )),\n        Err(e) => {\n            repo.mark_failed(&mut job, &e.to_string());\n            Err(e)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn send_error(stream: &mut TcpStream, e: &Error) -> Result<()> {\n    let status = e.http_status();\n    let reason = reason_phrase(status);\n    let body = format!(\"{{\\\"error\\\":\\\"{}\\\",\\\"code\\\":\\\"{}\\\"}}\\n\", crate::repository::json_escape(&e.to_string()), e.code());\n    send_json(stream, status, reason, body)\n}\n\n/// After a failed run the status.json holds the durable failure; surface it.\nfn send_error_with_body(\n    stream: &mut TcpStream,\n    root: &str,\n    id: &str,\n    e: &Error,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let status = e.http_status();\n    let reason = reason_phrase(status);\n    let detail = Repository::new(root)\n        .read_status(id)\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"{}\".into());\n    let body = format!(\n        \"{{\\\"job_id\\\":\\\"{id}\\\",\\\"error\\\":\\\"{}\\\",\\\"code\\\":\\\"{}\\\",\\\"status\\\":{}}}\\n\",\n        crate::repository::json_escape(&e.to_string()),\n        e.code(),\n        detail.trim()\n    );\n    send_json(stream, status, reason, body)\n}\n\nfn reason_phrase(status: u16) -> &'static str {\n    match status {\n        200 => \"OK\",\n        400 => \"Bad Request\",\n        404 => \"Not Found\",\n        _ => \"Internal Server Error\",\n    }\n}\n\nfn new_job_id() -> String {\n    use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};\n    let nanos = SystemTime::now()\n        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)\n        .map(|d| d.as_nanos())\n        .unwrap_or(0);\n    // Cheap uniqueness without external crates: nanos + pid + a mutating tail.\n    let pid = std::process::id();\n    let tail = (nanos & 0xFFFF) as u32;\n    format!(\"j-{:x}-{:x}\", nanos, pid ^ tail)\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_976e1d4d32fb33f0c8739337","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":1255,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":127800,"output_tokens":4912,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_sph3vpez9o88h5ay2jpcfgbv":{"content":"//! stream: &mut TcpStream,\n    root: &str,\n    q: &HashMap<String, String>,\n    req: &Request,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let cfg = match parse_config(q) {\n        Ok(c) => c,\n        Err(e) => return v\n            .parse()\n            .map_err(|_| Error::Config(\"lanes must be an integer >= 2\".into()))?;\n    }\n    if let Some(v) = q.get(\"keep_temp\") {\n        cfg.keep_temp = v == \"1\" || v.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"true\");\n    }\n    Ok(cfg)\n}\n\nfn run_with_repo(\n    root: &str,\n    id: &str,\n    cfg: &JobConfig,\n    body: &[u8],\n    fault: Option<FaultPlan>,\n) -> crate::io::atomic_write_bytes(vfs.as_ref(), &input_tmp, &input_dst, body)?;\n\n    let stats = run_job(&repo, &mut job);\n    match stats {\n        Ok(s) => Ok(format!(\n            \"{{\\\"job_id\\\":\\\"{id}\\\",\\\"state\\\":\\\"done\\\",\\\"records\\\":{},\\\"level0_runs\\\":{},\\\"merge_passes\\\":{},\\\"merge_batches\\\":{},\\\"resumed\\\":{},\\\"output_bytes\\\":{},\\\"output\\\":\\\"/jobs/{id}/output\\\"}}\\n\",\n            s.records, s.level0_runs, s.merge_passes, s.merge_batches, s.resumed, s.output_bytes\n        )),\n        Err(e) => {\n            repo.mark_failed(&mut job, &e.to_string());\n            Err(e)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn send_error(stream: &mut TcpStream, e: &Error) -> Result<()> {\n    let status = e.http_status();\n    let reason = reason_phrase(status);\n    let body = detail.trim()\n    );\n    send_json(stream, status, reason, body)\n}\n\nfn reason_phrase(status: u16) -> &'static str {\n    match status {\n        200 => \"OK\",\n        400 => \"Bad Request\",\n
