Command-line entry point.\n//!\n//! Commands:\n//! * `serve --root DIR [--addr 127.0.0.1:8080]`\n//!   Run the local HTTP validation server.\n//! * `sort --input FILE --output FILE [--root DIR] [--spec SPEC]\n//!          [--delim ,] [--budget BYTES] [--lanes N] [--keep-temp]\n//!          [--fault GRAMMAR]`\n//!   Run one job end to end (resumable). With `--fault`, the named faults are\n//!   injected; rerun with `--resume` to demonstrate recovery.\n//! * `resume --root DIR --job ID`\n//!   Reopen a crashed/interrupted job and continue.\n\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::process::ExitCode;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse extsort::io::{FaultPlan, FaultVfs, RealVfs};\nuse extsort::repository::{JobConfig, Repository};\nuse extsort::server::ServerConfig;\nuse extsort::{run_job, Error};\n\nfn main() -> ExitCode {\n    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();\n    match run(&args) {\n        Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"error: {e}\");\n            ExitCode::FAILURE\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn run(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    let cmd = args.get(1).map(|s| s.as_str()).unwrap_or(\"help\");\n    match cmd {\n        \"serve\" => cmd_serve(&args[2..]),\n        \"sort\" => cmd_sort(&args[2..]),\n        \"resume\" => cmd_resume(&args[2..]),\n        \"help\" | \"--help\" | \"-h\" => {\n            print_help();\n            Ok(())\n        }\n        other => {\n            eprintln!(\"unknown command: {other}\\n\");\n            print_help();\n            Err(Error::BadRequest(\"unknown command\".into()))\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn print_help() {\n    println!(\n        \"extsort — bounded-memory file-backed stable external sort\\n\\\n\\n\\\nUSAGE:\\n\\\n  extsort serve  --root DIR [--addr 127.0.0.1:8080]\\n\\\n  extsort sort   --input FILE --output FILE [--root DIR]\\n\\\n                 [--spec \\\"field:asc,field:desc\\\"] [--delim ,]\\n\\\n                 [--budget BYTES] [--lanes N] [--keep-temp]\\n\\\n                 [--fault GRAMMAR] [--job ID]\\n\\\n  extsort resume --root DIR --job ID\\n\"\n    );\n}\n\nstruct Opts {\n    map: Vec<(String, String)>,\n}\n\nfn parse_opts(args: &[String]) -> Result<Opts, Error> {\n    let mut map = Vec::new();\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i < args.len() {\n        let a = &args[i];\n        if let Some(key) = a.strip_prefix(\"--\") {\n            // Allow --key=value and --key value.\n            if let Some((k, v)) = key.split_once('=') {\n                map.push((k.to_string(), v.to_string()));\n            } else if i + 1 < args.len() {\n                map.push((key.to_string(), args[i + 1].clone()));\n                i += 1;\n            } else {\n                return Err(Error::BadRequest(format!(\"option {a} needs a value\")));\n            }\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    Ok(Opts { map })\n}\n\nimpl Opts {\n    fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&str> {\n        self.map.iter().find(|(k, _)| k == key).map(|(_, v)| v.as_str())\n    }\n}\n\nfn cmd_serve(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    let opts = parse_opts(args)?;\n    let root = opts\n        .get(\"root\")\n        .unwrap_or(\"./extsort-data\")\n        .to_string();\n    let addr = opts\n        .get(\"addr\")\n        .unwrap_or(\"127.0.0.1:8080\")\n        .to_string();\n    extsort::server::serve(ServerConfig { root, addr })\n}\n\nfn cmd_sort(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    let opts = parse_opts(args)?;\n    let input = opts\n        .get(\"input\")\n        .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"--input is required\".into()))?;\n    let output = opts\n        .get(\"output\")\n        .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"--output is required\".into()))?;\n    let root = opts\n        .get(\"root\")\n        .map(|s| s.to_string())\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| temp_root());\n\n    let cfg = JobConfig {\n        key_spec: opts.get(\"spec\").unwrap_or(\"\").to_string(),\n        delim: opts\n            .get(\"delim\")\n            .map(|d| d.as_bytes().first().copied().unwrap_or(b','))\n            .unwrap_or(b','),\n        budget: opts\n            .get(\"budget\")\n            .map(|b| b.parse::<u64>())\n            .transpose()\n            .map_err(|_| Error::BadRequest(\"bad --budget\".into()))?\n            .unwrap_or(4 * 1024 * 1024),\n        max_lanes: opts\n            .get(\"lanes\")\n            .map(|b| b.parse::<usize>())\n            .transpose()\n            .map_err(|_| Error::BadRequest(\"bad --lanes\".into()))?\n            .unwrap_or(4),\n        keep_temp: opts.get(\"keep-temp\").is_some(),\n    };\n\n    let data = fs::read(input).map_err(|e| Error::io(e, input.to_string()))?;\n    let id = opts\n        .get(\"job\")\n        .map(|s| s.to_string())\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| \"local\".to_string());\n\n    let repo = if let Some(grammar) = opts.get(\"fault\") {\n        let plan = FaultPlan::parse(grammar)\n            .map_err(|m| Error::BadRequest(format!(\"bad --fault: {m}\")))?;\n        let real = Arc::new(RealVfs::new(PathBuf::from(&root)));\n        Repository::with_vfs(&root, Arc::new(FaultVfs::new(real, plan)))\n    } else {\n        Repository::new(&root)\n    };\n    let vfs = repo.vfs();\n\n    // Remove a stale same-id job so `sort` starts clean (resume uses `resume`).\n    vfs.remove_dir_all(&format!(\"jobs/{id}\"))?;\n    let mut job = repo.create_job(&id, cfg.clone())?;\n    crate::io::atomic_write_bytes(\n        vfs.as_ref(),\n        &format!(\"jobs/{id}/input.dat.tmp\"),\n        &format!(\"jobs/{id}/input.dat\"),\n        &data,\n    )?;\n\n    let stats = run_job(&repo, &mut job)?;\n    // Copy output to the requested destination.\n    let produced = crate::io::read_all(vfs.as_ref(), &format!(\"jobs/{id}/output.txt\"))?;\n    fs::write(output, produced).map_err(|e| Error::io(e, output.to_string()))?;\n\n    eprintln!(\n        \"done: records={} level0_runs={} merge_passes={} merge_batches={} output_bytes={}\",\n        stats.records, stats.level0_runs, stats.merge_passes, stats.merge_batches, stats.output_bytes\n    );\n    eprintln!(\"job state kept at {root}/jobs/{id}\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn cmd_resume(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    let opts = parse_opts(args)?;\n    let root = opts\n        .get(\"root\")\n        .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"--root is required\".into()))?;\n    let id = opts\n        .get(\"job\")\n        .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"--job is required\".into()))?;\n    let output = opts.get(\"output\");\n\n    let repo = Repository::new(root);\n    let mut job = repo.open_job(id)?;\n    let stats = run_job(&repo, &mut job)?;\n    eprintln!(\n        \"resumed to done: records={} level0_runs={} merge_passes={} resumed=true output_bytes={}\",\n        stats.records, stats.level0_runs, stats.merge_passes, stats.output_bytes\n    );\n    if let Some(path) = output {\n        let bytes = crate::io::read_all(repo.vfs().as_ref(), &format!(\"jobs/{id}/output.txt\"))?;\n        fs::write(path, bytes).map_err(|e| Error::io(e, path.to_string()))?;\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn temp_root() -> String {\n    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\n        \"extsort-cli-{}\",\n        std::time::SystemTime::now()\n            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n            .map(|d| d.as_nanos())\n            .unwrap_or(0)\n    ));\n    dir.display().to_string()\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_c313d99da2575e2289bbb113","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":5029,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":128824,"output_tokens":2357,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_xoa2ux4uamgw4pakew9usqg2":{"content":"//! IEEE CRC-32 (poly 0xEDB88320, the zlib/checksum32 variant), std-only.\n//!\n//! Used to detect torn writes and corrupted temporary segments. This is an\n//! integrity check, not a cryptographic hash.\n\n/// Precomputed 256-entry lookup table.\npub struct Table {\n    entries: [u32; 256],\n}\n\nimpl Table {\n    pub const fn new() -> Self {\n        let mut entries = [0u32; 256];\n        let mut i = 0usize;\n        while i < 256 {\n            let mut c = i as u32;\n            let mut k = 0;\n            while k < 8 {\n                c = if c & 1 != 0 {\n                    0xEDB88320 ^ (c >> 1)\n                } else {\n                    c >> 1\n                };\n                k += 1;\n            }\n            entries[i] = c;\n            i += 1;\n        }\n        Table { entries }\n    }\n\n    /// Update `crc` with `bytes`; start from [`Crc::INIT`].\n    pub const fn update(&self, mut crc: u32, bytes: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n        let mut i = 0;\n        while i < bytes.len() {\n            let idx = ((crc ^ bytes[i] as u32) & 0xFF) as usize;\n            crc = self.entries[idx] ^ (crc >> 8);\n            i += 1;\n        }\n        crc\n    }\n}\n\n/// Streaming CRC-32 accumulator.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct Crc {\n    table: Table,\n    value: u32,\n}\n\nimpl Default for Crc {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Crc {\n    pub const INIT: u32 = 0xFFFF_FFFF;\n\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Crc {\n            table: Table::new(),\n            value: Self::INIT,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn write(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) {\n        self.value = self.table.update(self.value, bytes);\n    }\n\n    pub fn finish(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.value ^ 0xFFFF_FFFF\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// Known-answer vectors (CRC-32/ISO-HDLC as produced by `crc32` util).\n    #[test]\n    fn known_vectors() {\n        fn crc(b: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n            let mut c = Crc::new();\n            c.write(b);\n            c.finish()\n        }\n        assert_eq!(crc(b\"\"), 0);\n        assert_eq!(crc(b\"123456789\"), 0xCBF43926);\n        assert_eq!(crc(b\"a\"), 0xE8B7_BE43);\n        // Streaming == one-shot.\n        let mut c = Crc::new();\n        c.write(b\"1234\");\n        c.write(b\"56789\");\n        assert_eq!(c.finish(), 0xCBF43926);\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":4,"oldLines":6,"newStart":4,"newLines":7,"lines":[" //! integrity check, not a cryptographic hash."," "," /// Precomputed 256-entry lookup table.","+#[derive(Clone, Copy)]"," pub struct Table {","     entries: [u32; {"parentUuid":"d625ff30-0e5a-4c80-a914-054e30a93ee8","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"edited_text_file","filename":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp2/a/src/scanner.rs","snippet":"1\t//! Bounded-memory input scanner.\n2\t//!\n3\t//! Records are lines separated by `\\n`; a `\\r` immediately before `\\n` is a\n4\t//! terminator and stripped (CRLF). At most `small_limit` bytes of any line are\n5\t//! retained.\n6\t//!\n7\t//! * Short lines are returned owned as [`ScannerEvent::Small`].\n8\t//! * A line that reaches the limit becomes a [`ScannerEvent::Giant`]: its key\n9\t//!   is resolved from a bounded prefix (or bounded prefix + a one-byte\n10\t//!   lookahead) and the caller streams the remainder through the scanner's\n11\t//! Bounded-memory input scanner.\n//!\n//! Records are lines separated by `\\n`; a `\\r` immediately before `\\n` is a\n//! terminator and stripped (CRLF).\n//!\n//! * Lines up to `small_limit` bytes are returned owned as\n//!   [`ScannerEvent::Small`] and sorted in memory.\n//! * A line that grows past `small_limit` becomes a [`ScannerEvent::Giant`]:\n//!   scanning keeps buffering only until its key columns are known (capped by\n//!   `head_limit`, the run writer's bounded head-chunk window), then the\n//!   caller streams the rest through the [`GiantDrain`] impl straight into a\n//!   run. A key that cannot be resolved within `head_limit` is a\n//!   [`Error::KeyTooLarge`].\n//!\n//! Output convention (shared with the in-memory reference): every emitted\n//! record is followed by `\\n`, even the last — so no per-record newline flag is\n//! persisted in runs.\n\nuse std::io;\n\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::key::{prefix_has_key, KeySpec};\nuse crate::sortfile::{GiantDrain, Pull};\n\n/// Input stream the scanner reads from.\npub type Input = Box<dyn io::Read + Send>;\n\n/// Internal read buffer (counted toward the memory budget).\npub const READ_BUFFER: usize = 16 * 1024;\n\n/// A record that fits inside the memory window.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct SmallRecord {\n    pub line: Vec<u8>,\n    pub seq: u64,\n}\n\n/// Event yielded per input record.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum ScannerEvent {\n    Small(SmallRecord),\n    /// Drain this giant record via the [`GiantDrain`] impl before `next`.\n    Giant {\n        seq: u64,\n        keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n        /// Bounded head value (the buffered line prefix).\n        prefix: Vec<u8>,\n    },\n    End,\n}\n\npub struct LineScanner {\n    input: Input,\n    readbuf: Vec<u8>,\n    read_pos: usize,\n    read_fill: usize,\n    eof: bool,\n\n    small_limit: usize,\n    head_limit: usize,\n    spec: KeySpec,\n\n    cur: Vec<u8>,\n    seq: u64,\n\n    // Giant drain state.\n    giant_active: bool,\n    /// When true, the line ended during prefix resolution; the first pull\n    /// returns no bytes and signals end-of-record.\n    giant_immediate_end: bool,\n    look: Option<u8>,\n    pending_cr: bool,\n}\n\nimpl LineScanner {\n    /// `small_limit` is the resident-record cap (crossing it makes a line a\n    /// giant); `head_limit` is the larger head-chunk window within which a\n    /// giant's key must be resolvable.\n    pub fn new(\n        input: Input,\n        spec: KeySpec,\n        small_limit: usize,\n        head_limit: usize,\n    ) -> Self {\n        LineScanner {\n            input,\n            readbuf: vec![0u8; READ_BUFFER],\n            read_pos: 0,\n            read_fill: 0,\n            eof: false,\n            small_limit,\n            head_limit,\n            spec,\n            cur: Vec::new(),\n            seq: 0,\n            giant_active: false,\n            giant_immediate_end: false,\n            look: None,\n            pending_cr: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn seq(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.seq\n    }\n    pub fn spec(&self) -> &KeySpec {\n        &self.spec\n    }\n\n    fn next_input_byte(&mut self) -> Result<Option<u8>> {\n        if self.read_pos >= self.read_fill {\n            if self.eof {\n                return Ok(None);\n            }\n            let n = self.input.read(&mut self.readbuf)?;\n            if n == 0 {\n                self.eof = true;\n                return Ok(None);\n            }\n            self.read_pos = 0;\n            self.read_fill = n;\n        }\n        let b = self.readbuf[self.read_pos];\n        self.read_pos += 1;\n        Ok(Some(b))\n    }\n\n    /// Scan the next record.\n    pub fn next(&mut self) -> Result<ScannerEvent> {\n        debug_assert!(!self.giant_active, \"giant record not fully drained\");\n        self.cur.clear();\n        self.look = None;\n        self.pending_cr = false;\n        self.giant_immediate_end = false;\n        let seq = self.seq;\n        let mut nl = false;\n\n        // Phase 1: buffer up to small_limit bytes.\n        while self.cur.len() < self.small_limit {\n            match self.next_input_byte()? {\n                Some(b'\\n') => {\n                    nl = true;\n                    break;\n                }\n                Some(b) => self.cur.push(b),\n                None => break,\n            }\n        }\n\n        // A line terminated within the resident window is a small record.\n        if nl || self.cur.len() < self.small_limit {\n            if self.cur.is_empty() && !nl {\n                return Ok(ScannerEvent::End);\n            }\n            if nl && self.cur.last() == Some(&b'\\r') {\n                self.cur.pop();\n            }\n            self.seq += 1;\n            return Ok(ScannerEvent::Small(SmallRecord {\n                line: std::mem::take(&mut self.cur),\n                seq,\n            }));\n        }\n\n        // Phase 2: the line crossed the resident cap. Keep buffering until its\n        // key columns are known, capped by the writer's head window.\n        if crate::key::key_needs_whole_line(&self.spec) {\n            return Err(Error::KeyTooLarge {\n                seq,\n                needed: self.small_limit + 1,\n                budget: self.head_limit as u64,\n            });\n        }\n        loop {\n            if prefix_has_key(&self.spec, &self.cur) {\n                break;\n            }\n            match self.next_input_byte()? {\n                Some(b'\\n') => {\n                    nl = true;\n                    break;\n                }\n                Some(b) => {\n                    if self.cur.len() >= self.head_limit {\n                        return Err(Error::KeyTooLarge {\n                            seq,\n                            needed: self.cur.len() + 1,\n                            budget: self.head_limit as u64,\n                        });\n                    }\n                    self.cur.push(b);\n                }\n                None => break, // line ends without newline; key is known\n            }\n        }\n\n        let keys = self\n            .spec\n            .extract(&self.cur)\n            .into_iter()\n            .map(|k| k.to_vec())\n            .collect();\n        let prefix = std::mem::take(&mut self.cur);\n        self.giant_active = true;\n        self.giant_immediate_end = nl;\n        self.seq += 1;\n        Ok(ScannerEvent::Giant {\n            seq,\n            keys,\n            prefix,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n/// Streaming source for one giant record. When the line ended while its prefix\n/// was being resolved, the first pull returns 0 bytes + end-of-record. Bytes\n/// are read one at a time so CRLF CRs can be withheld and dropped if a newline\n/// follows.\nimpl GiantDrain for LineScanner {\n    fn pull(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<Pull> {\n        debug_assert!(self.giant_active);\n        if self.giant_immediate_end {\n            self.giant_immediate_end = false;\n            self.giant_active = false;\n            return Ok(Pull {\n Command-line entry point.\n//!\n//! Commands:\n//! * `serve --root DIR [--addr 127.0.0.1:8080]`\n//!   Run the local HTTP validation server.\n//! * `sort --input FILE --output FILE [--root DIR] [--spec SPEC]\n//!          [--delim ,] [--budget BYTES] [--lanes N] [--keep-temp]\n//!          [--fault GRAMMAR]`\n//!   Run one job end to end (resumable). With `--fault`, the named faults are\n//!   injected; rerun with `--resume` to demonstrate recovery.\n//! * `resume --root DIR --job ID`\n//!   Reopen a crashed/interrupted job and continue.\n\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::process::ExitCode;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse extsort::io::{FaultPlan, FaultVfs, RealVfs};\nuse extsort::repository::{JobConfig, Repository};\nuse extsort::server::ServerConfig;\nuse extsort::{run_job, Error};\n\nfn main() -> ExitCode {\n    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();\n    match run(&args) {\n        Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"error: {e}\");\n            ExitCode::FAILURE\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn run(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    let cmd = args.get(1).map(|s| s.as_str()).unwrap_or(\"help\");\n    match cmd {\n        \"serve\" => cmd_serve(&args[2..]),\n        \"sort\" => cmd_sort(&args[2..]),\n        \"resume\" => cmd_resume(&args[2..]),\n        \"help\" | \"--help\" | \"-h\" => {\n            print_help();\n            Ok(())\n        }\n        other => {\n            eprintln!(\"unknown command: {other}\\n\");\n            print_help();\n            Err(Error::BadRequest(\"unknown command\".into()))\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn print_help() {\n    println!(\n        \"extsort — bounded-memory file-backed stable external sort\\n\\\n\\n\\\nUSAGE:\\n\\\n  extsort serve  --root DIR [--addr 127.0.0.1:8080]\\n\\\n  extsort sort   --input FILE --output FILE [--root DIR]\\n\\\n                 [--spec \\\"field:asc,field:desc\\\"] [--delim ,]\\n\\\n                 [--budget BYTES] [--lanes N] [--keep-temp]\\n\\\n                 [--fault GRAMMAR] [--job ID]\\n\\\n  extsort resume --root DIR --job ID\\n\"\n    );\n}\n\nstruct Opts {\n    map: Vec<(String, String)>,\n}\n\nfn parse_opts(args: &[String]) -> Result<Opts, Error> {\n    let mut map = Vec::new();\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i < args.len() {\n        let a = &args[i];\n        if let Some(key) = a.strip_prefix(\"--\") {\n            // Allow --key=value and --key value.\n            if let Some((k, v)) = key.split_once('=') {\n                map.push((k.to_string(), v.to_string()));\n            } else if i + 1 < args.len() {\n                map.push((key.to_string(), args[i + 1].clone()));\n                i += 1;\n            } else {\n                return Err(Error::BadRequest(format!(\"option {a} needs a value\")));\n            }\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    Ok(Opts { map })\n}\n\nimpl Opts {\n    fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&str> {\n        self.map.iter().find(|(k, _)| k == key).map(|(_, v)| v.as_str())\n    }\n}\n\nfn cmd_serve(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    let opts = parse_opts(args)?;\n    let root = opts\n        .get(\"root\")\n        .unwrap_or(\"./extsort-data\")\n        .to_string();\n    let addr = opts\n        .get(\"addr\")\n        .unwrap_or(\"127.0.0.1:8080\")\n        .to_string();\n    extsort::server::serve(ServerConfig { root, addr })\n}\n\nfn cmd_sort(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    let opts = parse_opts(args)?;\n    let input = opts\n        .get(\"input\")\n        .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"--input is required\".into()))?;\n    let output = opts\n        .get(\"output\")\n        .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"--output is required\".into()))?;\n    let root = opts\n        .get(\"root\")\n        .map(|s| s.to_string())\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| temp_root());\n\n    let cfg = JobConfig {\n        key_spec: opts.get(\"spec\").unwrap_or(\"\").to_string(),\n        delim: opts\n            .get(\"delim\")\n            .map(|d| d.as_bytes().first().copied().unwrap_or(b','))\n            .unwrap_or(b','),\n        budget: opts\n            .get(\"budget\")\n            .map(|b| b.parse::<u64>())\n            .transpose()\n            .map_err(|_| Error::BadRequest(\"bad --budget\".into()))?\n            .unwrap_or(4 * 1024 * 1024),\n        max_lanes: opts\n            .get(\"lanes\")\n            .map(|b| b.parse::<usize>())\n            .transpose()\n            .map_err(|_| Error::BadRequest(\"bad --lanes\".into()))?\n            .unwrap_or(4),\n        keep_temp: opts.get(\"keep-temp\").is_some(),\n    };\n\n    let data = fs::read(input).map_err(|e| Error::io(e, input.to_string()))?;\n    let id = opts\n        .get(\"job\")\n        .map(|s| s.to_string())\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| \"local\".to_string());\n\n    let repo = if let Some(grammar) = opts.get(\"fault\") {\n        let plan = FaultPlan::parse(grammar)\n            .map_err(|m| Error::BadRequest(format!(\"bad --fault: {m}\")))?;\n        let real = Arc::new(RealVfs::new(PathBuf::from(&root)));\n        Repository::with_vfs(&root, Arc::new(FaultVfs::new(real, plan)))\n    } else {\n        Repository::new(&root)\n    };\n    let vfs = repo.vfs();\n\n    // Remove a stale same-id job so `sort` starts clean (resume uses `resume`).\n    vfs.remove_dir_all(&format!(\"jobs/{id}\"))?;\n    let mut job = repo.create_job(&id, cfg.clone())?;\n    extsort::io::atomic_write_bytes(\n        vfs.as_ref(),\n        &format!(\"jobs/{id}/input.dat.tmp\"),\n        &format!(\"jobs/{id}/input.dat\"),\n        &data,\n    )?;\n\n    let stats = run_job(&repo, &mut job)?;\n    // Copy output to the requested destination.\n    let produced = extsort::io::read_all(vfs.as_ref(), &format!(\"jobs/{id}/output.txt\"))?;\n    fs::write(output, produced).map_err(|e| Error::io(e, output.to_string()))?;\n\n    eprintln!(\n        \"done: records={} level0_runs={} merge_passes={} merge_batches={} output_bytes={}\",\n        stats.records, stats.level0_runs, stats.merge_passes, stats.merge_batches, stats.output_bytes\n    );\n    eprintln!(\"job state kept at {root}/jobs/{id}\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn cmd_resume(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    let opts = parse_opts(args)?;\n    let root = opts\n        .get(\"root\")\n        .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"--root is required\".into()))?;\n    let id = opts\n        .get(\"job\")\n        .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"--job is required\".into()))?;\n    let output = opts.get(\"output\");\n\n    let repo = Repository::new(root);\n    let mut job = repo.open_job(id)?;\n    let stats = run_job(&repo, &mut job)?;\n    eprintln!(\n        \"resumed to done: records={} level0_runs={} merge_passes={} resumed=true output_bytes={}\",\n        stats.records, stats.level0_runs, stats.merge_passes, stats.output_bytes\n    );\n    if let Some(path) = output {\n        let bytes = extsort::io::read_all(repo.vfs().as_ref(), &format!(\"jobs/{id}/output.txt\"))?;\n        fs::write(path, bytes).map_err(|e| Error::io(e, path.to_string()))?;\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn temp_root() -> String {\n    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\n        \"extsort-cli-{}\",\n        std::time::SystemTime::now()\n            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n            .map(|d| d.as_nanos())\n            .unwrap_or(0)\n    ));\n    dir.display().to_string()\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":69,"oldLines":15,"newStart":69,"newLines":22,"lines":[" }"," "," fn Memory accounting.\n//!\n//! The budget explicitly **includes buffers** — it is not just the size of the\n//! records held in memory. [`Budget::plan`] reserves fixed costs first (input\n//! read buffer, output write buffer, per-run merge buffers) and hands the\n//! engine the remaining bytes for resident records. The engine flushes a run\n//! whenever resident records approach that allowance.\n\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::scanner::READ_BUFFER;\n\n/// Hard floor below which no sort can run: read buffer + output buffer + one\n/// merge lane (head up to one chunk + readahead) + giant-spill work buffers +\n/// a minimal record allowance.\npub const MIN_BUDGET: u64 = 128 * 1024;\n\n/// Output stream write buffer.\npub const OUTPUT_BUFFER: usize = 16 * 1024;\n/// Per-lane readahead buffer while streaming a value.\npub const MERGE_LANE_BUFFER: usize = 8 * 1024;\n/// Worst-case resident head prefix per merge lane (one full first chunk).\npub const MERGE_LANE_HEAD: usize = 16 * 1024;\n/// Transient work buffers used while streaming one giant record to a run\n/// (writer chunk assembly + scanner chunk staging).\npub const SPILL_WORK: usize = 48 * 1024;\n/// Minimum bytes left for resident records after fixed reservations.\npub const MIN_RECORD_ALLOWANCE: usize = 4 * 1024;\n\n/// Resolved memory plan for one sort job.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct Budget {\n    /// Total bytes the job is allowed to use across all tracked buffers.\n    pub total: u64,\n    /// Resident-record allowance (what triggers a run flush).\n    pub record_allowance: usize,\n    pub read_buffer: usize,\n    pub output_buffer: usize,\n    pub lane_buffer: usize,\n    /// Merge fan-in supported under this budget (extra passes if reduced).\n    pub lane_count: usize,\n}\n\nimpl Budget {\n    /// Plan a budget with a target maximum number of simultaneous merge lanes.\n    /// Fixed buffers are reserved first; if the budget cannot fund\n    /// `max_lanes` lanes plus [`MIN_RECORD_ALLOWANCE`], lanes are reduced (the\n    /// merge then performs extra passes) rather than exceeding the budget.\n    pub fn plan(total: u64, max_lanes: usize) -> Result<Budget> {\n        if total < MIN_BUDGET {\n            return Err(Error::BudgetTooSmall {\n                budget: total,\n                min: MIN_BUDGET,\n            });\n        }\n        let fixed = (READ_BUFFER + OUTPUT_BUFFER) as u64;\n        let mut lanes = (max_lanes.max(1)) as u64;\n        loop {\n            let lane_bytes = lanes * MERGE_LANE_BUFFER as u64;\n            let left = total.saturating_sub(fixed + lane_bytes);\n            if left >= MIN_RECORD_ALLOWANCE as u64 || lanes == 1 {\n Memory accounting.\n//!\n//! The budget explicitly **includes buffers** — it is not just the size of the\n//! records held in memory. [`Budget::plan`] reserves fixed costs first (input\n//! read buffer, output write buffer, per-run merge buffers) and hands the\n//! engine the remaining bytes for resident records. The engine flushes a run\n//! whenever resident records approach that allowance.\n\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::scanner::READ_BUFFER;\n\n/// Hard floor below which no sort can run: read buffer + output buffer + one\n/// merge lane (head up to one chunk + readahead) + giant-spill work buffers +\n/// a minimal record allowance.\npub const MIN_BUDGET: u64 = 128 * 1024;\n\n/// Output stream write buffer.\npub const OUTPUT_BUFFER: usize = 16 * 1024;\n/// Per-lane readahead buffer while streaming a value.\npub const MERGE_LANE_BUFFER: usize = 8 * 1024;\n/// Worst-case resident head prefix per merge lane (one full first chunk).\npub const MERGE_LANE_HEAD: usize = 16 * 1024;\n/// Transient work buffers used while streaming one giant record to a run\n/// (writer chunk assembly + scanner chunk staging).\npub const SPILL_WORK: usize = 48 * 1024;\n/// Minimum bytes left for resident records after fixed reservations.\npub const MIN_RECORD_ALLOWANCE: usize = 4 * 1024;\n\n/// Resolved memory plan for one sort job.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct Budget {\n    /// Total bytes the job is allowed to use across all tracked buffers.\n    pub total: u64,\n    /// Resident-record allowance (what triggers a run flush).\n    pub record_allowance: usize,\n    pub read_buffer: usize,\n    pub output_buffer: usize,\n    pub lane_buffer: usize,\n    /// Merge fan-in supported under this budget (extra passes if reduced).\n    pub lane_count: usize,\n}\n\nimpl Budget {\n    /// Plan a budget with a target maximum number of simultaneous merge lanes.\n    /// Fixed buffers are reserved first; if the budget cannot fund\n    /// `max_lanes` lanes plus [`MIN_RECORD_ALLOWANCE`], lanes are reduced (the\n    /// merge then performs extra passes) rather than exceeding the budget.\n    pub fn plan(total: u64, max_lanes: usize) -> Result<Budget> {\n        if total < MIN_BUDGET {\n            return Err(Error::BudgetTooSmall {\n                budget: total,\n                min: MIN_BUDGET,\n            });\n        }\n        // Fixed costs present in every job: input read buffer, output write\n        // buffer, and the transient giant-spill work area.\n        let base_fixed = (READ_BUFFER + OUTPUT_BUFFER + SPILL_WORK) as u64;\n        let per_lane = (MERGE_LANE_BUFFER + MERGE_LANE_HEAD) as u64;\n        let mut lanes = (max_lanes.max(1)) as u64;\n        loop {\n            let lane_bytes = lanes * per_lane;\n            let left = total.saturating_sub(base_fixed + lane_bytes);\n            if left >= MIN_RECORD_ALLOWANCE as u64 || lanes == 1 {\n                break;\n            }\n            lanes -= 1;\n        }\n        let lane_bytes = lanes * per_lane;\n        let record_allowance = (total - base_fixed - lane_bytes) as usize;\n        Ok(Budget {\n            total,\n            record_allowance,\n            read_buffer: READ_BUFFER,\n            output_buffer: OUTPUT_BUFFER,\n            lane_buffer: MERGE_LANE_BUFFER,\n            lane_count: lanes as usize,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Number of simultaneous merge lanes supported under this plan.\n    pub fn lanes(&self) -> usize {\n        self.lane_count\n    }\n\n    /// Resident bytes permitted for in-memory records.\n    pub fn record_bytes(&self) -> usize {\n        self.record_allowance\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn rejects_tiny_budget() {\n        assert!(matches!(\n            Budget::plan(1024, 8),\n            Err(Error::BudgetTooSmall { .. })\n        ));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn reserves_buffers_and_scales_lanes() {\n        let small = Budget::plan(MIN_BUDGET, 8).unwrap();\n Memory accounting.\n//!\n//! The budget explicitly **includes buffers** — it is not just the size of the\n//! records held in memory. [`Budget::plan`] reserves fixed costs first (input\n//! read buffer, output write buffer, per-run merge buffers) and hands the\n//! engine the remaining bytes for resident records. The engine flushes a run\n//! whenever resident records approach that allowance.\n\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::scanner::READ_BUFFER;\n\n/// Hard floor below which no sort can run: read buffer + output buffer + one\n/// merge lane (head up to one chunk + readahead) + giant-spill work buffers +\n/// a minimal record allowance.\npub const MIN_BUDGET: u64 = 128 * 1024;\n\n/// Output stream write buffer.\npub const OUTPUT_BUFFER: usize = 16 * 1024;\n/// Per-lane readahead buffer while streaming a value.\npub const MERGE_LANE_BUFFER: usize = 8 * 1024;\n/// Worst-case resident head prefix per merge lane (one full first chunk).\npub const MERGE_LANE_HEAD: usize = 16 * 1024;\n/// Transient work buffers used while streaming one giant record to a run\n/// (writer chunk assembly + scanner chunk staging).\npub const SPILL_WORK: usize = 48 * 1024;\n/// Minimum bytes left for resident records after fixed reservations.\npub const MIN_RECORD_ALLOWANCE: usize = 4 * 1024;\n\n/// Resolved memory plan for one sort job.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct Budget {\n    /// Total bytes the job is allowed to use across all tracked buffers.\n    pub total: u64,\n    /// Resident-record allowance (what triggers a run flush).\n    pub record_allowance: usize,\n    pub read_buffer: usize,\n    pub output_buffer: usize,\n    pub lane_buffer: usize,\n    /// Merge fan-in supported under this budget (extra passes if reduced).\n    pub lane_count: usize,\n}\n\nimpl Budget {\n    /// Plan a budget with a target maximum number of simultaneous merge lanes.\n    /// Fixed buffers are reserved first; if the budget cannot fund\n    /// `max_lanes` lanes plus [`MIN_RECORD_ALLOWANCE`], lanes are reduced (the\n    /// merge then performs extra passes) rather than exceeding the budget.\n    pub fn plan(total: u64, max_lanes: usize) -> Result<Budget> {\n        if total < MIN_BUDGET {\n            return Err(Error::BudgetTooSmall {\n                budget: total,\n                min: MIN_BUDGET,\n            });\n        }\n        // Fixed costs present in every job: input read buffer, output write\n        // buffer, and the transient giant-spill work area.\n        let base_fixed = (READ_BUFFER + OUTPUT_BUFFER + SPILL_WORK) as u64;\n        let per_lane = (MERGE_LANE_BUFFER + MERGE_LANE_HEAD) as u64;\n        let mut lanes = (max_lanes.max(1)) as u64;\n        loop {\n            let lane_bytes = lanes * per_lane;\n            let left = total.saturating_sub(base_fixed + lane_bytes);\n            if left >= MIN_RECORD_ALLOWANCE as u64 || lanes == 1 {\n                break;\n            }\n            lanes -= 1;\n        }\n        let lane_bytes = lanes * per_lane;\n        let record_allowance = (total - base_fixed - lane_bytes) as usize;\n        Ok(Budget {\n            total,\n            record_allowance,\n            read_buffer: READ_BUFFER,\n            output_buffer: OUTPUT_BUFFER,\n            lane_buffer: MERGE_LANE_BUFFER,\n            lane_count: lanes as usize,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Number of simultaneous merge lanes supported under this plan.\n    pub fn lanes(&self) -> usize {\n        self.lane_count\n    }\n\n    /// Resident bytes permitted for in-memory records.\n    pub fn record_bytes(&self) -> usize {\n        self.record_allowance\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn rejects_tiny_budget() {\n        assert!(matches!(\n            Budget::plan(1024, 8),\n            Err(Error::BudgetTooSmall { .. })\n        ));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn reserves_buffers_and_scales_lanes() {\n        let small = Budget::plan(MIN_BUDGET, 8).unwrap();\n        assert!(small.record_allowance >= MIN_RECORD_ALLOWANCE);\n        assert!(small.lanes() >= 1);\n\n        let big = Budget::plan(64 * 1024 * 1024, 8).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(big.lanes(), 8);\n        let accounted = big.record_allowance\n            + big.read_buffer\n            + big.output_buffer\n            + SPILL_WORK\n            + big.lanes() * (big.lane_buffer + MERGE_LANE_HEAD);\n        assert_eq!(accounted as u64, big.total);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn never_exceeds_total() {\n        for &b in &[MIN_BUDGET, 200_000u64, 1_000_000, 16u64 << 20] {\n            let plan = Budget::plan(b, 16).unwrap();\n            let accounted = plan.record_allowance\n                + plan.read_buffer\n                + plan.output_buffer\n                + SPILL_WORK\n                + plan.lanes() * (plan.lane_buffer + MERGE_LANE_HEAD);\n            assert_eq!(accounted as u64, b, \"budget {b} oversubscribed\");\n        }\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":9,"oldLines":11,"newStart":9,"newLines":17,"lines":[" use crate::error::{Error, Result};"," use crate::scanner::READ_BUFFER;"," ","-/// Hard floor below which no Memory accounting.\n//!\n//! The budget explicitly **includes buffers** — it is not just the size of the\n//! records held in memory. [`Budget::plan`] reserves fixed costs first (input\n//! read buffer, output write buffer, per-run merge buffers) and hands the\n//! engine the remaining bytes for resident records. The engine flushes a run\n//! whenever resident records approach that allowance.\n\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::scanner::READ_BUFFER;\n\n/// Minimum merge fan-in that still reduces run count. A 1-way merge makes no\n/// progress (one run in, one run out), so the engine always reserves at least\n/// two lanes.\npub const MIN_MERGE_LANES: usize = 2;\n\n/// Hard floor: fixed buffers + two merge lanes + the minimum record allowance.\n/// Computed from the parts so it cannot drift from the accounting above.\npub const MIN_BUDGET: u64 = (READ_BUFFER + OUTPUT_BUFFER + SPILL_WORK) as u64\n    + (MIN_MERGE_LANES as u64) * (MERGE_LANE_BUFFER + MERGE_LANE_HEAD) as u64\n    + MIN_RECORD_ALLOWANCE as u64;\n\n/// Output stream write buffer.\npub const OUTPUT_BUFFER: usize = 16 * 1024;\n/// Per-lane readahead buffer while streaming a value.\npub const MERGE_LANE_BUFFER: usize = 8 * 1024;\n/// Worst-case resident head prefix per merge lane (one full first chunk).\npub const MERGE_LANE_HEAD: usize = 16 * 1024;\n/// Transient work buffers used while streaming one giant record to a run\n/// (writer chunk assembly + scanner chunk staging).\npub const SPILL_WORK: usize = 48 * 1024;\n/// Minimum bytes left for resident records after fixed reservations.\npub const MIN_RECORD_ALLOWANCE: usize = 4 * 1024;\n\n/// Resolved memory plan for one sort job.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\npub struct Budget {\n    /// Total bytes the job is allowed to use across all tracked buffers.\n    pub total: u64,\n    /// Resident-record allowance (what triggers a run flush).\n    pub record_allowance: usize,\n    pub read_buffer: usize,\n    pub output_buffer: usize,\n    pub lane_buffer: usize,\n    /// Merge fan-in supported under this budget (extra passes if reduced).\n    pub lane_count: usize,\n}\n\nimpl Budget {\n    /// Plan a budget with a target maximum number of simultaneous merge lanes.\n    /// Fixed buffers are reserved first; if the budget cannot fund\n    /// `max_lanes` lanes plus [`MIN_RECORD_ALLOWANCE`], lanes are reduced (the\n    /// merge then performs extra passes) rather than exceeding the budget.\n    pub fn plan(total: u64, max_lanes: usize) -> Result<Budget> {\n        if total < MIN_BUDGET {\n            return Err(Error::BudgetTooSmall {\n                budget: total,\n                min: MIN_BUDGET,\n            });\n        }\n        // Fixed costs present in every job: input read buffer, output write\n        // buffer, and the transient giant-spill work area.\n        let base_fixed = (READ_BUFFER + OUTPUT_BUFFER + SPILL_WORK) as u64;\n        let per_lane = (MERGE_LANE_BUFFER + MERGE_LANE_HEAD) as u64;\n        let mut lanes = (max_lanes.max(1)) as u64;\n        loop {\n            let lane_bytes = lanes * per_lane;\n            let left = total.saturating_sub(base_fixed + lane_bytes);\n            if left >= MIN_RECORD_ALLOWANCE as u64 || lanes == 1 {\n                break;\n            }\n            lanes -= 1;\n        }\n        let lane_bytes = lanes * per_lane;\n        let record_allowance = (total - base_fixed - lane_bytes) as usize;\n        Ok(Budget {\n            total,\n            record_allowance,\n            read_buffer: READ_BUFFER,\n            output_buffer: OUTPUT_BUFFER,\n            lane_buffer: MERGE_LANE_BUFFER,\n            lane_count: lanes as usize,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Number of simultaneous merge lanes supported under this plan.\n    pub fn lanes(&self) -> usize {\n        self.lane_count\n    }\n\n    /// Resident bytes permitted for in-memory records.\n    pub fn record_bytes(&self) -> usize {\n        self.record_allowance\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn rejects_tiny_budget() {\n        assert!(matches!(\n            Budget::plan(1024, 8),\n            Err(Error::BudgetTooSmall { .. })\n        ));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn reserves_buffers_and_scales_lanes() {\n        let small = Budget::plan(MIN_BUDGET, 8).unwrap();\n        assert!(small.record_allowance >= MIN_RECORD_ALLOWANCE);\n        assert!(small.lanes() >= 1);\n\n        let big = Budget::plan(64 * 1024 * 1024, 8).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(big.lanes(), 8);\n        let accounted = big.record_allowance\n            + big.read_buffer\n            + big.output_buffer\n            + SPILL_WORK\n            + big.lanes() * (big.lane_buffer + MERGE_LANE_HEAD);\n        assert_eq!(accounted as u64, big.total);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn never_exceeds_total() {\n        for &b in &[MIN_BUDGET, 200_000u64, {"parentUuid":"150ddf07-7caa-48d8-8b88-ff1c2284e5f1","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_0f11iyctmeb9b2h4276617il","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp2/a/src/testutil.rs","content":"//! Test-only helpers exposed publicly so integration tests under `tests/` can\n//! drive the engine with in-memory bytes and the injectable VFS without\n//! depending on the CLI binary.\n\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse crate::error::Result;\nuse crate::io::{FaultPlan, FaultVfs, RealVfs, Vfs};\nuse crate::key::KeySpec;\nuse crate::reference::reference_sort_bytes;\nuse crate::repository::{JobConfig, Repository};\nuse crate::sort::run_job;\n\n/// Description of one end-to-end sort to run through the repository.\npub struct Harness {\n    pub root: std::path::PathBuf,\n    pub repo: Repository,\n    pub id: String,\n}\n\nimpl Harness {\n    /// Create a fresh job rooted in a unique temp directory.\n    pub fn new(id: &str, spec: &str, budget: u64, lanes: usize, keep_temp: bool) -> Self {\n        let root = unique_root(id);\n        let repo = Repository::new(&root);\n        let cfg = JobConfig {\n            key_spec: spec.to_string(),\n            delim: b',',\n            budget,\n            max_lanes: lanes,\n            keep_temp,\n        };\n        repo.create_job(id, cfg).expect(\"create job\");\n        Harness {\n            root,\n            repo,\n            id: id.to_string(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Like [`Harness::new`] but wraps the VFS in a [`FaultVfs`] using `plan`.\n    pub fn with_faults(id: &str, spec: &str, budget: u64, lanes: usize, plan: FaultPlan) -> Self {\n        let root = unique_root(id);\n        let real = Arc::new(RealVfs::new(Path::new(&root)));\n        let vfs: Arc<dyn Vfs> = Arc::new(FaultVfs::new(real, plan));\n        let repo = Repository::with_vfs(&root, vfs);\n        let cfg = JobConfig {\n            key_spec: spec.to_string(),\n            delim: b',',\n            budget,\n            max_lanes: lanes,\n            keep_temp: true,\n        };\n        repo.create_job(id, cfg).expect(\"create job\");\n        Harness {\n            root,\n            repo,\n            id: id.to_string(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Reopen a previously created (possibly faulted) job through normal\n    /// recovery on a plain, non-faulting VFS.\n    pub fn reopen(id: &str, root: &std::path::Path) -> (Repository, crate::repository::Job) {\n        let repo = Repository::new(root);\n        let job = repo.open_job(id).expect(\"open/recover job\");\n        (repo, job)\n    }\n\n    pub fn vfs(&self) -> Arc<dyn Vfs> {\n        self.repo.vfs()\n    }\n\n    pub fn input_path(&self) -> String {\n        format!(\"jobs/{}/input.dat\", self.id)\n    }\n    pub fn output_path(&self) -> String {\n        format!(\"jobs/{}/output.txt\", self.id)\n    }\n\n    pub fn write_input(&self, data: &[u8]) {\n        let vfs = self.vfs();\n        crate::io::atomic_write_bytes(\n            vfs.as_ref(),\n            &format!(\"jobs/{}/input.dat.tmp\", self.id),\n            &self.input_path(),\n            data,\n        )\n        .expect(\"write input\");\n    }\n\n    /// Run to completion.\n    pub fn run(&mut self) -> Result<crate::sort::SortStats> {\n        let mut job = self\n            .repo\n            .open_job(&self.id)\n            .unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!(\"job {} missing\", self.id));\n        run_job(&self.repo, &mut job)\n    }\n\n    pub fn output(&self) -> Vec<u8> {\n        crate::io::read_all(self.vfs().as_ref(), &self.output_path()).expect(\"read output\")\n    }\n\n    pub fn cleanup(self) {\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.root);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Compute the in-memory reference result for `data` under `spec`.\npub fn reference(data: &[u8], spec: &str) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let ks = KeySpec::parse(spec, b',').unwrap();\n    reference_sort_bytes(data, &ks).expect(\"reference sort\")\n}\n\nfn unique_root(id: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {\n    let nanos = std::time::SystemTime::now()\n        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n        .map(|d| d.as_nanos())\n        .unwrap_or(0);\n    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\n        \"extsort-it-{id}-{}-{}\",\n        std::process::id(),\n        nanos\n    ));\n    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();\n    dir\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_07bba43a47709ef3eb9ce31c","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":1079,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":171832,"output_tokens":1304,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_0f11iyctmeb9b2h4276617il":{"content":"//! {"parentUuid":"9526b967-9943-4b4d-9e30-095c19bcd092","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_03u99t7bwadrg8u26b0zg39y","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp2/a/tests/acceptance.rs","content":"//! End-to-end acceptance tests.\n//!\n//! These drive the real repository + engine through the public API with\n//! deliberately tiny memory budgets, compare against the in-memory reference\n//! sort, and exercise empty input, an over-budget single line, segment\n//! corruption, and crash/fault recovery from completed segments.\n\nuse std::io::Write;\n\nuse extsort::io::{FaultKind, FaultPlan};\nuse extsort::testutil::{reference, Harness};\n\n// The accounting floor for two merge lanes + buffers. Use a comfortably larger\n// but still tiny budget so many runs are produced.\nconst TINY: u64 = 160 * 1024;\nconst LANES: usize = 2;\n\nfn dataset(rows: usize, seed: u64) -> Vec<u8> {\n    // Small deterministic LCG so no rand dependency is needed.\n    let mut s = seed.wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005).wrapping_add(1442695040888963407);\n    let mut next = |n: u64| {\n        s ^= s >> 12;\n        s = s.wrapping_mul(2862933555777941757);\n        s ^= s >> 13;\n        s % n\n    };\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\n    for i in 0..rows {\n        let g = next(24);\n        let nlen = 2 + next(9) as usize;\n        let mut name = Vec::with_capacity(nlen);\n        for _ in 0..nlen {\n            name.push(b'a' + next(7) as u8);\n        }\n        let _ = write!(\n            out,\n            \"{g:02},{},{i}\\n\",\n            std::str::from_utf8(&name).unwrap()\n        );\n    }\n    out\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn empty_input_produces_empty_output() {\n    let mut h = Harness::new(\"empty\", \"\", TINY, LANES, false);\n    h.write_input(b\"\");\n    let st = h.run().expect(\"run empty\");\n    assert_eq!(st.records, 0);\n    assert_eq!(h.output(), b\"\");\n    h.cleanup();\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn single_line_no_newline_normalized() {\n    let mut h = Harness::new(\"one\", \"1\", TINY, LANES, false);\n    h.write_input(b\"alpha,beta\");\n    h.run().unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(h.output(), b\"alpha,beta\\n\");\n    h.cleanup();\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn multi_pass_merge_matches_reference_asc() {\n    let data = dataset(20_000, 11);\n    let spec = \"1:asc,2:asc\";\n    let mut h = Harness::new(\"mp-asc\", spec, TINY, LANES, true);\n    h.write_input(&data);\n    let st = h.run().expect(\"run\");\n    // 20k rows in a tiny budget must force several level-0 runs and >0 passes.\n    assert!(st.level0_runs >= 5, \"expected many runs, got {}\", st.level0_runs);\n    assert!(st.merge_passes >= 2, \"expected multi-pass, got {}\", st.merge_passes);\n    assert_eq!(h.output(), reference(&data, spec));\n    h.cleanup();\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn composite_asc_desc_with_stability_matches_reference() {\n    // Deliberately include repeated (col1,col2) pairs so the seq tie-break is\n    // observable via col3.\n    let data = b\"1,aa,0\\n1,bb,1\\n2,zz,2\\n1,aa,3\\n1,aa,4\\n2,zz,5\\n1,bb,6\\n\"\n        .repeat(300)\n        .concat();\n    let spec = \"1:asc,2:desc\";\n    let mut h = Harness::new(\"mp-mix\", spec, TINY, LANES, true);\n    h.write_input(&data);\n    let st = h.run().unwrap();\n    assert!(st.level0_runs > 1);\n    assert_eq!(h.output(), reference(&data, spec));\n    h.cleanup();\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn whole_line_default_key_matches_reference() {\n    let data = dataset(5_000, 23);\n    let mut h = Harness::new(\"mp-line\", \"\", TINY, LANES, true);\n    h.write_input(&data);\n    h.run().unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(h.output(), reference(&data, \"\"));\n    h.cleanup();\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn giant_single_line_larger_than_budget_preserves_bytes() {\n    // 300 KB value in column 2; key is column 1, so it streams past the budget.\n    let mut data = b\"k1,\".to_vec();\n    data.extend(std::iter::repeat(b'x').take(300_000));\n    data.extend_from_slice(b\"\\nzz,second\\n\");\n\n    let spec = \"1:asc\";\n    let mut h = Harness::new(\"giant\", spec, TINY, LANES, true);\n    h.write_input(&data);\n    let st = h.run().expect(\"run giant\");\n    assert_eq!(st.records, 2);\n    let out = h.output();\n    let mut lines = out.splitn(3, |&b| b == b'\\n');\n    let first = expected.as_slice());\n    assert_eq!(second, b\"zz,second\");\n    h.cleanup();\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn many_records_then_one_giant_interleaved() {\n    let mut data = dataset(3_000, 47);\n    let mut assert_eq!(h.output(), reference(&data, spec));\n    h.cleanup();\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn whole_line_default_key_matches_reference() {\n    let data = dataset(5_000, 23);\n    let mut h = End-to-end acceptance tests.\n2\t//!\n3\t//! These drive the real repository + engine through the public API with\n4\t//! deliberately tiny memory budgets, compare against the in-memory reference\n5\t//! sort, and exercise empty input, an over-budget single line, segment\n6\t//! corruption, and crash/fault recovery from completed segments.\n7\t\n8\tuse std::io::Write;\n9\t\n10\tuse extsort::io::{FaultKind, FaultPlan};\n11\tuse extsort::testutil::{reference, Harness};\n12\t\n13\t// The accounting floor for two merge lanes + buffers. Use a comfortably larger\n14\t// but still tiny budget so many runs are produced.\n15\tconst TINY: u64 = 160 * 1024;\n16\tconst LANES: usize = 2;\n17\t\n18\tfn dataset(rows: usize, seed: u64) -> Vec<u8> {\n19\t    // Small deterministic LCG so no rand dependency is needed.\n20\t    let mut s = seed.wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005).wrapping_add(1442695040888963407);\n21\t    let mut next = |n: u64| {\n22\t        s ^= s >> 12;\n23\t        s = s.wrapping_mul(2862933555777941757);\n24\t        s ^= s >> 13;\n25\t        s % n\n26\t    };\n27\t    let mut out = Vec::new();\n28\t    for i in 0..rows {\n29\t        let g = next(24);\n30\t        let nlen = 2 + next(9) as usize;\n31\t        let mut name = Vec::with_capacity(nlen);\n32\t        for _ in 0..nlen {\n33\t            name.push(b'a' + next(7) as u8);\n34\t        }\n35\t        let _ = write!(\n36\t            out,\n37\t            \"{g:02},{},{i}\\n\",\n38\t            std::str::from_utf8(&name).unwrap()\n39\t        );\n40\t    }\n41\t    out\n42\t}\n43\t\n44\t#[test]\n45\tfn empty_input_produces_empty_output() {\n46\t    let mut h = Harness::new(\"empty\", \"\", TINY, LANES, false);\n47\t    h.write_input(b\"\");\n48\t    let st = h.run().expect(\"run empty\");\n49\t    assert_eq!(st.records, 0);\n50\t    assert_eq!(h.output(), b\"\");\n51\t    h.cleanup();\n52\t}\n53\t\n54\t#[test]\n55\tfn single_line_no_newline_normalized() {\n56\t    let mut h = Harness::new(\"one\", \"1\", TINY, LANES, false);\n57\t    h.write_input(b\"alpha,beta\");\n58\t    h.run().unwrap();\n59\t    assert_eq!(h.output(), b\"alpha,beta\\n\");\n60\t    h.cleanup();\n61\t}\n62\t\n63\t#[test]\n64\tfn multi_pass_merge_matches_reference_asc() {\n65\t    let data = dataset(20_000, 11);\n66\t    let spec = \"1:asc,2:asc\";\n67\t    let mut h = Harness::new(\"mp-asc\", spec, TINY, LANES, true);\n68\t    h.write_input(&data);\n69\t    let st = h.run().expect(\"run\");\n70\t    // 20k rows in a tiny budget must force several level-0 runs and >0 passes.\n71\t    assert!(st.level0_runs >= 5, \"expected many runs, got {}\", st.level0_runs);\n72\t    assert!(st.merge_passes >= 2, \"expected multi-pass, got {}\", st.merge_passes);\n73\t    assert_eq!(h.output(), reference(&data, spec));\n74\t    h.cleanup();\n75\t}\n76\t\n77\t#[test]\n78\tfn composite_asc_desc_with_stability_matches_reference() {\n79\t    // Deliberately include repeated (col1,col2) pairs so the seq tie-break is\n80\t    // observable via col3.\n81\t    let data = b\"1,aa,0\\n1,bb,1\\n2,zz,2\\n1,aa,3\\n1,aa,4\\n2,zz,5\\n1,bb,6\\n\"\n82\t        .repeat(300)\n83\t        .into_iter()\n84\t        .flatten()\n85\t        .collect();\n86\t    let spec = \"1:asc,2:desc\";\n87\t    let mut h = Harness::new(\"mp-mix\", spec, TINY, LANES, true);\n88\t    h.write_input(&data);\n89\t    let st = h.run().unwrap();\n90\t    assert!(st.level0_runs > 1);\n91\t    assert_eq!(h.output(), reference(&data, spec));\n92\t    h.cleanup();\n93\t}\n94\t\n95\t#[test]\n96\tfn whole_line_default_key_matches_reference() {\n97\t    let data = dataset(5_000, 23);\n98\t    let mut h = Harness::new(\"mp-line\", \"\", TINY, LANES, true);\n99\t    h.write_input(&data);\n100\t    h.run().unwrap();\n101\t    assert_eq!(h.output(), reference(&data, \"\"));\n102\t    h.cleanup();\n103\t}\n104\t\n105\t#[test]\n106\tfn giant_single_line_larger_than_budget_preserves_bytes() {\n107\t    // 300 KB value in column 2; key is column 1, so it streams past the budget.\n108\t    let mut data = b\"k1,\".to_vec();\n109\t    data.extend(std::iter::repeat(b'x').take(300_000));\n110\t    data.extend_from_slice(b\"\\nzz,second\\n\");\n111\t\n112\t    let spec = \"1:asc\";\n113\t    let mut h = Harness::new(\"giant\", spec, TINY, LANES, true);\n114\t    h.write_input(&data);\n115\t    let st = h.run().expect(\"run giant\");\n116\t    assert_eq!(st.records, 2);\n117\t    let out = h.output();\n118\t    let mut lines = out.splitn(3, |&b| b == b'\\n');\n119\t    let first = lines.next().unwrap();\n120\t    let second = lines.next().unwrap();\n121\t    let mut expected = b\"k1,\".to_vec();\n122\t    expected.extend(std::iter::repeat(b'x').take(300_000));\n123\t    assert_eq!(first, expected.as_slice());\n124\t    assert_eq!(second, b\"zz,second\");\n125\t    h.cleanup();\n126\t}\n127\t\n128\t#[test]\n129\tfn many_records_then_one_giant_interleaved() {\n130\t data.extend_from_slice(&giant);\n135\t    data.extend_from_slice(b\"aa,last\\n\");\n136\t\n137\t    let spec = \"1:asc\";\n138\t    let mut h = Harness::new(\"giantmix\", spec, TINY, LANES, true);\n139\t    h.write_input(&data);\n140\t    h.run().unwrap();\n141\t    assert_eq!(h.output(), reference(&data, spec));\n142\t    h.cleanup();\n143\t}\n144\t\n145\t#[test]\n146\tfn whole_line_key_giant_is_rejected_not_silently_oversized() {\n147\t    // With the default whole-line key, a line larger than the head window must\n148\t    // fail loudly rather than exceed the memory IEEE CRC-32 (poly 0xEDB88320, the zlib/checksum32 variant), std-only.\n//!\n//! Used to detect torn writes and corrupted temporary segments. This is an\n//! integrity check, not a cryptographic hash.\n\n/// Precomputed 256-entry lookup table.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy)]\npub struct Table {\n    entries: [u32; 256],\n}\n\nimpl Table {\n    pub const fn new() -> Self {\n        let mut entries = [0u32; 256];\n        let mut i = 0usize;\n        while i < 256 {\n            let mut c = i as u32;\n            let mut k = 0;\n            while k < 8 {\n                c = if c & 1 != 0 {\n                    0xEDB88320 ^ (c >> 1)\n                } else {\n                    c >> 1\n                };\n                k += 1;\n            }\n            entries[i] = c;\n            i += 1;\n        }\n        Table { entries }\n    }\n\n    /// Update `crc` with `bytes`; start from [`Crc::INIT`].\n    pub const fn update(&self, mut crc: u32, bytes: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n        let mut i = 0;\n        while i < bytes.len() {\n            let idx = ((crc ^ bytes[i] as u32) & 0xFF) as usize;\n            crc = self.entries[idx] ^ (crc >> 8);\n            i += 1;\n        }\n        crc\n    }\n}\n\n/// Streaming CRC-32 accumulator.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct Crc {\n    table: Table,\n    value: u32,\n}\n\nimpl Default for Crc {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Crc {\n    pub const INIT: u32 = 0xFFFF_FFFF;\n\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Crc {\n            table: Table::new(),\n            value: Self::INIT,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn write(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) {\n        self.value = self.table.update(self.value, bytes);\n    }\n\n    pub fn finish(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.value ^ 0xFFFF_FFFF\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// Known-answer vectors (CRC-32/ISO-HDLC as produced by `crc32` util).\n    #[test]\n    fn known_vectors() {\n        fn crc(b: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n            let mut c = Crc::new();\n            c.write(b);\n            c.finish()\n        }\n        assert_eq!(crc(b\"\"), 0);\n        assert_eq!(crc(b\"123456789\"), 0xCBF43926);\n        assert_eq!(crc(b\"a\"), 0xE8B7_BE43);\n        // Streaming == one-shot.\n        let mut c = Crc::new();\n        c.write(b\"1234\");\n        c.write(b\"56789\");\n        assert_eq!(c.finish(), 0xCBF43926);\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":4,"oldLines":7,"newStart":4,"newLines":7,"lines":[" //! integrity check, not a cryptographic hash."," "," /// Precomputed 256-entry lookup table.","-#[derive(Clone, Copy)]","+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]"," pub struct Table {","     entries: [u32; Command-line entry point.\n//!\n//! Commands:\n//! * `serve --root DIR [--addr 127.0.0.1:8080]`\n//!   Run the local HTTP validation server.\n//! * `sort --input FILE --output FILE [--root DIR] [--spec SPEC]\n//!          [--delim ,] [--budget BYTES] [--lanes N] [--keep-temp]\n//!          [--fault GRAMMAR]`\n//!   Run one job end to end (resumable). With `--fault`, the named faults are\n//!   injected; rerun with `--resume` to demonstrate recovery.\n//! * `resume --root DIR --job ID`\n//!   Reopen a crashed/interrupted job and continue.\n\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::process::ExitCode;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse extsort::io::{FaultPlan, FaultVfs, RealVfs};\nuse extsort::repository::{JobConfig, Repository};\nuse extsort::server::ServerConfig;\nuse extsort::{run_job, Error};\n\nfn main() -> ExitCode {\n    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();\n    match run(&args) {\n        Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"error: {e}\");\n            ExitCode::FAILURE\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn run(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    let cmd = args.get(1).map(|s| s.as_str()).unwrap_or(\"help\");\n    match cmd {\n        \"serve\" => cmd_serve(&args[2..]),\n        \"sort\" => cmd_sort(&args[2..]),\n        \"resume\" => cmd_resume(&args[2..]),\n        \"help\" | \"--help\" | \"-h\" => {\n            print_help();\n            Ok(())\n        }\n        other => {\n            eprintln!(\"unknown command: {other}\\n\");\n            print_help();\n            Err(Error::BadRequest(\"unknown command\".into()))\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn print_help() {\n    println!(\n        \"extsort — bounded-memory file-backed stable external sort\\n\\\n\\n\\\nUSAGE:\\n\\\n  extsort serve  --root DIR [--addr 127.0.0.1:8080]\\n\\\n  extsort sort   --input FILE --output FILE [--root DIR]\\n\\\n                 [--spec \\\"field:asc,field:desc\\\"] [--delim ,]\\n\\\n                 [--budget BYTES] [--lanes N] [--keep-temp]\\n\\\n                 [--fault GRAMMAR] [--job ID]\\n\\\n  extsort resume --root DIR --job ID\\n\"\n    );\n}\n\nstruct Opts {\n    map: Vec<(String, String)>,\n}\n\nfn parse_opts(args: &[String]) -> Result<Opts, Error> {\n    // Options that are boolean switches and consume no following value.\n    const FLAGS: &[&str] = &[\"keep-temp\"];\n    let mut map = Vec::new();\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i < args.len() {\n        let a = &args[i];\n        if let Some(key) = a.strip_prefix(\"--\") {\n            if let Some((k, v)) = key.split_once('=') {\n                map.push((k.to_string(), v.to_string()));\n            } else if FLAGS.contains(&key) {\n                map.push((key.to_string(), \"1\".to_string()));\n            } else if i + 1 < args.len() && !args[i + 1].starts_with(\"--\") {\n                map.push((key.to_string(), args[i + 1].clone()));\n                i += 1;\n            } else if i + 1 < args.len() {\n                // Value that happens to start with \"--\" (rare) still consumed.\n                map.push((key.to_string(), args[i + 1].clone()));\n                i += 1;\n            } else {\n                return Err(Error::BadRequest(format!(\"option {a} needs a value\")));\n            }\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    Ok(Opts { map })\n}\n\nimpl Opts {\n    fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&str> {\n        self.map.iter().find(|(k, _)| k == key).map(|(_, v)| v.as_str())\n    }\n}\n\nfn cmd_serve(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    let opts = parse_opts(args)?;\n    let root = opts\n        .get(\"root\")\n        .unwrap_or(\"./extsort-data\")\n        .to_string();\n    let addr = opts\n        .get(\"addr\")\n        .unwrap_or(\"127.0.0.1:8080\")\n        .to_string();\n    extsort::server::serve(ServerConfig { root, addr })\n}\n\nfn cmd_sort(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    let opts = parse_opts(args)?;\n    let input = opts\n        .get(\"input\")\n        .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"--input is required\".into()))?;\n    let output = opts\n        .get(\"output\")\n        .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"--output is required\".into()))?;\n    let root = opts\n        .get(\"root\")\n        .map(|s| s.to_string())\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| temp_root());\n\n    let cfg = JobConfig {\n        key_spec: opts.get(\"spec\").unwrap_or(\"\").to_string(),\n        delim: opts\n            .get(\"delim\")\n            .map(|d| d.as_bytes().first().copied().unwrap_or(b','))\n            .unwrap_or(b','),\n        budget: opts\n            .get(\"budget\")\n            .map(|b| b.parse::<u64>())\n            .transpose()\n            .map_err(|_| Error::BadRequest(\"bad --budget\".into()))?\n            .unwrap_or(4 * 1024 * 1024),\n        max_lanes: opts\n            .get(\"lanes\")\n            .map(|b| b.parse::<usize>())\n            .transpose()\n            .map_err(|_| Error::BadRequest(\"bad --lanes\".into()))?\n            .unwrap_or(4),\n        keep_temp: opts.get(\"keep-temp\").is_some(),\n    };\n\n    let data = fs::read(input).map_err(|e| Error::io(e, input.to_string()))?;\n    let id = opts\n        .get(\"job\")\n        .map(|s| s.to_string())\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| \"local\".to_string());\n\n    let repo = if let Some(grammar) = opts.get(\"fault\") {\n        let plan = FaultPlan::parse(grammar)\n            .map_err(|m| Error::BadRequest(format!(\"bad --fault: {m}\")))?;\n        let real = Arc::new(RealVfs::new(PathBuf::from(&root)));\n        Repository::with_vfs(&root, Arc::new(FaultVfs::new(real, plan)))\n    } else {\n        Repository::new(&root)\n    };\n    let vfs = repo.vfs();\n\n    // Remove a stale same-id job so `sort` starts clean (resume uses `resume`).\n    vfs.remove_dir_all(&format!(\"jobs/{id}\"))?;\n    let mut job = repo.create_job(&id, cfg.clone())?;\n    extsort::io::atomic_write_bytes(\n        vfs.as_ref(),\n        &format!(\"jobs/{id}/input.dat.tmp\"),\n        &format!(\"jobs/{id}/input.dat\"),\n        &data,\n    )?;\n\n    let stats = run_job(&repo, &mut job)?;\n    // Copy output to the requested destination.\n    let produced = extsort::io::read_all(vfs.as_ref(), &format!(\"jobs/{id}/output.txt\"))?;\n    fs::write(output, produced).map_err(|e| Error::io(e, output.to_string()))?;\n\n    eprintln!(\n        \"done: records={} level0_runs={} merge_passes={} merge_batches={} output_bytes={}\",\n        stats.records, stats.level0_runs, stats.merge_passes, stats.merge_batches, stats.output_bytes\n    );\n    eprintln!(\"job state kept at {root}/jobs/{id}\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn cmd_resume(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    let opts = parse_opts(args)?;\n    let root = opts\n        .get(\"root\")\n        .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"--root is required\".into()))?;\n    let id = opts\n        .get(\"job\")\n        .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"--job is required\".into()))?;\n    let output = opts.get(\"output\");\n\n    let repo = Repository::new(root);\n    let mut job = repo.open_job(id)?;\n    let stats = run_job(&repo, &mut job)?;\n    eprintln!(\n        \"resumed to done: records={} level0_runs={} merge_passes={} resumed=true output_bytes={}\",\n        stats.records, stats.level0_runs, stats.merge_passes, stats.output_bytes\n    );\n    if let Some(path) = output {\n        let bytes = extsort::io::read_all(repo.vfs().as_ref(), &format!(\"jobs/{id}/output.txt\"))?;\n        fs::write(path, bytes).map_err(|e| Error::io(e, path.to_string()))?;\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn temp_root() -> String {\n    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\n        \"extsort-cli-{}\",\n        std::time::SystemTime::now()\n            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n            .map(|d| d.as_nanos())\n            .unwrap_or(0)\n    ));\n This is an\n//! integrity check, not a cryptographic hash.\n\n/// Precomputed 256-entry lookup table.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]\npub struct Table {\n    entries: [u32; 256],\n}\n\nimpl Table {\n    pub const fn new() -> Self {\n        let mut entries = [0u32; 256];\n        let mut i = 0usize;\n        while i < 256 {\n            let mut c = i as u32;\n            let mut k = 0;\n            while k < 8 {\n                c = if c & 1 != 0 {\n                    0xEDB88320 ^ (c >> 1)\n                } else {\n                    c >> 1\n                };\n                k += 1;\n            }\n            entries[i] = c;\n            i += 1;\n        }\n        Table { entries }\n    }\n\n    /// Update `crc` with `bytes`; start from [`Crc::INIT`].\n    pub const fn update(&self, mut crc: u32, bytes: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n        let mut i = 0;\n        while i < bytes.len() {\n            let idx = ((crc ^ bytes[i] as u32) & 0xFF) as usize;\n            crc = self.entries[idx] ^ (crc >> 8);\n            i += 1;\n        }\n        crc\n    }\n}\n\n/// Streaming CRC-32 accumulator.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct Crc {\n    table: Table,\n    value: u32,\n}\n\nimpl Default for Crc {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Crc {\n    pub const INIT: u32 = 0xFFFF_FFFF;\n\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Crc {\n            table: Table::new(),\n            value: Self::INIT,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn write(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) {\n        self.value = self.table.update(self.value, bytes);\n    }\n\n    pub fn finish(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.value ^ 0xFFFF_FFFF\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    /// Known-answer vectors (CRC-32/ISO-HDLC as produced by `crc32` util).\n    #[test]\n    fn known_vectors() {\n        fn crc(b: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n            let mut c = Crc::new();\n            c.write(b);\n            c.finish()\n        }\n        assert_eq!(crc(b\"\"), 0);\n        assert_eq!(crc(b\"123456789\"), 0xCBF43926);\n        assert_eq!(crc(b\"a\"), 0xE8B7_BE43);\n        // Streaming == one-shot.\n        let mut c = Crc::new();\n        c.write(b\"1234\");\n        c.write(b\"56789\");\n        assert_eq!(c.finish(), 0xCBF43926);\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":4,"oldLines":11,"newStart":4,"newLines":17,"lines":[" //! integrity check, not a cryptographic hash."," "," /// Precomputed 256-entry lookup table.","-#[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]","+#[derive(Clone, Copy)]"," pub struct Table {","     entries: [u32; {"parentUuid":"4c210d29-3184-4779-8ade-8d52b4a8e3b2","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_icuzm7o7tavtyz671fvtjxk2","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp2/a/README.md","content":"# extsort — 有界内存、文件支持的稳定外排序（纯后端）\n\n一个用 Rust 标准库实现（**零第三方依赖**）的外部排序服务：\n\n- **有界内存**：内存预算显式包含读缓冲、写缓冲、归并车道缓冲与溢出工作区；\n  超过额度的记录在分段阶段就落盘，绝不会把整行读进内存。\n- **稳定**：按复合键比较，重复键严格按**原始输入序号**（sequence number）排序。\n- **复合键升降序**：如 `1:asc,2:desc`，字段 0 表示整行（兼容 `sort(1)`）。\n- **分段落盘 + 多路归并**：map 阶段产生有序 level-0 段，merge 阶段按预算车道数\n  做 k 路归并，可强制产生**多轮**归并。\n- **崩溃恢复**：每完成一个段 / 一个归并批，就把清单（manifest）原子写并\n  fsync；失败后从已提交的分段继续，未提交的 `*.tmp` 被丢弃。\n- **可注入 I/O 层**：所有磁盘操作走 `Vfs` trait，测试 / HTTP 头可注入\n  创建、写、sync、改名、读故障。\n- **段文件完整性**：魔数 + 每块 CRC-32 + 尾部记录计数，能检测位翻转与截断。\n- **本地 HTTP 验证入口**：纯 `std::net` 实现，无前端。\n\n---\n\n## 1. 构建\n\n```bash\ncargo build --release\n# 二进制：target/release/extsort\n```\n\n无需联网、无外部 crate。要求 Rust ≥ 1.75（在 1.98 上开发验证）。\n\n## 2. 快速开始（CLI）\n\n```bash\n# 基本：整行升序\n./target/release/extsort sort --input data.txt --output out.txt\n\n# 复合键：第 1 列升序、第 2 列降序；用极小内存强制多轮归并\n./target/release/extsort sort \\\n  --input data.csv --output out.csv \\\n  --spec \"1:asc,2:desc\" --delim , \\\n  --budget 163840 --lanes 2 --keep-temp\n\n# 失败后续跑（同一 --root/--job）\n./target/release/extsort resume --root ./repo --job local --output out.csv\n```\n\n输出统计形如：\n\n```\ndone: records=20000 level0_runs=17 merge_passes=5 merge_batches=20 output_bytes=358868\n```\n\n- `level0_runs`：map 阶段产生的分段数；\n- `merge_passes`：归并层数（多轮）；\n- `merge_batches`：归并批次数。\n\n### 键规格语法\n\n```\nspec       := [ field-spec (\",\" field-spec)* ]\nfield-spec := 字段序号 [ \":\" (asc|desc) ]     # 默认 asc\n```\n\n- 字段 `0` = 整行；`1` = 第一列（按单字节分隔符切分，默认 `,`）。\n- 不存在的列按空字节处理。\n- 字节序字典序比较（对合法 UTF-8 即码点序）；`desc` 只反转该字段方向。\n- 各字段全等时按输入序号升序——这是稳定性的来源。\n\n### 输出约定\n\n每条记录输出后补一个 `\\n`（含最后一条）；输入中的 CRLF 会规范化为 LF，\n因此“无尾换行的最后一行”和“空输入”都有确定、可对照的结果。\n\n---\n\n## 3. HTTP 验证入口\n\n```bash\n./target/release/extsort serve --root ./httproot --addr 127.0.0.1:8080\n```\n\n| 方法与路径 | 作用 |\n|---|---|\n| `GET  /healthz` | 存活检查 |\n| `POST /jobs?spec=…&budget=…&lanes=…` | 请求体即原始输入；创建作业并运行 |\n| `GET  /jobs` | 列出作业 id |\n| `GET  /jobs/{id}` | 状态 JSON（`status.json`） |\n| `GET  /jobs/{id}/output` | 排序结果字节 |\n| `DELETE /jobs/{id}` | 删除作业目录 |\n\n查询参数：`spec`、`delim`（单字节，默认 `,`）、`budget`（字节）、\n`lanes`（归并扇入，≥2，默认 4）、`keep_temp=1`。\n\n故障注入：在 `POST /jobs` 上加请求头 `X-Fault-Inject`（语法见\n[`examples/http-requests.sh`](examples/http-requests.sh) 与第 7 节）。\n\n---\n\n## 4. 磁盘格式与目录布局\n\n作业目录 `<root>/jobs/<job-id>/`：\n\n```\ninput.dat                 原始输入（上传后原子落盘）\noutput.txt                排序结果（state=done 后存在）\nmanifest.txt              持久化作业状态（提交点）\nstatus.json               面向 HTTP 的状态快照\nlevel0/run-00000.run      map 阶段有序分段\nlevel0/run-00001.run\nlevel1/m-1-00000.run      各轮归并输出\nlevel2/...\n*.run.tmp                 未提交的临时文件，恢复时一律删除\n```\n\n### 段（run）文件格式\n\n```\nmagic   : 8 字节 = b\"EXTSORT\\x02\"\nframes  : 0..N 个记录帧\ntrailer : 帧类型字节 FRAME_TRAILER(0x20) + u64 LE 记录数\n```\n\n每个帧以 1 字节类型开头，使顺序读取能区分记录与尾部：\n\n```\nFRAME_CHUNK = 0x10      FRAME_TRAILER = 0x20\n```\n\nchunk 帧：\n\n```\nftype   u8      = FRAME_CHUNK\nflags   u8      bit0=FIRST（记录首块） bit1=CONT（后面还有块）\nlength  u32 LE  负载长度（≤ CHUNK_MAX = 16 KiB）\ncrc32   u32 LE  负载的 CRC-32/IEEE\npayload length 字节\n```\n\nFIRST 块负载：\n\n```\nu64 LE  seq        原始输入序号（稳定 tie-break）\nu32 LE  key_count  键分量个数\n每个键: u32 LE len + 键字节\n字节流  value 前缀（记录本身，不含行结束符）\n```\n\n后续块只装 value 续接字节。这样**任意长度**的一行都能以有界内存落盘：\n超长行的键放在 FIRST 块，value 逐块流式写出 / 读入。\n\n完整性：每块带 CRC，消费即校验；尾部重复记录数以检测 torn tail；\n魔数检测错误 / 截断文件。\n\n---\n\n## 5. 同步（durability）边界\n\n- 段写入流程：写 `*.run.tmp` → `flush` + `fsync` → 关闭 → **原子 rename**\n  为 `*.run` → 对父目录再 `fsync`（见 `RealVfs::rename`）。\n  因此 rename 是一次崩溃一致的提交点。\n- 但“文件已 rename”不等于“作业已采用它”：**manifest 才是逻辑提交点**。\n  每次写完一个 map 段或一个归并批，都把 `manifest.txt.tmp` 写好 fsync 后\n  原子 rename 成 `manifest.txt`。崩溃后：\n  - manifest 记录的段 → 校验后复用；\n  - 磁盘上有但 manifest 未登记的段 / `*.tmp` → 删除重做；\n  - map 阶段：重开输入，跳过 `map_consumed` 条已持久化记录；\n  - merge 阶段：`runs` 是当前层尚未归并的段，`merge_done` 是本轮已提交的\n    上层输出，崩溃最多重做**当前未提交的那一个批**。\n\n### manifest 文本格式\n\n```\nEXTSORT-MANIFEST/1\njob <id>\nstate <map|merge|done|failed>\nlevel <n>\ntotal_records <n>\nmap_consumed <n>\nspec <键规格>\ndelim <byte>\nbudget <bytes>\nmax_lanes <n>\nkeep_temp <0|1>\nrun <name> <count>          # 当前层就绪 / 待归并段\nmerge_done <name> <count>   # 本轮已产出的上层段\nerror <可选失败原因>\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. 内存预算如何计算（含缓冲区）\n\n`Budget::plan(total, max_lanes)` 先扣固定成本，再把剩余额度给驻留记录：\n\n```\n固定 = 读缓冲 16 KiB + 输出缓冲 16 KiB + 溢出工作区 48 KiB\n每车道 = 续读缓冲 8 KiB + 车道头块 16 KiB\n驻留额度 = total - 固定 - 车道数 * 每车道\n```\n\n车道数在预算紧张时下调（但**绝不低于 2**：1 路归并不会减少段数，会死循环），\n下限 `MIN_BUDGET = 固定 + 2*每车道 + 4 KiB 驻留额度`。驻留记录字节达到额度\n即落盘一个段。要“用小内存强制多轮归并”，只需把 `--budget` 调到接近下限、\n`--lanes 2`，并让数据量远大于驻留额度（见验收测试与示例）。\n\n> 说明：单个记录的**键**必须能放进 FIRST 块头窗口（默认约 16 KiB）。\n> value 可任意长（流式）。若键本身比头窗口还大，作业以 `key_too_large`\n> 明确失败，而不是悄悄超内存。\n\n---\n\n## 7. 可注入 I/O 与故障语法\n\n所有磁盘操作经过 `Vfs` trait；生产用 `RealVfs`，测试 / HTTP 用\n`FaultVfs` 装饰。故障规则语法（逗号分隔多条）：\n\n```\nrule := kind[ \":\" needle ][ \":\" count ]\nkind := write_fail | sync_fail | rename_fail | create_fail | read_fail\n```\n\n- `needle`：对受影响路径做子串匹配（缺省匹配任意路径）；\n- `count`：连续命中的失败次数（缺省 1，0 表示禁用）。\n\n示例：\n\n- `--fault \"write_fail:run-00001\"`：写第二个 map 段时失败（第 0 段保留）；\n- `--fault \"create_fail:m-1-\"`：创建首个 level-1 归并输出时失败；\n- HTTP：`-H 'X-Fault-Inject: sync_fail:run-00003.run.tmp'`。\n\n---\n\n## 8. 测试\n\n```bash\ncargo test               # 27 单元测试 + 14 端到端验收测试\ncargo clippy             # 无警告\n```\n\n`tests/acceptance.rs`
